## 4.15 Non-negotiable rules

Each rule is stated, then its failure mode. Performance rules carry their measured cost.

1. **Run the mtime-diff fallback only post-turn.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* a pre-turn scan of ~199 files on every message, costing **+2–138 ms**, to find changes the pre-turn snapshot does not need.

2. **Run the pre-turn snapshot write and the pre-turn mtime record in parallel** (one gather of two executor calls).
   *Failure mode if violated:* sequential awaits add **60–70 ms** per turn. Measured pre-turn work went from 66–139 ms to **10 ms** when parallelized.

3. **Reset the per-turn direct-edit flag *before* the gather starts.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* placed between or after, the snapshot reads last turn's `true` and **skips the snapshot entirely**. This is a race, not merely slowness — Rewind silently loses a turn's backups.

4. **Carry the post-turn mtime map forward into the next pre-turn map, with a full rescan every 10 turns** to pick up new files.
   *Failure mode if violated:* a full enumeration plus stat on every turn — **60–80 ms** on a 200-file project.

5. **Start the first-turn mtime scan before awaiting `connect()`.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* connect takes **700–1000 ms** and the scan **70–90 ms**; overlapped, the scan is free. Moving it after adds the full 70–90 ms to every session start.

6. **Expose an entry-*count* IPC method that returns the list length without serializing.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* a 10-second watchdog poll serializes every entry, JSON-encodes it, ships it over IPC, and decodes it — **25–32 ms to return the integer 300**, versus **0–1 ms**.

7. **Filesystem-detected changes are snapshot extras only** — never added to the persistent tracked set, and never re-derived from snapshot records on resume.
   *Failure mode if violated:* the set snowballs past **1400 entries**; turns take **20–55 s**; on Windows with real-time antivirus, pre-turn waits of **130–380 s**.

8. **Debounce queue saves on a 1-second timer; never call the immediate save from a queue operation.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* every add/edit/remove/clear/dispatch rewrites the whole file; auto-dispatch chains cause I/O contention.

9. **Keep the `git ls-files` cache TTL at 180 s; never below 120 s.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* the subprocess re-runs on every follow-up message. New files are already caught by tool-event tracking, so the cache only needs to catch external changes.

10. **Cache the cross-session state list with a 2-second TTL.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* every WebSocket reconnect handshake triggers a fresh IPC round-trip; under a reconnect burst this congestion **tripped the 8-second heartbeat** and produced spurious "engine stopped" overlays.

11. **Cache application config with a 10-second TTL, invalidated on save.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* config is read on hot paths, including the pre-resume pass.

12. **Use a module-level thread pool for WebSocket setup work, never a per-request one.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a thread pool is constructed on every connect.

13. **Run system-session cleanup at startup only, never from a per-request path.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a listing endpoint becomes a filesystem sweep.

14. **Keep the IPC client's logger namespace in the profiling handler list.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* you silently lose all IPC round-trip timing — the primary latency diagnostic.

15. **Keep both traversal budgets at 2 s and the entry-trim thresholds at 500 → 200 (IDLE/STOPPED only).**
    *Failure mode if violated:* unbounded traversal makes sessions look hung; unbounded entries consume hundreds of MB.

16. **Do not "free memory" by clearing the mtime dictionaries or the git-file cache on IDLE.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* an earlier version did exactly this. It ran **between** a turn's pre-turn record and its post-turn diff, so **every file looked changed**. On a 3789-file project, every turn rewrote 3789 backups — **5–6 s of disk I/O per turn**. This was the root cause of the "looks fast, then dogshit slow" cycle. Holding the dicts costs a few hundred KB per session.

17. **Cancel the old post-turn listener before launching a new query, and set the supersede flag inside the same lock as the state flip.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* two consumers race the single shared SDK buffer; a straggling auto-resume `RESULT` clobbers the new turn's state back to IDLE.

18. **Read the interrupted flag in the sender thread; clear it on the loop after a `sleep(0)` yield.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* clearing it from the caller races the cancelled task's handler, which then believes it was a normal cancel and resets state to IDLE mid-turn.

19. **Arm the API retry before the post-turn drain, and keep `retry_at > 0` until the retry's send has flipped to WORKING.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* on a transient-error turn the listener blocks forever, the `finally` never runs, and the session is stuck ("ended with error then stopped forever"); and a queued follow-up dispatches ahead of the continuation, abandoning the failed work.

20. **Normalize `None` to `{}` in any IPC handler that can return a falsy value; and add a source-guard test for attribute names accessed only inside broad `except` blocks.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a null result is indistinguishable from a timeout. Separately, a misspelled registry attribute inside a swallow-everything block **went unnoticed for months** — every auto-resumed session ran with an empty working directory, name, and model, and the empty cwd then made those sessions pass a permissive project filter and appear in **every** project's sidebar.

21. **On Windows, never use the POSIX "signal 0" existence idiom.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* Python's Windows implementation **calls the terminate API for any signal other than the two console events**. The orphan sweep ran this "existence check" on every idle session every 60 s and thereby **killed the live CLI of every idle session**; users saw "CLI process exited — reconnecting" on every single message. Use a read-only query handle (`OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)`) plus `GetExitCodeProcess`, alive iff the code is `STILL_ACTIVE` (259).

22. **Refuse `killpg` when the target's process group equals your own.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a race, a bypassed spawn path, or PID reuse lands the target in your group and the kill **takes down the entire daemon**. This shipped to Linux users. Fall back to a per-PID kill: descendants leak, but a leak is recoverable and a dead daemon is not.

23. **Hard-stop guard before any signal: refuse a PID that is `None`, ≤ 1, or equal to your own.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* signalling 0 broadcasts to your whole process group (including you); −1 broadcasts to everything you can signal; 1 is init. The explicit `None` check must come first, because a numeric comparison against `None` raises.

24. **Capture the CLI PID before the SDK disconnect.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the disconnect destroys the handle and the process tree leaks.

25. **On Windows, `taskkill /T` only works while the parent is alive.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* grandchildren (worker processes) survive. If the parent already died, enumerate children by parent id and kill each with `/T` so the tree is reaped recursively. POSIX teardown is SIGTERM → 300 ms → SIGKILL on the group.

26. **The post-turn listener must never flag a stream-heal, and the post-turn drain must always hand off to the listener.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the first produces the "Reconnected — retrying last message automatically" loop on healthy idle sessions; the second leaves the SDK buffer with no consumer, so future auto-resume content is read as the *next* user query's response.

27. **Resolve session ids through the alias map at the top of message processing.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the listener holds the pre-remap id, every lookup silently finds nothing, the wake-up's `RESULT` never sets IDLE, and the queue is stranded indefinitely.

28. **Drain the bare-resume startup `init` within a 3-second window.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the post-turn peek reads it as an auto-resume, flips to WORKING, and waits forever for a `RESULT` that will never come.

29. **Guard the model switch with an in-progress flag, and do not emit state after a successful switch.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the CLI's side-effect `init` is mistaken for an auto-resume; and the post-switch IDLE emit dispatches a queued message the user did not expect, making the first turn look hung.

30. **Apply the tolerant-parser patch in both the parser module and the client module.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the client imported the function by name at import time, so patching one module is a **silent no-op** and one unknown message type kills the entire receive generator.

31. **Never allow `updatedInput` to be null in a permission allow-response; enforce it in two layers.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the CLI's sandbox validator crashes with "undefined is not an object". Remember that `dict.get("input", {})` returns `None` when the key exists with a null value.

32. **Guard import-time environment/path augmentation with a marker in the environment, not a module global.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* module globals reset on reload, so repeated augmentation grew the environment block past the Windows 32 767-character limit and raised on subsequent reloads.

33. **Wrap every stream message in its own try/except, and sleep 0.5 s when a response cycle yields zero messages.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* one bad message prevents the turn's `RESULT` from arriving and setting IDLE; and a zero-message iterator spins a core.

34. **Detect the thinking-block 400 structurally (prefix + `messages.<i>.content.<j>` path), not lexically.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a loose keyword match caught a session's own *diagnosis* of the bug and suppressed the model's real output.

35. **Never persist a transcript that does not re-parse, and never rewrite when nothing changed.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* one bad write destroys a session permanently; a no-op rewrite busts the prompt cache on every resume.

36. **Keep the starvation watchdog's armed timestamp across sweeps.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* resetting it each sweep means the timeout is never reached — that flicker *was* the original starvation, and it left four queued messages dead overnight.

37. **Replicate the source-level guard mechanism.** Mark performance-critical code with a `PERF-CRITICAL` marker comment and add an automated test that scans the current diff for changes within a proximity window of any such marker and fails, forcing an explicit acknowledgement.
    *Failure mode if violated:* roughly a third of the defects catalogued here are invisible to behavioural tests. Twenty-two such markers exist in the daemon alone. Every rule above exists because a plausible-looking simplification silently reversed it.

38. **Adopt log-lines-as-forensic-artifacts.** Uniform trigger lines with a `site=` field, one-line spawn-mode records at startup, and a diagnosis paragraph attached to fatal signals.
    *Failure mode if violated:* several of these bugs were declared "not reproducible" for months purely because the logs recorded the symptom without the source.

---

## 4.16 Implementation prompts

Build these in order. Do not start one until the previous is observable end to end.

````text
PROMPT 4.1 — The pipe and the proxy

Implement the daemon's IPC layer and its web-side proxy client. No sessions yet.

Daemon side:
- Bind 127.0.0.1 on a port from <APP>_DAEMON_PORT (default 5051) with
  SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE on Windows, SO_REUSEADDR + SO_REUSEPORT on POSIX.
- listen(1). A new connection replaces the previous one: close the old socket first.
- Set TCP_NODELAY and SO_KEEPALIVE (idle 15 s, interval 5 s, count 3; on macOS set
  TCP_KEEPALIVE=15) on every accepted socket.
- Accept loop uses a 1 s socket timeout so shutdown is responsive.
- Framing: accumulate RAW BYTES, find the last newline, decode only up to it, keep the
  remainder. Skip and log undecodable chunks and unparseable JSON lines.
- Dispatch each request on its own ephemeral thread. Serialize all socket writes with a
  single write lock.
- Wire shapes:
    request  {"req_id","method","params"}
    response {"req_id","result"}
    error    {"req_id","error"}
    push     {"event","data"}          (no req_id)
  req_id = first 8 hex chars of a UUID4.
- Implement exactly one method: ping -> {"ok": true, "pid": <int>}.
- Unknown method -> {"req_id":…, "error": "Unknown method: <name>"}.
- Any handler that may return a falsy value must normalize None to {}.

Web side (a proxy class whose method names mirror the future session manager):
- Threads: reader, emitter, heartbeat, reconnect.
- Reader is the ONLY socket reader. Correlate by req_id into {req_id: (Event, holder)};
  push events onto an internal queue.
- Emitter drains that queue and calls the WebSocket emit function.
- Heartbeat: ping every 20 s with an 8 s timeout; on failure force-disconnect.
- Force-disconnect calls shutdown(SHUT_RDWR) BEFORE close().
- Reconnect loop at 2 s cadence emitting a daemon_reconnect progress event with status in
  {connecting, connected, restarting, disconnected}; after 5 failed rounds, respawn the
  daemon detached (Windows: CREATE_NO_WINDOW|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP; POSIX:
  start_new_session=True) with output to <repo-root>/logs/daemon_debug.log.
- start() MUST connect without resync, then start reader/emitter/heartbeat, then resync
  on a background thread.
- The reader snapshots its socket object and only sets connected=False on exit if the
  current socket is still that same object.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A ping round-trip returns {"ok":true,"pid":N} where N is the daemon's PID.
2. Killing the daemon causes the client to report disconnected within ~30 s and to
   respawn it within ~10 s of the first failed reconnect round.
3. A unit test proves that a UTF-8 multi-byte character split across two recv() chunks is
   reassembled correctly and does not raise.
4. A unit test asserts HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT < HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL with bounds 5–60 and 2–30.
5. Connecting a second client closes the first socket and the second receives traffic.
6. A test proves resync is not attempted before the reader thread is running.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.2 — Singleton, spawn, and boot hardening

Make the daemon safely single-instance and self-diagnosing. Assume PROMPT 4.1 is done.

- Acquire a named mutex (Windows) or an flock lockfile (POSIX) before binding.
- If the lock is held but nothing is LISTENING on the port, declare the lock stale and
  proceed.
- Write a PID file at <agent-home>/gui_daemon.pid, or gui_daemon_<port>.pid for a
  non-default port. Remove it on graceful shutdown.
- BEFORE any third-party import: pre-seed the platform uname cache (on Windows,
  platform.system() issues a WMI query that can hang forever, and the HTTP import chain
  calls it), and arm a faulthandler hang dump with a 120 s fuse. Disarm the fuse once the
  socket binds.
- Log exactly one startup line recording spawn mode, executable name, session id, and
  process group id, e.g.
    spawn exe=<name> mode=detached(<detail>) sid=<n> pgid=<n>
- POSIX signal forensics: block SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP process-wide and run a thread on
  sigwaitinfo(). On receipt, log signal name, si_code, si_uid, sender pid/ppid/comm/
  cmdline, own pid/pgid/sid/ppid, plus a diagnosis line:
    sender == self          -> bug in our own kill path
    sender is a Python proc -> the web tier's restart endpoint
    otherwise               -> external (service manager / OOM / user)
  Then unblock and re-raise the signal to self so the graceful handler runs on main.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Starting a second daemon on the same port exits cleanly with a clear message.
2. Deleting a stale lock scenario (lock held, port closed) allows startup.
3. Sending SIGTERM from a helper process produces a log block naming that helper's PID
   and command line, plus the correct diagnosis line.
4. A test that binds the port, kills the process with SIGKILL, and immediately restarts
   proves the bind succeeds despite TIME_WAIT.
5. Forcing a 130 s artificial hang before bind produces a thread dump in the log.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.3 — The backend abstraction and the SDK patches

Define the agent-backend seam, then apply the five SDK patches. Write NO session logic.

Backend interface (nine methods): create_client, connect, send_query, receive_response,
interrupt, set_model, disconnect, extract_cli_pid, is_cli_alive. Plus apply_patches and
permission-result factories. A separate store interface handles persistence.
- receive_response MUST terminate after the turn-complete message and MUST filter out
  None values.
- set_model is non-abstract and raises by default, so a backend without live switching
  produces an honest error rather than a silent no-op.
- The session manager must never import the SDK. Provide a fake backend for tests.

Normalized message type (Layer 1):
  kind in {assistant, user, system, result, stream_event}
  blocks: list of {kind: text|tool_use|tool_result|thinking}
    text        {kind, text}
    tool_use    {kind, name, id, input}      // non-dict input coerced to {}
    tool_result {kind, text, tool_use_id, is_error}
    thinking    {kind}                       // NO text; never forward chain-of-thought
  plus is_sub_agent, subtype, data, cost_usd, is_error, session_id, usage, duration_ms,
  num_turns, raw.

Five patches, applied once at manager construction, idempotent, EACH preceded by
structural assertions that fail loudly if the SDK internals changed:
 1. Tolerant message parser: return None for a structurally valid but unknown message
    (it has a "type" field); re-raise for genuinely malformed input. APPLY IN TWO
    MODULES — the parser module and the client module, because the client imports the
    function by name at import time.
 2. Transport adapter injected at the abstract-base-class boundary right after query
    construction. Two behaviours: (a) reformat permission responses from
    {"allow":true,"input":{…}} / {"allow":false,"reason":…} to
    {"behavior":"allow","updatedInput":{…}} / {"behavior":"deny","message":…}, ONLY when
    the nested response contains an "allow" key, passing everything else through
    byte-identically; (b) suppress the end-of-input call so stdin stays open for the
    bidirectional control protocol.
 3. Windows: inject the no-window creation flag into every subprocess spawn when creation
    flags were not explicitly set. Patch the process constructor, NOT the async
    process-open helper and NOT connect().
 4. POSIX: FORCE session isolation on every subprocess spawn whenever the caller supplied
    no child-setup hook. Do not honour an explicit start_new_session=False — the SDK
    passes it as False at every layer, which made the patch a silent no-op.
 5. Raise the transport's single-message JSON ceiling from 1 MB to a bounded 100 MB
    default (env-overridable, never below the SDK's own value) by reassigning the
    module-level constant.

Never allow a null updatedInput. Enforce it twice: every allow result echoes back the
original tool input dict, AND the adapter re-checks with isinstance and substitutes {}.
Note that dict.get("input", {}) returns None when the key exists with a null value.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Tests prove each patch is idempotent and that each structural assertion fails loudly
   when its precondition is removed.
2. A test proves the tolerant parser is active when reached through the CLIENT module,
   not only the parser module.
3. A test feeds an allow result whose input is None and asserts the emitted control
   response carries updatedInput == {}.
4. A test asserts non-permission control messages pass through the adapter byte-identically.
5. A 5 MB single message is received without error.
6. The whole manager test suite runs against the fake backend with no CLI installed.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.4 — States, a single turn, and the safety nets

Implement the session state machine and one complete turn. NO queue, wake-ups, retries,
or file snapshots yet.

States (serialized lowercase): starting, working, waiting, idle, stopped.
substatus in {"", "compacting", "auto-resuming"} — ALWAYS emitted, empty string included.

State payload — always: session_id, state, cost_usd, error, name, cwd, model,
session_type, working_since (0 unless working), created_ts, tracked_files (LAST 5 ONLY),
substatus, retry_at, retry_attempt, retry_max, retry_reason, entry_count.
Conditional: usage; permission {tool_name, tool_input} when WAITING with a pending tool;
parent_session_id + subsession_origin_turn; inbox_dirty; auto_report_on_idle; queue.

Entry schema (Layer 2): kind, text, name, desc, id, tool_use_id, is_error, timestamp.
Omit empty-string fields on serialization; timestamp always present; is_error only when
true. Kinds: user, asst, tool_use, tool_result, system, permission. Produce NO entry for
thinking blocks or stream events. Truncate assistant text at 50 000; user text and
tool-result text at 20 000. Derive the tool `desc` by first match: description (when both
description and prompt exist) 200 → command 300 → file_path (+ "write N chars" when
content present) → path → pattern 200 → first_key: value 200.

Driver coroutine order: [prepare transcript if resuming] → compute permission mode →
build options and client → START the pre-turn mtime scan in an executor → await connect →
capture CLI PID → state WORKING + emit → reset per-turn flags → await the mtime task →
send prompt and stream (or, with no prompt, consume AT MOST ONE init system message
within a 3-second window and go IDLE).

Follow-up send path, in this exact order: resolve aliases → not-in-memory disk fallback →
under the per-session lock {reject if STOPPED; read but DO NOT CLEAR the interrupted flag;
capture any listener task; set supersede in the SAME lock as the state flip; append the
user entry; state = WORKING} → emit → cancel the captured listener OUTSIDE the lock →
schedule the query coroutine. Inside the query coroutine: await sleep(0) first, then
clear the interrupted and supersede flags.

Implement all four safety nets now:
 (a) stream ended with no RESULT while still WORKING -> force IDLE;
 (b) a finally catch-all that forces IDLE if still WORKING;
 (c) zombie detection in start_session: task done() but state never left WORKING/STARTING
     -> force-clean the record so a restart is possible;
 (d) every handler that mutates state re-checks BOTH task identity AND the supersede flag.

start_session on a live session WITH a prompt forwards to send_message — and must do so
OUTSIDE the manager lock, which is non-reentrant. With no prompt, return
{ok:false, error:"Session already running"}.

Acceptance criteria:
1. One prompt in produces streamed user/asst/tool_use/tool_result entries and ends IDLE.
2. A test drives a fake backend that ends the stream with no RESULT and asserts IDLE.
3. A test asserts start_session on a done-but-WORKING record restarts cleanly.
4. A test asserts a superseded listener cannot set IDLE after a new turn began.
5. A source-guard test asserts the supersede assignment appears inside the same lock block
   as the state flip.
6. A bare resume with no prompt reaches IDLE within ~3 s and leaves nothing in the buffer.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.5 — Permissions

Implement both permission mechanisms and the policy engine.

Primary: an SDK "can use tool" callback with this decision ladder IN STRICT ORDER:
 1. session missing            -> deny WITH interrupt
 2. transport dead             -> flag stream-heal, log STREAM_HEAL_TRIGGER
                                  site=can_use_tool_transport_dead, post ONE visible
                                  "Connection lost — aborting turn, will reconnect and
                                  retry automatically" entry, deny WITH interrupt
 3. question-tool intercept    -> deny WITHOUT interrupt, with a directive redirect
 4. per-session "always"       -> allow
 5. per-session "almost always"-> allow unless dangerous; if dangerous, log a blocked
                                  audit entry and fall through to a manual prompt
 6. global policy auto-approval-> allow
 7. otherwise                  -> store pending event + result holder, record tool name
                                  and input, set WAITING, push session_state and
                                  session_permission, then poll

Poll with a plain threading.Event checked every 0.1 s from the coroutine, up to 36 000
iterations (1 hour). Do NOT use an async event plus call_soon_threadsafe — it does not
reliably wake the waiter. EARLY BAIL: if the client disappears while waiting, auto-ALLOW,
restore WORKING, return. On resolution, remember always/almost-always for the session and
restore WORKING UNLESS the result was deny-with-interrupt. Catch BaseException (not just
Exception) — cancellation is a BaseException subclass — and on any exception restore the
PREVIOUS state and deny with interrupt.

Question-tool intercept: match the tool by name BEFORE every auto-approval path and deny
it WITHOUT interrupt. The denial message must direct the agent to proceed, choose the most
reasonable option at each decision point, complete the work, and present the alternatives
at the END. Record a `permission` entry for the intercept.

Policies: manual | auto | almost_always | sdk_auto | custom; unknown or corrupt behaves as
manual (fail closed). sdk_auto sets the SDK permission mode to accept-edits, but ONLY when
the caller has not pinned a per-session mode. Custom rules are independent and OR-combined:
approve-all-reads, approve-project-reads, approve-all-shell, approve-project-writes (write
AND edit), approve-glob, approve-grep, plus a user regex matched case-insensitively against
a synthesized string built from the tool name and the first of command/file_path/path/
pattern. An invalid regex is silently ignored, never raised.

Dangerous-command detection applies ONLY to the shell tool's `command` string, compiled
lazily into ONE case-insensitive multiline alternation. Block only irreversible or
hard-to-repair actions: permanent file/data destruction, shared-history rewrites, DROP/
TRUNCATE SQL, package publish, and download-piped-to-shell. Explicitly ALLOW recoverable
actions (process kill, permission change, move to temp, container removal, branch delete).

Legacy hook path: a blocking hook_pre_tool IPC method dispatched on its own thread, waiting
up to 3600 s, registering the request in a map keyed by an 8-char id, setting WAITING,
pushing the prompt, and restoring WORKING on resolution. The web route retries IPC 3 times
with 1 s delays and defaults to ALLOW on final failure. Expose ONE unified
resolve_permission to the UI that detects a stored hook id and routes accordingly.

Audit logging appends a `permission` entry for every auto-approval and every almost-always
block; this function MUST NEVER raise.

Persistence: policy at <agent-home>/gui_permission_policy.json (missing/corrupt -> manual);
UI prefs at <agent-home>/gui_ui_prefs.json where the setter MERGES rather than replaces,
ignores non-dict payloads, validates known keys at the daemon boundary, rejects a bool
explicitly where an int is expected (bool is an int subclass), and drops only the invalid
key while siblings still save.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Table-driven tests cover the ladder in order, including that the question-tool intercept
   precedes every auto-approval branch.
2. A test asserts a WAITING session's state payload carries the pending permission, so a
   reconnecting browser can re-render the prompt.
3. A test asserts client-gone during the wait results in ALLOW, not deny.
4. A test asserts a cancelled permission wait restores the PREVIOUS state.
5. A corrupt policy file yields manual.
6. Dangerous-command tests include both true positives and the explicitly-allowed
   recoverable commands.
7. set_ui_prefs with {retention_days: True} rejects that key and still saves siblings.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.6 — Persistence, recovery, the queue, and its gate

Implement durable state and the message queue. Assume PROMPTS 4.1–4.5 are done.

Registry at <agent-home>/gui_active_sessions.json:
  {"sessions": {"<sid>": {name, cwd, model, session_type, state, started_at,
                          last_activity, parent_session_id, subsession_origin_turn,
                          parent_deleted_at, auto_report_on_idle}}}
Exclude STOPPED sessions. Write atomically: temp file IN THE SAME DIRECTORY, then
`replace` (NOT `rename` — Windows rename fails when the destination exists). Debounce on
a 3 s timer with skip-if-a-timer-is-pending. Readers use defaulted lookups and ignore
unknown keys.

Queue at <agent-home>/gui_message_queues.json, a flat {sid: [text, …]}; omit empty
queues; debounce saves on a 1 s timer; NEVER call the immediate save from a queue
operation; cancel the timer and write synchronously on shutdown.

Queue semantics: FIFO (pop index 0); adjacent-duplicate suppression that still emits a
queue update; re-queue AT THE FRONT on dispatch failure; remap with the session on id
change; clear on interrupt by default (clear_queue=True), except the health monitor's
watchdog interrupt which passes clear_queue=False.

Dispatch gate — suppress dispatch on an IDLE emit when ANY of:
  (1) the interrupted flag is set;
  (2) retry_at > 0;
  (3) in-post-turn AND wakeup-pending, UNLESS force-dispatch is set.
Gate (2) and (3) MUST live at the single chokepoint AND be duplicated inside
queue_message, which dispatches directly when the session is already idle.
After a dispatch attempt on IDLE, arm a 3 s deferred re-check that applies the same gates,
retries dispatch, and re-emits IDLE.

Starvation watchdog: sweep every 30 s. Arm a blocked-since timestamp the first sweep a
live, non-stopped session has an undrained queue, and KEEP IT ARMED across sweeps until
the queue empties. Past 120 s (env-overridable), set force-dispatch. Force-dispatch only
when IDLE; a WORKING session just receives the flag. Do not condition the watchdog on
wake-up state.

Transcript repair, both passes, FULL SCOPE:
  Pass 1 — complete an interrupted trailing turn: find the last conversational record
  (skipping trailing snapshot records); if it is an assistant message with a null stop
  reason, set the stop reason to end-of-turn, clear the stop sequence, DROP every
  thinking / redacted-thinking / tool-use block, and append an interruption notice.
  Pass 2 — remove unreplayable thinking blocks across the WHOLE file: a thinking block
  with empty text, or a redacted-thinking block with empty data. A record whose ONLY block
  is unreplayable is DELETED and the parent-uuid chain relinked to the nearest survivor; a
  mixed record has only bad blocks stripped.
Re-parse every line before writing; write nothing on failure; be idempotent; scan with
errors="replace". Run repair on the resume path too, not only at recovery.

Crash recovery at startup on a background thread:
  cycle-detect parent chains (32 hops, force-clear cycles) → read the queue file once →
  for each registry entry, recover if state was working/waiting/starting OR it has queued
  messages; skip pure-idle-with-no-queue, planner sessions, anything older than 3600 s,
  and anything whose transcript file is gone → repair before resuming → resume with the
  full field set → re-hydrate inbox_dirty from disk.

Restart memory: snapshot previously-active sessions BEFORE the first registry write;
get_dormant_states serves it, omitting any session that has since gone live; an explicit
stop calls forget_dormant, removing the id under BOTH its raw and alias-resolved forms.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A test kills the process mid-write and proves the registry is never half-written.
2. A test asserts recovery restores an IDLE session that has a non-empty queue, and skips
   an IDLE session that does not.
3. A test asserts recovery skips a session whose transcript file is missing.
4. Repair is idempotent: a second run leaves bytes identical.
5. A fixture with an empty-but-signed thinking block in the FIRST half of the file is
   repaired (proving the pass is not tail-only).
6. A test asserts a queued message does NOT dispatch while retry_at > 0.
7. A test asserts the starvation watchdog force-dispatches after the timeout even when a
   wake-up is re-armed on every result.
8. A test asserts a stopped session disappears from get_dormant_states under both its raw
   and alias-resolved ids.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.7 — Resilience: heal, retry, watchdogs, reapers

Implement recovery machinery, in this order.

A. Transport self-heal. Six trigger sites, each logging a uniform line
   `STREAM_HEAL_TRIGGER site=<site>` with session, state, post-turn flag, supersede flag,
   and heal count: cli_watchdog, drive_session_except, send_query_except,
   can_use_tool_transport_dead, tool_result_stream_closed, asst_thinking_block_400.
   Classify an error as TRANSPORT when the message contains "Stream closed", "exit code",
   or (case-insensitively) "closed", or when the exception type name contains
   "CLIConnection", "Process", or "ClosedResource"; everything else is an API error.
   Heal policy in the finally of BOTH drive loops: skip entirely if the user stopped/slept;
   otherwise, while heal count <= 3, back off 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, RE-CHECK user-stop AFTER the
   sleep, reconnect, and resend the last user message with a self-heal flag that preserves
   the counter. Never reset the counter on a successful reconnect — reset it ONLY on a
   genuine new user message. Bound reconnects with a semaphore of 2; tear down the dead
   client, run pre-resume preparation, sleep 0.5 s as a stagger, then connect a fresh
   client with resume=<canonical id> and update the tracked PID.
   The post-turn listener must NEVER flag a heal.
   "User stopped" = state is STOPPED OR the interrupted flag is set; check it before any
   reconnect, before the heal reconnect, and AGAIN after the heal's backoff sleep.

B. API-error auto-retry. Three channels: a transient-classified error RESULT; a
   transient-classified non-transport exception mid-stream; an escalated heal that the
   3-try budget could not recover (this one also sets a needs-reconnect flag and refuses
   when the session has NEVER produced a RESULT).
   Classifier — a pure function, no clock, no I/O:
     subtype containing max_turns -> permanent;
     invalid request / authentication / unauthorized / 401 / 403 forbidden /
       permission denied / not found / 404 -> permanent;
     overload(ed) / rate limit / 429 / 529 / 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 / internal server error
       / service unavailable / gateway / temporarily / unavailable / try again, or any
       connectivity signature (timeout, timed out, connection, network, could not resolve,
       name resolution, getaddrinfo, dns, refused, reset, aborted, broken pipe,
       unreachable, no route to host, ssl, tls, handshake, eof occurred, remote end closed,
       temporary failure, failed to establish, max retries exceeded) -> transient;
     unknown -> transient.
   Schedule: base 10 s, factor 2, cap 1800 s, max 30 attempts, jitter +/-20 % floored at
   0.5 s. Base delays for attempts 0..9 must be exactly 10,20,40,80,160,320,640,1280,
   1800,1800.
   Resend decision comes from the TRANSCRIPT: if any tool_use or tool_result entry appears
   after the last user entry, send "Continue from where you left off."; otherwise re-send
   the original user text. Do not key off assistant text.
   ARM THE RETRY BEFORE THE DRAIN. Keep retry_at > 0 until the retry's send has flipped to
   WORKING. Clear the budget and the error banner on a successful turn.
   Controls: cancel clears everything and leaves an explanatory banner; retry-now consumes
   an attempt during a countdown and restores the full budget from a settled error, and
   reconnects ON THE LOOP so the request thread is not blocked.

C. CLI watchdog, 1 s poll, only while WORKING. If the CLI PID reads 0: increment the heal
   counter, set the heal flag, log site=cli_watchdog, disconnect the transport so the
   iterator raises, return. Long-turn heartbeat: after 75 s with no visible content, emit
   EXACTLY ONE system entry with an elapsed-minutes hint and a /compact tip. Never run
   during the post-turn listener.

D. Health monitor, one thread, 30 s tick. Stall detection uses an O(1) fingerprint of
   (entry count, last entry text length, last entry timestamp), NOT elapsed time; threshold
   default 10 minutes (floor 60 s, env <APP>_STALL_MINUTES). Recovery: announce, snapshot
   the queue, interrupt with clear_queue=False, and send a nudge ONLY if the queue was
   empty. Cap at 2 auto-restarts (env <APP>_STALL_MAX_RESTARTS), then give up and leave the
   session IDLE. Never fire for a pending wake-up, a compacting substatus, or a turn
   younger than the window. Sleep detection: a tick gap exceeding tick + 120 s resets EVERY
   stall clock. Windows keep-awake: pulse system-required (never display-required) while
   any session is WORKING. The monitor must never die to an unexpected error.

E. Orphan sweep every 60 s: skip WORKING/WAITING; refresh a stale recorded PID and skip;
   otherwise probe liveness NON-DESTRUCTIVELY — on Windows use
   OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + GetExitCodeProcess, alive iff
   STILL_ACTIVE (259). NEVER use the POSIX signal-0 idiom on Windows: Python's Windows
   implementation TERMINATES the target. Kill dead sessions' process trees.
   Kill guards: refuse a PID that is None, <= 1, or equal to your own (check None FIRST);
   refuse killpg when the target's group equals your own and fall back to a per-PID kill;
   capture the CLI PID BEFORE the SDK disconnect; on Windows, if the parent already died,
   enumerate children by parent id and kill each with /T; on POSIX use
   SIGTERM -> 300 ms -> SIGKILL on the group.

F. Runaway reaper (POSIX only), 60 s sweep: kill any process whose command name is in a
   small allowlist AND whose ACCUMULATED CPU TIME exceeds 120 s. CPU time, not wall time.
   Env knobs for comm list, CPU seconds, interval, and a disable switch.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A test asserts the exact base delay sequence for attempts 0..9.
2. Table-driven classifier tests cover every listed signature plus "unknown -> transient".
3. A test asserts the heal counter is NOT reset by a successful reconnect and IS reset by
   a new user message.
4. A test asserts sleeping the session during the 2/4/8 s backoff aborts the heal.
5. A test asserts the post-turn listener never sets the heal flag, even on a
   transport-shaped error.
6. A test asserts a session producing continuous streaming output is never stalled, and
   one producing nothing is stalled after the window.
7. A test asserts the Windows liveness probe never terminates the target.
8. A test asserts killpg is refused when the target group equals the caller's group.
9. A test asserts the retry is armed BEFORE the drain on a transient-error result.
````

````text
PROMPT 4.8 — File tracking, snapshots, and media eviction — instrumented first

Implement changed-file tracking and context snapshots. BUILD THE INSTRUMENTATION FIRST,
then each optimization against a measured baseline. Do not port an optimization without
its measurement.

Step 1 — instrumentation. Emit one profiling line per snapshot call reporting tracked
count, extras count, total, short-circuit hits, new backups, and loop wall time. Add a
source-level guard test: mark performance-critical regions with a PERF-CRITICAL comment,
and fail the test suite when the current diff touches within a proximity window of any
marker without an explicit acknowledgement.

Step 2 — the snapshot record. Content-addressed backups at
<agent-home>/file-history/<sid>/<md5-16-hex>@v<version>. Append to the transcript:
  {"type":"file-history-snapshot","messageId":<outer uuid>,
   "snapshot":{"messageId":<inner uuid>,
               "trackedFileBackups":{"<abs path>":{backupFileName,version,backupTime} |
                                     {backupFileName:null,version:0,backupTime:null}},
               "timestamp":"<iso8601 Z>"},
   "isSnapshotUpdate":<bool>}
Pre-turn: outer = inner = last USER uuid, isSnapshotUpdate false.
Post-turn: outer = last ASSISTANT uuid, inner = the user uuid, isSnapshotUpdate true.
Read only the LAST 64 KB of the transcript to find those uuids.
Write NO pre-turn snapshot on the first turn (the session id is not yet remapped).

Step 3 — the two change sources. Edit-family tool-use blocks are the ONLY thing that grows
the persistent tracked set. Filesystem mtime diff supplies per-snapshot EXTRAS ONLY, and
runs POST-TURN ONLY. On resume, rebuild the tracked set from edit-tool blocks only;
consult existing snapshot records ONLY to recover version counters.

Step 4 — the optimizations, each with a before/after measurement:
  - (mtime, size) short-circuit against the stat recorded at last backup.
  - Bounded ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) for files that need hashing.
  - Hash-match refresh: when the mtime changed but the content hash did not, refresh the
    stat cache so the short-circuit catches it next turn.
  - `git ls-files` enumeration with a 180 s per-session cache (never below 120 s).
    Two-step discovery: run at the working directory; if that fails, union the results of
    immediate child directories containing a repository.
  - Fallback walk with pruning when there is no repository: skip a fixed set of
    build/cache directory names AND any directory containing a virtualenv marker file.
  - A hard 2 s traversal budget on each scanning function, checked every 256 files; on
    exceedance, log a warning and return the partial result.
  - Mtime carry-forward from the post-turn map into the next pre-turn map, with a full
    rescan every 10 turns.
  - An allowlist of roughly 35 source extensions, and a file_tracking_enabled master
    switch defaulting true.
  - Run the pre-turn snapshot write and the pre-turn mtime record IN PARALLEL via a
    gather of two executor calls, and reset the per-turn direct-edit flag BEFORE the
    gather starts.
  - Start the first-turn mtime scan BEFORE awaiting connect.

Step 5 — memory. Trim in-memory entries to the last 200 once above 500, ONLY on IDLE or
STOPPED. DO NOT clear the mtime dictionaries or the git-file cache there.

Step 6 — pre-resume preparation. Combine transcript repair with stale-media eviction in
ONE read and AT MOST ONE conditional rewrite, writing nothing when nothing changed.
Images inside the last K genuine human user turns (default 4) stay inline; a genuine human
turn excludes sidechain/sub-agent records and user records whose content is only tool
results. Older images are decoded, written content-addressed as <sha256>.<ext> under a
per-session media directory (atomic temp+replace), and replaced IN PLACE with a text
placeholder naming the relative path, media type, and original size, plus an instruction
that the source can be re-read. NO JSONL LINE MAY BE ADDED OR REMOVED. De-duplicate the
byte-identical copy carried in auxiliary tool-result metadata into the same file, replaced
with a marker carrying externalized, sha256, relpath, media_type. An undecodable image
stays inline and the rest proceed; any eviction failure falls back to the repaired-but-
unevicted lines.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A benchmark with 1000 tracked files and 1 changed completes the snapshot loop in
   under 100 ms, with 999 short-circuit hits in the profiling line.
2. A test asserts filesystem-detected files never appear in the persisted tracked set,
   including across a resume.
3. A test asserts the direct-edit flag reset appears before the gather (source-level
   assertion is acceptable and encouraged).
4. A test asserts no pre-turn snapshot is written on the first turn.
5. A degenerate directory tree proves the 2 s traversal budget returns a partial result
   with a warning rather than blocking.
6. A media-eviction test proves the JSONL line count is unchanged, the uuid chain is
   intact, and a second run rewrites nothing.
7. A test asserts the IDLE trim does not clear the mtime dictionaries or the git cache.
````

# Part 5 — The Web Tier: HTTP and WebSocket Surface

## 5.1 What this part covers

This part specifies the **web tier**: the single HTTP + WebSocket server that renders the
application shell, serves every REST endpoint, and brokers all real-time traffic between the
browser and the session engine. It is the only process a browser ever talks to.

It does **not** specify the session engine itself (the process that owns live agent
sessions), the task-board feature, the composition feature, or the git integration. Those
are separate parts. Where this part must reference them, it references them as contracts,
not as implementations.

### Terms, defined once

- **Agent CLI** — the vendor-supplied command-line coding agent that this product wraps. It
  is launched as a subprocess, it writes a transcript to disk, and it exposes hooks. The web
  tier never launches it directly.
- **Session** — one conversation with the agent, identified by a UUID-shaped **session id**
  (`sid`). A session has a working directory, a model, a state, and an ordered list of
  entries.
- **Transcript / JSONL** — the on-disk record of a session, one JSON object per line, written
  by the Agent CLI. The web tier **reads** and **deletes** transcripts; it never writes
  conversational content into them (with one narrow exception, custom-title records).
- **Entry** — one normalized, display-ready item parsed out of a transcript or held in daemon
  memory. Kinds: `user`, `asst`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `system`.
- **Daemon** — the long-lived second process that owns every live session, the agent
  subprocesses, message queues, permission policy, and crash-recovery registry. It survives
  web-tier restarts. The web tier reaches it only over a local IPC socket.
- **Project** — a directory on disk that the user works in. Everywhere in the API a project
  is identified by its **encoded project id**: the absolute path with the five characters
  `\`, `/`, `:`, `_`, `.` each replaced by `-`. (Why five, and why exactly those, is
  specified in the path-handling part; get it byte-exact or sessions silently vanish from
  filtered views.)
- **Utility session** — a short-lived internal session the product spawns for itself
  (`session_type` of `planner` or `title`). Utility sessions are forced into a system working
  directory, hidden from the user's session list, and their transcripts are deleted when they
  finish.
- **Subsession** — a user-visible child session spawned from a parent session, seeded with the
  parent's transcript. Subsessions are explicitly **not** utility sessions.

Two artifacts in this part are the load-bearing deliverables: the **complete HTTP endpoint
table** (§5.5) and the **complete WebSocket event catalogue** (§5.6). Everything else exists
to make those two tables implementable correctly.

---

## 5.2 Server topology and the async-mode decision

### 5.2.1 Process layout

The product must run as two cooperating processes on one machine, both bound to loopback
only, plus one optional third:

| Tier | Default port | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| **Web** | 5050 (override via `WEB_PORT`, or `TEST_PORT` for a fully isolated test instance) | HTTP + WebSocket surface; all side-car state on disk (names, tombstones, trash, search index); all transcript **reading**; browser assets |
| **Daemon** | 5051 (override via `DAEMON_PORT`) | Every live session, agent subprocesses, message queues, permission policy, UI prefs, crash-recovery registry, per-turn file snapshots |
| **Reviver** (opt-in) | control 5052, guardian 5053; binds 5050 only while the web tier is down | A phone-facing "Start the app" page so a remote user is not stranded on a bare proxy error |

Both servers must bind `127.0.0.1` exclusively. The development WSGI server *is* the
production server — this is a single-user local tool and that trade is deliberate. Do not
introduce a reverse proxy, a WSGI container, or a multi-process worker model; several
invariants in this document (in-process broadcast from background threads, a module-level
thread pool, a process-wide config cache) assume exactly one web process.

**Why a separate daemon at all:** the daemon must survive web-tier restarts so that running
sessions continue uninterrupted when the user restarts the UI. A web-only restart must set
an environment flag (call it `PRESERVE_DAEMON=1`) that makes the replacement web process skip
the "kill whatever is on the daemon port" step.

> **Hard operational rule.** No automated agent may restart the daemon. Restarting it
> destroys every live session in the application. Expose the daemon-restart path only as an
> explicit, human-initiated UI action, and make any programmatic restart endpoint default to
> web-only scope.

### 5.2.2 Ownership boundary

Draw this line once and never blur it:

| Concern | Owner |
|---|---|
| Live session state, entries, cost, permission prompts, queues | Daemon (web reads over IPC) |
| Session transcripts (`*.jsonl`) | Written by the Agent CLI; **read** by web; **deleted/moved** by web |
| Session display names, delete tombstones, utility-session marks, id remaps, access timestamps, trash | Web |
| Active-session registry, message queues, permission policy, UI prefs | Daemon (web may read the UI-prefs file directly, read-only) |
| Search index | Web |
| Application config | Web |
| Agent CLI's own settings file | The Agent CLI; web offers a read/write editor over it |

**The web tier must never hold a real session-manager object.** It must hold only a *proxy*
whose every method is an IPC call. This matters more than it looks: in testing mode the proxy
is typically replaced with an auto-mocking stub, and an auto-mocking stub fabricates any
attribute you ask for. A method that exists on the daemon but was never added to the proxy
therefore passes every unit test and raises `AttributeError` in production.

> **Learned the hard way.** A missing proxy method shipped and produced a 500 on a real user
> action. The fix is a **static parity test**: for every `proxy.<method>` call site in route
> and event-handler code, assert the proxy class defines `<method>`, and assert that method
> issues an IPC request whose name matches a handler key registered on the daemon. Pure
> source analysis, no runtime, no mocks. Build this test before the proxy grows past ten
> methods.

### 5.2.3 The async-mode decision

**Run the WebSocket layer in threading mode.** One OS thread per event handler and per HTTP
request, drawn from a pool. No event loop in the web tier at all. Allow all origins for the
WebSocket handshake (it is loopback-bound; the tailnet exposure discussed in §5.11 is the
real trust question and CORS does not help there).

Consequences you must design around:

- **Synchronous blocking libraries are safe.** Blocking IPC, `subprocess.run`, and
  synchronous browser-automation APIs can all be called directly from a handler.
- **Handlers serialize behind the slowest one.** This is not theoretical. An active
  client-heartbeat mechanism (`client_ping` / `client_pong`) was added and reverted within a
  day because pongs were served on the same worker pool as daemon IPC. Under load the pong
  exceeded the client's 8-second liveness timeout, the client cycled its socket, the
  reconnect fired a fresh connect handler, the connect handler issued a blocking
  "get all states" IPC call, and the congestion got worse — producing a cascade of spurious
  "engine stopped" overlays.
  **The rule that emerged: any liveness probe must be served by a path that cannot be starved
  by IPC latency.** In practice this means HTTP `/api/ping` (which touches nothing) is the
  liveness probe, and there is no WebSocket-level heartbeat of your own on top of the
  transport's.
- **No external message broker.** Single web process, so background threads inside the
  process may call the broadcast emit function directly.
- **No namespaces and no rooms.** See §5.6.5 — this is a real design decision with real
  costs, and it must be stated explicitly rather than discovered.

---

## 5.3 Startup sequence (ordered, with what must run exactly once)

Boot is where this class of product usually fails silently, so the sequence is specified in
full. Steps marked **[D]** are detached/backgrounded.

### 5.3.1 Launcher

1. **Windows:** change directory to the script's own directory, then locate the
   *windowless* Python interpreter (`pythonw`). If present, spawn the bootstrap script with
   it and exit immediately **[D]**. A windowless interpreter has no console, so there is
   nothing the user — or an OS sign-out — can close. Fall back to a minimized console launch
   *only* when the windowless interpreter is genuinely absent.
2. **POSIX:** spawn the bootstrap with `nohup … &` and then `disown`, appending output to a
   server log. The trio `nohup` + `&` + `disown` is what makes it a true daemon under bash;
   drop any one and closing the terminal takes the server with it.

> **Failure mode this prevents:** a user minimized the launcher window, later closed it, and
> the web server died while the daemon and all sessions stayed alive. The UI showed a dead
> page and the user believed they had lost their work.

### 5.3.2 Bootstrap script (the universal launch choke point)

Every launch path — desktop shortcut, both launchers, and the restart endpoint — must run
through this one script.

3. `chdir` to the script's own resolved parent. Lock the working directory regardless of how
   the process was started.
4. **PATH augmentation, POSIX only, before any import.** Prepend the usual user-local binary
   directories and the active Node version-manager bin directory (resolving one level of
   alias indirection). Desktop-entry launches and windowless interpreters do not source a
   login shell, so a naive `which(agent-cli)` fails and the daemon subprocess inherits a
   broken PATH.
5. If stdout/stderr are `None` (windowless interpreter), redirect both to the server log.
6. **Spawn-mode probe.** Append exactly one line to the server log recording the interpreter
   and whether the process is detached (on POSIX, detached ⇔ session id equals pid). This is
   the only on-disk signal that says whether a given run was attached or detached. If a
   future launcher change silently foregrounds the server, this line is the smoking gun.
7. **Boot splash [D].** Pre-flight the GUI toolkit import *in-process* (some Linux
   distributions ship it as a separate package and the splash would otherwise exit silently).
   Create an empty status file in the temp directory, export its path, spawn the splash
   process. On failure fall back to an OS notification that names the missing package.
8. **Reviver hand-off**, only when the remote-access feature is enabled in config: POST to the
   reviver's control port asking it to release port 5050 *without dying* (2 s timeout), then
   best-effort re-spawn the reviver **[D]**.
9. Execute the main entry module.

### 5.3.3 Main entry module

10. **Import the early-boot shim first, before any third-party import.** Two jobs:
    (a) pre-seed the platform-identification cache so nothing later triggers a system
    management query — a wedged OS management service froze boot indefinitely and the splash
    misleadingly displayed a much earlier step; (b) arm a 120-second hang dump that writes
    every thread's stack to the log.
11. `STEP:cache` → recursively remove compiled-bytecode caches so code changes always take
    effect.
12. Resolve ports from environment. A test port must skip *all* production setup (no port
    killing, no daemon spawn, no singleton).
13. Start a **boot watchdog** thread ticking every 3 s with per-step budgets:
    cache 20 s, loading 75 s, ports 30 s, deps 600 s, daemon 45 s, server 60 s (default 45 s).
    On overrun: dump stacks and write an `ERROR:` line naming the step and elapsed seconds to
    the splash.
14. `STEP:loading` → perform the heavy application import. **This step exists solely so the
    splash does not sit on the previous step during a long import.** Without it, a freeze here
    looked like a stuck cache purge.
15. `STEP:ports` → kill whatever holds the web port; kill the daemon port **only if
    `PRESERVE_DAEMON != 1`**. Retry up to 5 rounds with 0.5 s sleeps, using the
    platform-appropriate discovery tool with a fallback for systems missing the primary one.
16. **Singleton gate.** Acquire a named kernel mutex (Windows) or an exclusive non-blocking
    file lock (POSIX). **The lock name must include the port.** Hardcoding the name made every
    test instance and side-by-side instance fail the check because the production instance
    held it. On failure, log "stale singleton, starting anyway" and proceed — the ports were
    just killed, so proceeding is the correct recovery.
17. Self-heal the desktop shortcut so it points at the windowless interpreter.
18. `STEP:deps` → for each required package check whether it is importable and install the
    missing ones with a 600 s timeout, **capturing output**. A previous quiet install with an
    ignored return code printed "Packages installed successfully" on a failed install with
    zero diagnostics.
19. Start the agent auto-update worker **[D]**. It waits for boot to complete, then probes
    network reachability every 300 s until reachable, throttled to once per 24 h via a state
    file. **It must not run synchronously before daemon startup** — a slow or dead network
    stalled boot until the watchdog declared it dead. Accepted trade: an update lands on disk
    mid-session and takes effect on the daemon's next *cold* start.
20. `STEP:daemon` → ensure the daemon is running:
    - Try connecting to the daemon port with a 1 s timeout; if it answers, return.
    - Otherwise spawn it with an **explicit environment dict** (the WSGI environ filter on the
      restart path can strip the port variable), stdout/stderr to a daemon log preceded by a
      boundary marker line, detached (no window + new process group on Windows, new session on
      POSIX) **[D]**.
    - Poll for the bind: **100 attempts × 0.1 s = 10 s**. Short-circuit if the child already
      exited. (5 s was not enough: cold daemon start with recovery work takes 5–7 s on slow
      machines.)
    - Distinguish three failure modes loudly — *process dead, no bind*; *process alive, no
      bind*; *spawn never fired* — and print the **last 30 lines of the daemon log inline**.
      The historic version of this bug was silent: the web tier came up daemonless, the UI
      looked normal, and tool calls failed mysteriously a minute later.
21. `STEP:server` → build the application object. On exception, write `ERROR:` to the splash
    and re-raise.
22. Signal boot done and disarm the hang dump.
23. Logging: tee stdout/stderr to a web log; root logger at INFO; attach the console handler
    to **exactly two logger namespaces — the route package and the daemon-client module.**
    Removing the daemon-client namespace silences all IPC latency logging; nothing crashes,
    the operator just goes blind. Silence the WSGI access log to ERROR and suppress the
    framework banner.
24. `STEP:browser`, then `DONE`; a 5-second timer unlinks the splash status file.
25. Launch the browser **[D]**, but **only on a cold start** (skip when `PRESERVE_DAEMON=1`)
    — on a web restart the user already has a tab open and the socket reconnects on its own.
    Wait for the server with up to 60 one-second polls and abort rather than open a broken tab.
26. Serve.

### 5.3.4 Application factory — internal order

1. Create the app with explicit template and static directories; enable template auto-reload.
2. Initialize the WebSocket layer in threading mode.
3. **If not testing:** construct the daemon proxy, **start its threads**, and *then* register
   the WebSocket handlers. Order matters — the proxy's reader/emitter threads must be alive
   before any handler can be invoked.
   **If testing:** install an auto-mocking stub *with explicit non-mock defaults* for at least
   `has_session → False`, `get_all_states → []`, `get_dormant_states → {}`,
   `get_entry_count → 0`. A bare mock is truthy and not JSON-serializable, so it leaks into
   session lists and makes serialization raise.
4. Register all blueprints. None takes a URL prefix except the composition blueprint. There
   must be no path collisions and registration order must not be load-bearing.
5. Mount optional subsystems (voice) defensively — a failed import must leave the rest of the
   product running with that feature off. Pre-warm expensive subsystem installs in the
   background so they are ready before the user finishes reading the boot animation.
6. **Startup-only cleanups.** Prune orphaned system/utility sessions and title-only stub
   transcripts here — **exactly once, at boot, never on a request path** (§5.14 rule 4).
7. Start background workers: git status fetcher, composition file watcher (4 s poll), remote
   access re-arm (threaded, non-blocking).
8. Register a template helper that appends `?v=<file mtime>` to static URLs.
9. **Cache headers.** Set the default static max-age to 0, and add an after-request hook:
   `/static/*` gets `no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` plus legacy `Pragma`/`Expires`, and
   **`text/html` gets `no-cache, must-revalidate`.** Without the HTML rule, mobile Safari and
   home-screen web apps serve cached HTML that points at stale cache-busted asset URLs, so
   fixes never reach the device even though the `?v=` changed.

---

## 5.4 Talking to the daemon: the client side of IPC, heartbeats, and failure UX

### 5.4.1 Wire protocol

Raw TCP over loopback, newline-delimited JSON, **one** long-lived connection, `TCP_NODELAY`
set. Four message shapes:

```
request  { "req_id": "<8 hex>", "method": "<name>", "params": { ... } }
response { "req_id": "<8 hex>", "result": <any> }
error    { "req_id": "<8 hex>", "error": "<text>" }
push     { "event": "<name>", "data": { ... } }        // no req_id
```

A `push` is unsolicited: the daemon originates it and the web tier forwards it to browsers.

### 5.4.2 Thread model inside the proxy

| Thread | Job |
|---|---|
| reader | `recv()` into a byte buffer; decode **only up to the last newline**; route responses to waiting events and pushes onto the emit queue |
| emitter | Drain an unbounded queue and call the broadcast emit. **Exists so WebSocket backpressure can never delay IPC response processing.** |
| heartbeat | `ping` every 20 s with an 8 s timeout |
| resync (one-shot) | After connect, fetch id-alias map and permission policy |
| reconnect (on demand) | 2 s retry loop; at attempt 5 (~10 s) respawn the daemon process |

Locks: one write lock serializing socket sends; one pending-map lock protecting the
`req_id → (event, result-holder)` dictionary. Default request timeout **30 s**. The
permission-hook request uses **3600 s** because it blocks on a human answering a prompt.

### 5.4.3 Framing and disconnect rules — each of these was a bug

- **Decode only up to the last newline in the buffer.** A multi-byte character split across
  two `recv()` calls otherwise raises a decode error and desynchronizes the stream.
- **Stale-disconnect guard.** The reader must snapshot the socket object it is reading and
  only mark the client disconnected if that snapshot is still the current socket. Otherwise a
  reconnect that already succeeded gets stomped back to disconnected.
- **Force-disconnect must `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` before `close()`.** On Linux, `close()` alone
  does not unblock a `recv()` already mid-call — it can hang until the next packet arrives.
- **Both TCP keepalive and an application heartbeat are required.** Keepalive alone has too
  long a worst-case detection window on some kernels; the heartbeat alone will not catch a
  send blocking inside a zombie socket buffer. Tune keepalive to roughly 30 s total
  (idle 15 s, interval 5 s, count 3), with the platform-specific fallback where the granular
  options do not exist.
- **Connect without resync, then resync from a background thread.** Resyncing before the
  reader thread exists blocks the full 30 s waiting for a response nobody will deliver — and
  it blocks application construction, so the whole product fails to boot.

### 5.4.4 Failure UX

The reconnect state machine must broadcast a `daemon_reconnect` event at four discrete points
with `status ∈ {disconnected, connecting, restarting, connected}`, plus `attempt` and a
human-readable `message`. `restarting` fires at exactly attempt 5, when the client respawns
the daemon.

The browser turns this into a blocking overlay only after a **five consecutive failure**
threshold on a *separate* HTTP health probe (§5.11.3), not on the first `disconnected` event.
Rationale: transient network handoffs on mobile produce short disconnects constantly, and an
overlay that flashes on every one of them trains users to ignore it.

---

## 5.5 Complete HTTP API

Conventions used in every table:

- `?project` is always an **encoded project id**. It is optional; absent means "the active
  project."
- Unless stated otherwise, responses are JSON objects and errors are
  `{"error": "<message>"}` with the listed status code.
- `<sid>` is a session id.

**Blueprint-wide traversal guard (session routes).** Before any handler runs, if a `project`
value — taken from the query string, or from the JSON body on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE —
contains `/`, `\`, or `..`, respond `400 {"error": "invalid project name"}`. Additionally,
**every route that composes a filesystem path from a session id must validate the sid shape
first**: reject empty, over-long, and anything containing `..`, `/`, `\`, `:`, a NUL byte, or
characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

### 5.5.1 Shell, health, lifecycle

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/` | Single-page app shell | — | HTML, with a device-name string injected for the add-to-home-screen title | — |
| GET | `/manifest.webmanifest` | Per-machine installable-app manifest, generated at request time | — | `name`, `short_name` (≤12 chars else product name), `description`, `start_url` `/`, `scope` `/`, `display` `standalone`, `orientation` `portrait`, `background_color`, `theme_color`, one 256×256 icon with `purpose: "any maskable"`; mimetype `application/manifest+json` | — |
| GET | `/api/ping` | Liveness | — | `{ok: true}` | never |
| GET | `/api/health` | Full-stack readiness | — | `ok`, `web` (always true), `daemon` (bool, read from a **cached flag**, never a round-trip), `ready` (= `daemon`) | never |
| GET | `/api/docs` | API reference page | — | HTML | 404 |
| GET | `/api/docs/<path:filename>` | Reference assets (the OpenAPI document) | — | file | 404 |
| POST | `/api/restart` | Restart web / daemon / both | `scope` ∈ `web` (default) \| `daemon` \| `both` | `{ok: true, message: "Restarting (<scope>)..."}` | 500 |
| POST | `/api/shutdown` | Stop web + daemon | — | `{ok: true, message: "Server shutting down..."}` | 500 |

### 5.5.2 Sessions: CRUD, trash, fork/rewind, subsessions

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/sessions` | Merged disk + daemon session list | `?project` | **array** of `id, display_title, custom_title, user_named, date, last_activity, last_activity_ts, effective_ts, sort_ts, size, file_bytes, message_count, preview, model`; optionally `parent_session_id, subsession_origin_turn, session_type:"subsession", inbox_dirty, last_state` | 400 |
| GET | `/api/resolve-session/<sid>` | Old id → canonical id | `?project` | `id`, `remapped` | — |
| GET | `/api/session/<sid>` | Session detail | `?meta_only=1`, `?project` | meta: `id, display_title, custom_title`; full adds `date, size, message_count, messages[{role, content, type}], preview` | 404 |
| POST | `/api/rename/<sid>` | User rename | `title` (required), `project` | `ok`, `title` | 400 on empty title or non-JSON body |
| POST | `/api/remap-name` | Move a stored name to a new id | `old_id`, `new_id`, `project` | `ok`, `title`; or `ok`, `skipped` | 400 missing ids |
| POST | `/api/autoname/<sid>` | Generate a title (§5.9) | `project`, `prompt`, `re_evaluate` | `ok`, `title`, `renamed`; or `ok`, `skipped`, `reason` | 404, 500 |
| DELETE | `/api/delete/<sid>` | Four-phase soft delete | `?project` | `ok` | — |
| GET | `/api/trash` | Recoverable sessions, newest first | `?project` | `ok`, `trash[{id, name, deleted_at, deleted_at_iso, purge_at, purge_at_iso, size}]`; `purge_at: null` means kept forever | — |
| POST | `/api/trash/<sid>/restore` | Restore and re-apply title | `project` | `ok`, `id`, `title` | 404 |
| DELETE | `/api/trash/<sid>` | Permanent purge | `?project` | `ok`, `purged` | — |
| DELETE | `/api/delete-all` | Delete every session in the project | `?project` | `ok`, `deleted` | — |
| DELETE | `/api/delete-empty` | Delete sessions with `message_count == 0` | `?project` | `ok`, `deleted` | — |
| POST | `/api/duplicate/<sid>` | Copy the transcript under a new id, rewriting the embedded session id on every line | `?project` | `ok`, `new_id` | 404 |
| POST | `/api/continue/<sid>` | New session seeded with a hand-off summary | `?project` | `ok`, `new_id`, `title` (prefixed `[cont]`, ≤55 chars) | 404 |
| GET | `/api/session-timeline/<sid>` | Data for the fork/rewind picker | `?project` | `messages[]`, `has_snapshots`, `title`. An in-memory-only session returns **200** with `messages: []` and an `error` string | 404 |
| POST | `/api/fork/<sid>` | New session from transcript lines ≤ N | `up_to_line` (required) | `ok`, `new_id`, `title` (prefixed `[fork]`) | 400, 404 |
| POST | `/api/rewind/<sid>` | Reverse file edits back to a message | `up_to_line` (required) | `ok`, `files_restored[]`, `files_skipped[]`, `rewind_orphans[]` | 400, 404 |
| POST | `/api/fork-rewind/<sid>` | Fork **and** restore files from snapshots | `up_to_line` (required) | `ok`, `new_id`, `title` (prefixed `[fork+rewind]`, ≤48 chars), `files_restored[]`, `files_skipped[]` | 400, 404 |
| POST | `/api/open/<sid>` | Resume a session via the daemon | `?project` | `ok`; plus `already_running: true` when applicable | 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<parent>/spawn-subsession` | Spawn a child seeded with the parent transcript | `?project` | `ok`, `new_id`, `parent_id`, `title` (prefixed `[sub]`), `subsession_origin_turn` | 400 bad sid / cross-project / planner parent; 404; **409 parent-chain cycle**; 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<child>/report-to-parent` | Append a conclusion to the parent's inbox | `summary` (required), `attachments[]` | `ok`, `report_id`, `parent_session_id`, `undelivered_count` | 400, 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<parent>/pull-subsession-updates` | Deliver pending reports as the parent's next turn | `?project` | `ok`, `pulled`, `queued`, `undelivered_count` | 400, 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<child>/reanchor` | Re-anchor a rewind-orphaned child | `origin_turn` (defaults to the parent's line count) | `ok`, `subsession_origin_turn` | 400, 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<child>/detach` | Detach from parent | `?project` | `ok` | 400, 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/sessions/<child>/auto-report-toggle` | Toggle report-on-idle | `on` (bool) | `ok`, `auto_report_on_idle` | 400, 404, 500 |
| GET | `/api/sessions/<sid>/last-conclusion` | Newest meaningful assistant text (prefills the report box) | `?project` | `ok`, `session_id`, `text` | 400, 404 |

Behavioral notes that belong to this group:

- **Fork/rewind rewind order:** process edits in **reverse** so nested edits undo correctly.
  A whole-file write cannot be reversed by string replacement — skip it in the edit loop so
  the snapshot loop gets a chance to find a backup, then add a catch-all so un-snapshotted
  write targets appear in `files_skipped` rather than silently vanishing.
- **Rewind orphans are surfaced, never auto-detached.** The response lists them; the UI offers
  re-anchor or detach.
- **`pull-subsession-updates` must be its own endpoint.** Routing it through the WebSocket
  send-message handler is impossible because that handler rejects empty text *before* any
  inbox-drain branch could run. This endpoint is the **deliver** side; the inbox write is a
  separate side. It must not fall back to writing the inbox, and it must no-op safely so a
  button mash cannot inject a stream of empty turns.
- **Parent deletion orphans children**: clear the child's parent pointer, record a
  `parent_deleted_at` timestamp, remove the inbox directory, and make `report-to-parent`
  refuse the write so the UI can render "Reports to: (parent deleted)". `parent_deleted_at`
  must survive daemon recovery — it once did not, and a daemon restart erased the orphan state
  so the UI flipped back to naming a parent that no longer existed.

**Every file endpoint must be gated to the user's home directory** and return **403** outside
it. Name collisions resolve as `"<stem> (<n>)<suffix>"` starting at n = 1. When the filename

the resolved-target home check is still the real guard.

### 5.5.4 Projects

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/projects` | Visible projects | — | array of `{encoded, display, custom_name, session_count, active}` | — |
| POST | `/api/set-project` | Switch the active project | `project` | `ok`, `project`, `display` | 404 |
| POST | `/api/rename-project` | Set or clear a display name | `encoded`, `name` (empty clears) | `ok` | 400 |
| POST | `/api/delete-project` | Remove the project's session directory | `encoded` | `ok` | 404, 500 |
| POST | `/api/add-project` | Register a project | `mode` ∈ `browse` \| `path` \| `create`, plus `path` / `name` | `ok`, `encoded`, `path`; or **200** `{ok:false, cancelled:true}` when the user dismissed the native picker | 400 invalid path / no name / unknown mode / no picker available; 500 |
| GET | `/api/find-projects` | Scan known roots one level deep for unregistered repositories | — | `{projects:[{path, name, encoded, type, indicators[]}]}` | — |
| POST | `/api/project-chat` | Keyword project finder — **not** an LLM | `message` | `content` (markdown), `suggestions[]`, `matches[{path, name, type, encoded, score}]` | — |
| POST | `/api/new-session` | Start or resume a session | `name`, `resume_id`, `prompt` | `ok`, `new_id` | 400 project directory missing; 500 |

Project **visibility filters**: skip internal agent directories; skip the system utility
project — checked **twice**, once by encoded name and once by normalized decoded path; and
require the decoded display path to start with the user's home directory.

**Project type detection.** Check indicator files in a fixed order and label by the first hit:
`.git, package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, pom.xml,
build.gradle, Makefile, .sln, .csproj, CMakeLists.txt, Gemfile, composer.json`. A `.git`
anywhere forces the "Git repo" label.

**Project-chat algorithm:** tokenize the message on non-word characters keeping tokens longer
than 2 characters; recurse at most 2 levels; stop at 15 matches; skip dependency,
build-cache, VCS, and virtual-environment directories and all dot-directories; score as
`2 × name_match + len(indicators)`; return the top 10 and suggest the top 5.

### 5.5.5 Analysis

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/summary/<sid>` | Server-rendered HTML digest | `?project` | `{html}` | 404; or 200 with a "no content" paragraph |
| GET | `/api/extract-code/<sid>` | All fenced code blocks | `?project` | `blocks[]`, `count`, `languages[]` | 404 |
| GET | `/api/export-project/<sid>` | ZIP of de-duplicated blocks plus a README | `?project` | `application/zip`, attachment | 404; or 200 `{error:"No code blocks found"}` |
| GET | `/api/compare/<id1>/<id2>` | Diff two sessions' code blocks | `?project` | `session1`, `session2` (each `{title, date, size, message_count}`), `code_diff[{filename, language, status, content1, content2}]`, `stats{s1_blocks, s2_blocks, added, removed, changed}` | 404 |

Summary layout the client must be able to style: a topic line, a stats line, an overview
built from the first ≤2 meaningful messages over 20 characters (capped 180/177 chars, broken
at 200 joined), a "key topics" section (messages split into `min(5, n)` chunks, highest-scoring
message per chunk, de-duplicated on the first 12 lowercased characters of the label, label =
first three content words longer than 3 characters that are not stop words, description capped
130/127), and a "recent focus" section (last 3 messages, 130 chars). Emit stable CSS class
names for these four regions.

Compare status values: present in only one session → `removed` / `added`; present in both →
similarity above 0.98 → `same`, else `changed`.

> **Known defect to fix in a clean-room build:** the summary endpoint interpolates user text
> into HTML without escaping. Escape it.

### 5.5.8 Admin

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/admin/scrub-phantoms` | Remove phantom rows from the stored-names file | `project?`, `dry_run` (**default true**) | `ok`, `dry_run`, `total_removed`, `per_project[{project, removed, backup, phantoms?, error?}]` | 400 unknown project (echo `valid_projects`); **429** when a scrub is already running |

The admin project enumerator deliberately diverges from the user-facing one: **no
home-directory filter** (an admin scrub is installation-wide) but it still skips
underscore-prefixed internal names. Serialize scrubs with a non-blocking lock and return 429
rather than queueing — two concurrent scrubs race the same names file.

### 5.5.9 Test runner

| Method | Path | Key request | Key response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/run-tests` | `{mode: "fast" \| "full"}` (anything else → `fast`) | `text/event-stream` with `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Frames: `{type:"line", line}` repeatedly, then `{type:"done", exit_code, passed, failed, errors, skipped, ok}`. Failures are **in-band** `{type:"error", line}` — including `"Tests already running"`. **Always HTTP 200.** |
| POST | `/api/cancel-tests` | — | `{ok:true, message:"Tests cancelled"}` or `{ok:false, message:"No tests running"}` |

Counts derived by tallying progress characters in emitted lines are approximate and inflated
by traceback text. **`exit_code` and `ok` are authoritative** — say so in the UI. Hold the
serialization lock *through* process spawn, or two simultaneous POSTs both observe "nothing
running" and both spawn a test run.

| Method | Path | Key request | Key response |

| GET | `/api/mobile/status` | — | `enabled, installed, logged_in, backend_state, serving, url, port, needs, https_help, device_name, account, phone_connected, phone_name, host_os, install_url` |

The port used for status and enable must be **parsed from the request's `Host` header** — the
port the browser actually reached *is* the port the tunnel should serve — falling back to

`enable_https` | `starting`.
