### 5.5.12 Watchdog bridge

| Method | Path | Key request | Key response | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/fix-from-watchdog` | `?d=<gzip + base64url JSON>` | `text/html` interstitial that stores the target project in local storage, polls the session list every **400 ms** up to a **12 000 ms** deadline, then replaces the location with the deep link to the new session | 400 missing/invalid payload; 502 start failure |

> **Security note a clean-room build must act on.** This is an unauthenticated, unsigned,
> link-triggerable GET that mutates global state and starts an agent with a fully
> attacker-controlled prompt, from an unbounded compressed payload (a decompression-bomb
> surface). **Sign the token and bound the decompressed size.**

**Build a coverage test** that walks the framework's URL map and asserts every route is
present in the published OpenAPI document (and vice versa). It is cheap and it catches the
entire class of "we shipped an endpoint nobody documented."

## 5.6 Complete WebSocket event catalogue

Endpoint: the same origin and port as HTTP. The handshake carries a `project` query parameter
(the encoded project id, read from browser local storage). **The client must rewrite that
query parameter on every connect attempt** so reconnect handshakes carry the *current* value,
not the value from page load.

Two delivery mechanisms, and the distinction is load-bearing:

- **Reply emit** — emitted from inside a handler, bound to the request context → delivered to
  **only the requesting socket**.
- **Broadcast emit** — emitted from the daemon-proxy emitter thread, a background watcher, or
  a REST handler → delivered to **every connected client**.

**Universal preamble:** if an inbound payload is not a JSON object, emit
`error {"message": "Invalid data"}` and return. The UI-preferences setter is the single
exception — it returns silently.

### 5.6.1 Client → server

| Event | Payload | Server behavior | Emits back |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connect` | (handshake `?project`) | Fetch all states from the daemon, filter by project, build the queue map, snapshot the id-alias map | `state_snapshot` (requester) |
| `disconnect` | — | Debug log only. **No per-socket state is tracked anywhere.** | — |
| `request_state_snapshot` | `project?` | If `project` differs from the server's active project and that directory exists, set the active project — a safety net for endpoints that receive no explicit project (notably the log fetch). Then build the same snapshot. | `state_snapshot`; an **empty** snapshot when the daemon proxy is disconnected |
| `start_session` | `session_id` (required), `prompt`, `cwd`, `name`, `resume`, `model`, `system_prompt`, `thinking_level`, `max_turns`, `allowed_tools`, `permission_mode`, `session_type`, `compose_task_id`, `voice`, `project`, `remote_tailnet` | §5.6.2 | `session_started {session_id}` or `error {message, session_id}` |
| `send_message` | `session_id`, `text` (required), `voice`, `project`, `remote_tailnet` | Optional remote-access preamble; forward to the daemon; **record session access even on failure** | `message_ack {session_id[, queued:true]}` or `send_failed {session_id, error, text}` |
| `permission_response` | `session_id`, `action` ∈ `y` \| `n` \| `a` \| `aa` | `allow = action ∈ {y,a,aa}`, `always = (a)`, `almost_always = (aa)` | nothing on success; `error` on failure |
| `interrupt_session` | `session_id` | Interrupt the running turn | `error` on failure |
| `set_session_model` | `session_id`, `model` | Ask the daemon to switch models | **always** `session_model_result {ok, session_id, model[, error]}` |
| `cancel_auto_retry` | `session_id` | Cancel a pending API-error retry countdown | `error` on failure |
| `retry_now` | `session_id` | Fire the pending retry immediately | `error` on failure |
| `close_session` | `session_id` | Stop the session | nothing; **an error whose text is exactly `"Session not found"` must be swallowed** |
| `get_session_log` | `session_id`, `since`, `limit`, `before`, `project` | §5.6.3 | `session_log` (requester) |
| `get_permission_policy` | — | Read policy from the daemon | `permission_policy_loaded`; on exception emit the safe default `{policy:"manual", custom_rules:{}}` |
| `set_permission_policy` | `policy`, **`customRules`** (camelCase) | Validate against the five allowed policies | `error` enumerating valid values on rejection |
| `get_ui_prefs` | — | Read prefs from the daemon | `ui_prefs_loaded`; `{}` on exception |
| `set_ui_prefs` | arbitrary object | Persist prefs | — |
| `queue_message` | `session_id`, `text` | Enqueue for the busy session | `error` on failure; the daemon pushes `queue_updated` |
| `remove_queue_item` | `session_id`, `index` (default −1) | Remove one queued item | `error` on failure |
| `edit_queue_item` | `session_id`, `index`, `text` | Edit one queued item | `error` on failure |
| `clear_queue` | `session_id` | Empty the queue | `error` on failure |
| `get_queue` | `session_id` | Fetch the queue | `queue_updated {session_id, queue}` (requester) |

> **Defect to fix rather than reproduce:** the queue index handlers coerce `index` to an
> integer without guarding. A non-numeric index raises inside the handler and — because there
> is no blanket exception wrapper (see `error` below) — **the client never hears back at all.**
> Validate and reply with `error`.

### 5.6.2 `start_session` — full ordered semantics

The order here is the specification; do not reorder.

1. Parse and normalize. Empty-string options become null. `permission_mode` must be one of
   `default | plan | acceptEdits | bypassPermissions`, else drop it. `allowed_tools` must be a
   list. `max_turns` coerces to int, else null.
2. If `session_type ∈ {planner, title}`, **forcibly rewrite `cwd` to the system utility
   directory** (creating it) so utility transcripts never land in the user's project.
3. *Then* check that `session_id` is present. (After the rewrite — the rewrite is
   unconditional on type, not on id validity.)
4. For non-utility sessions, record a session-access timestamp.
5. Read the cross-session-awareness flag from config (default on) for non-utility sessions.
6. **Parallel setup phase.** Two independent resolvers may each append to `system_prompt`: a
   composition-context resolver and a cross-session-awareness resolver. When **both** are
   needed, submit both to a **module-level** two-worker thread pool and harvest each with a
   10 s timeout. When only one is needed — the common case — run it **directly, with no pool
   at all**.
7. Apply results in a **fixed order: composition first, awareness second**, each separated by a
   blank line.
8. For non-utility sessions with a non-empty prompt, append a metadata tag:
   `"\n\nSent from <app> at YYYY-MM-DD hh:MM AM/PM"`, plus
   `" (transcribed from voice — may contain transcription errors)"` when the voice flag is set.
9. If the turn arrives over the remote-access tunnel, **prepend** the remote preamble block.
10. Map `thinking_level ∈ {low, medium, high, auto, max}` to the CLI's effort argument. `""`
    and `"none"` mean "model default" — pass nothing.
11. Start the session through the daemon.
12. **Emit `session_started` immediately**, so the client is not blocked, and *only then*
    perform composition-task linking, wrapped so a linking failure can never delay the start.

> **Spec consequence you must document to your own users:** the prompt the client sends is
> **not** the prompt the agent receives, and `cwd` and `system_prompt` are also
> server-mutated. Any test that asserts round-trip equality of the prompt will be wrong.

### 5.6.3 `get_session_log` — source selection and pagination

Source selection — *no merge, no fingerprinting; just pick the source that has more data*:

1. Always parse the on-disk transcript first.
2. If the daemon reports it has this session, fetch its in-memory entries and **replace** the
   transcript list if the daemon's list is strictly longer. The daemon holds the un-flushed
   current turn.
3. If the result is still empty, fall back to the daemon's entries (a brand-new session with
   no transcript yet).

> **Never use client-supplied state to make a server-side freshness decision.** An
> optimization once skipped the daemon call when the client passed an `is_working` hint. Send
> to session A, switch to B, switch back — the client's hint was stale, the server skipped the
> daemon, and returned old transcript data, **losing the new turn's entries from view.** Client
> state is *always* eventually stale during fast switching. The daemon is the source of truth
> for live entries.

Pagination branches:

| Branch | Response |
|---|---|
| `before` supplied | `end = min(before, total)`, `start = max(0, end − (limit or 50))`, `offset = start`, `has_more = start > 0`, **`prepend: true`** |
| `limit` supplied and `total > limit` | last `limit` entries, `offset = total − limit`, `has_more = offset > 0` |
| otherwise | all entries, `offset: 0`, `has_more: false` |

The default "load older" page size is **50**.

### 5.6.4 Server → client

| Event | Payload | Fires when | Recipients |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_snapshot` | `sessions[]` (full state dicts), `queues {sid: [text]}`, `aliases {old: new}` | on connect, on `request_state_snapshot`, and when a daemon IPC client attaches | requester for the first two; **broadcast** for the daemon-attach case, which omits `aliases` |
| `session_state` | `session_id, state, cost_usd, error, name, cwd, model, session_type, working_since` (0 unless working), `created_ts`, `tracked_files` (last 5), `substatus` (**always present**; `""` means cleared), `retry_at, retry_attempt, retry_max, retry_reason` (**always present**; `retry_at: 0` means none), `usage` (when truthy), `permission {tool_name, tool_input}` (only while waiting), `entry_count`, `parent_session_id` + `subsession_origin_turn` (when set), `inbox_dirty` (only when true), `auto_report_on_idle` (only when true), `queue` (when non-empty) | every state transition, plus a **deferred 3.0 s re-emit on going idle** | broadcast |
| `session_entry` | `session_id`, `entry {kind, text?, name?, desc?, id?, tool_use_id?, is_error?, timestamp}`, **`index`** | each new entry | broadcast |
| `session_permission` | `session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input` | tool permission needed; suppressed for utility sessions | broadcast |
| `session_started` | `session_id` | successful start | requester |
| `session_log` | `session_id, entries[], total, offset, has_more[, prepend]` | reply to `get_session_log` | requester |
| `session_model_result` | `ok, session_id, model[, error]` | reply to `set_session_model`. **The UI must update its model badge only on `ok: true`** — the daemon reports true only after the CLI confirmed the switch over its control protocol | requester |
| `session_usage` | `session_id`, `usage` | per-call token usage from the stream's message-start event — this is the **real context window size, not a cumulative total** | broadcast |
| `session_id_remapped` | `old_id`, `new_id` | the CLI/SDK reassigned the session id | broadcast; intercepted client-side to rewrite local maps |
| `session_renamed` | `session_id`, `title`, `project` | a title was **actually persisted** and is user-meaningful | broadcast |
| `sessions_refresh` | `{reason}` (e.g. `"scrub-phantoms"`) | after bulk mutations that invalidate the whole list | broadcast |
| `stream_event` | `session_id`, `event {event, data}` | raw streaming events; the client builds the live-typing bubble from content-block deltas | broadcast |
| `system_message` | `session_id`, `subtype`, `data` | unhandled daemon system messages, for debugging | broadcast |
| `message_ack` | `session_id[, queued: true]` | send accepted or auto-queued. **The key is absent when false**, not `false` | requester |
| `send_failed` | `session_id`, `error`, `text` | send failed; **returns the user's text** so the client can restore it inline instead of losing it | requester |
| `queue_updated` | `session_id`, `queue[]` | daemon queue mutation (broadcast) **or** reply to `get_queue` (requester) | mixed |
| `queue_dispatched` | `session_id`, `text`, `remaining` | a queued message was auto-dispatched | broadcast |
| `inbox_updated` | `parent_session_id`, `undelivered_count`, `from_child_session_id` [, `auto: true` on the daemon-initiated path] | a subsession report landed | broadcast |
| `daemon_reconnect` | `status` ∈ `disconnected` \| `connecting` \| `restarting` \| `connected`, `attempt`, `message` | four discrete points in the reconnect state machine; `restarting` at exactly attempt 5 | broadcast |
| `permission_policy_loaded` | `policy`, **`custom_rules`** (snake_case) | reply to the getter | requester |
| `ui_prefs_loaded` | arbitrary preferences object | reply to the getter | requester |
| `error` | `message` [, `session_id`] | **only** explicit validation or daemon failures | requester |
| `compose_context_updated`, `compose_changing` | `project_id`, `context` / `section_id` | the 4.0 s composition file-watcher poll | broadcast |

Two asymmetries that will bite an implementer who does not notice them:

- `set_permission_policy` takes **`customRules`** (camelCase) but
  `permission_policy_loaded` returns **`custom_rules`** (snake_case). Pick one in a clean-room
  build; if you inherit both, document it in the request/response schema, not in a comment.
- **`error` is not a catch-all.** There is no blanket try/except around handler bodies, so an
  unhandled exception inside a handler emits *nothing* and the client waits forever. Either
  wrap every handler and always reply, or accept that every handler must be individually
  total. Do not write documentation claiming "errors are emitted on any handler error" unless
  the wrapper actually exists.

### 5.6.5 Rooms, namespaces, and filtering

**There are none.** Everything runs on the default namespace with no rooms and no join/leave
protocol. State this explicitly in your own documentation, because it has consequences:

- Every daemon push is broadcast to **all** connected browsers regardless of which session or
  project each is viewing.
- Filtering is **client-side and display-level**: hide utility session types, hide any session
  id beginning with `_`, and hide sessions whose working directory does not match the active
  project.
- **Cross-project filtering must NOT happen at event ingress on the client.** Blocking events
  at that level breaks streaming for newly created sessions, whose working directory is not yet
  known locally.
- The only server-side scoping is project filtering of the **snapshot**, and there a session
  with **no working directory always passes**.
- The nearest analogue to a subscription is the client emitting `get_session_log` for the
  session it is displaying.

If you build this fresh and expect more than a handful of concurrent browsers, rooms are the
obvious upgrade — but implement the display-level filters *first*, because they also carry the
utility-session hiding rule, which rooms would not.

---

## 5.7 Reconnection semantics and what is NOT replayed

**Nothing is replayed. This is the single most important semantic in this part.**

The transport does not replay events missed during a disconnect. Every `session_entry`,
`session_state`, `stream_event`, `session_usage`, `session_permission`, and `queue_updated`
pushed during an outage is lost forever. There is a **second, deeper drop point**: the daemon
discards push events outright when no IPC client is attached — which is exactly the situation
during a web-tier restart.

Therefore the client must carry a compensation set. All of the following are load-bearing.

1. **Unconditionally re-emit `get_session_log` on every `connect`** when a live session is
   open: `{session_id, since: 0, limit: 100, project}`. This fires only on an actual
   reconnect, so it is cheap.
   *Incident:* a reconnect fetched policy and preferences but not the log, leaving stale
   entries on screen until a manual server restart.
2. **`request_state_snapshot` on connect, plus a 3 s retry** (in case the first was dropped
   because the daemon proxy had not itself reconnected yet), plus another **500 ms** after a
   `daemon_reconnect` with `status: "connected"`.
3. **Wake resync on `visibilitychange` / `pageshow` / `focus` / `online`, debounced 750 ms.**
   Strictly passive: reconnect only if the socket reports disconnected; otherwise emit
   `request_state_snapshot`. **It must never cycle a socket that reports connected.**
4. **Back/forward-cache reload.** On `pageshow` with `persisted === true`, do a full page
   reload, guarded off when an in-app restart overlay is present. The JS runtime was frozen
   and thawed with a dead transport; `disconnect() + connect()` cannot rebuild from corrupted
   transport state.
5. **Three-stage skeleton-stuck watchdog**, each stage firing only while the user is still
   looking at a stuck loading skeleton for the same live session:
   - **8 s** — re-emit `get_session_log`.
   - **16 s** — probe `/api/ping` over HTTP. If HTTP is healthy but the socket produced
     nothing, cycle the socket **at most once per 60 s**.
   - **28 s** — full page reload, **at most once per 120 s** (persist the timestamp in session
     storage), and guarded off when the restart overlay is present.
6. **Staleness stamping.** A `state_snapshot` must **skip** any session updated within the last
   **5000 ms**, so a late-arriving snapshot cannot revert fresher real-time data.
7. **Non-destructive re-fetch guards.** On a working→idle transition, re-fetch only if the DOM
   holds zero message elements. On idle/stopped, re-fetch only when the state's `entry_count`
   exceeds the count currently rendered. A blind re-fetch wipes the DOM and re-renders with
   pagination, slicing off the tail of the response the user just watched stream in.
8. **Disconnect indicator uses a 4000 ms grace timer**, because mobile network handoffs drop
   the socket and reconnect within 1–3 s and a flashing banner is worse than no banner.

### 5.7.1 The revert list — do not re-add these

Each of the following was implemented, shipped, and reverted because it caused a worse
regression than the bug it targeted.

- **Active client heartbeat (`client_ping` / `client_pong`).** See §5.2.3. Only revisit if
  (a) the pong is served by a path provably decoupled from IPC worker load, **and** (b) no
  socket cycle can chain into another within 60 s.
- **"Cycle the socket after the tab was backgrounded for N ms."** The timestamp variable was
  never reset after use, so once the tab had been backgrounded *once*, the computed background
  duration stayed enormous **forever** and every subsequent tap re-cycled the socket — dropping
  in-flight entry pushes ("the session stream got wrecked") and flooding the server with
  handshakes, each triggering a fresh all-states IPC call. If ever revived: reset the timestamp
  *inside* the resync after computing the duration, and impose a hard per-cycle rate limit.
- **A 20-second foreground zombie watchdog that cycled on event silence.** Idle sessions
  legitimately go 45 s+ between pushes. It fired on healthy-but-idle sockets and killed streams
  mid-response. Prefer an actively-emitted probe with a specific expected response over raw
  silence — subject to the heartbeat caveat above.
- **Calling wake-resync when opening the live panel.** Combined with the bug above it cycled
  the socket on every tap into a session.

> **The rule that emerged:** cycling a socket that reports `connected`, based on any heuristic,
> is a foot-gun. Cycle only on **proof** — a failed response to an actively-emitted probe, or a
> `disconnect` event from the transport itself.

### 5.7.2 Diagnosing future regressions

Log a distinctive prefix on every socket-lifecycle decision and every watchdog stage. When a
user reports "stale UI after being away," the presence of a "socket disconnected — forcing
reconnect" line near the incident means the recovery machinery ran; its absence means a
lifecycle binding was dropped. When a user reports "the stream cut off mid-response," search
for any `disconnect()` followed by `connect()` in the code path — that is almost always the
cause.

---

## 5.8 Cross-session awareness

**Purpose.** Build a ~300–400 token context block listing all *other* active sessions in the
same project — name, status, duration, recently edited files — and inject it into every new
session's system prompt so the agent can avoid stepping on a concurrent session's edits.

**Gate:** a config flag, default **on**.

**Algorithm** — `build_cross_session_context(daemon_proxy, project, current_session_id)`:

1. Fetch all states through the **cached** accessor (below). Return null on any exception or
   an empty list.
2. For each state, skip: itself; utility session types; any state not in
   `{working, idle, waiting}`; and any session whose working directory is set but does not
   match the active project.
3. Emit one line per surviving session:
   `- "<name>" [<status>, <duration>] — recent files: <basenames>`.
   Name defaults to `(unnamed)`. Duration formats as `<1m` / `Nm` / `NhMm` / `Nh`. Files are
   the **last 3 unique basenames**, taken in reverse (most-recent-first) order, or
   `(no file edits yet)`.
4. Cap at **12** sessions; if capped, append `(+N more)`.
5. **Return null when there are no qualifying sessions** — deliberately, so an empty block is
   never injected as noise.

**Template body.** Five numbered conflict rules, stated as instructions to the agent:
re-read files another session touched before editing them; on unexpected import or signature
errors, **back off rather than fight a mid-refactor**; if part of the task cannot be completed,
finish everything else and surface the incomplete part under a clearly-marked "not completed —
potential conflict" heading; keep edits surgical; and **do not attempt to coordinate with or
message other sessions** (there is no channel, and attempts to invent one waste turns).

**Caching rule — mandatory.** Cache the all-states fetch with a **2.0 s TTL** behind a lock.

- *Why:* this runs on **every** session start, and the fetch is a blocking IPC round-trip that
  serializes all session state — 20–100 ms per call under load. With 5–10 concurrent starts,
  each start triggers its own round-trip and the entire worker pool serializes.
- *Why staleness is acceptable:* the data is advisory, injected once at creation, and sessions
  run for minutes or hours.
- **The IPC call must run OUTSIDE the lock.** Hold the lock only around the dictionary
  read/write. Otherwise cache-hit threads block behind whichever thread happened to miss.
  Reproduce this exactly.
- Pin the TTL's existence with a structural test.

---

## 5.9 Automatic session titling

**Public contract:** `smart_title(messages) -> str`. Always returns a non-empty string. Never
raises. Fully synchronous, on the request thread. **No locks, no threads, no caching, no
in-flight de-duplication, no retries, no backoff inside the titling module** — all of that
belongs to the route, the persistence layer, and the client.

### 5.9.1 Input selection

Extract up to **5** user texts, each truncated to **300** characters, feeding all four
strategies. Iterate in order; keep only `role == "user"` entries that are not tool results;
clean each; drop trivial and system-junk items.

- **Cleaning:** strip paired and self-closing XML-ish tags up to 60 characters; strip
  continuation preambles; strip the boilerplate headings a hand-off summary emits; strip
  read-tool line-number prefixes; strip block-comment fences; normalize whitespace.
- **Trivial:** two words or fewer, every word in a ~48-entry stop set (`yes`, `ok`, `thanks`,
  `continue`, `the`, `a`, …).
- **System junk** — five detectors, applied **only to the first 500 characters**, because long
  pasted content produced false positives on arrow characters: agent-catalog markers; a
  "you have … agent" phrasing; five known continuation prefixes; more than two `→`
  characters; or length over 500 with no `?` in the head and more than 20 special characters
  from `{}()[];=><|&^~\`$@`.

### 5.9.2 Four-strategy chain, cheapest-correct first

| # | Strategy | Requirement | Model | Bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Daemon-spawned utility session | daemon proxy connected | cheapest/fastest model alias | **12 s** (60 polls × 0.2 s) |
| 2 | Direct API call | API key present and SDK importable | pinned small model, `max_tokens = 30` | SDK default |
| 3 | CLI shell-out | agent CLI on PATH | small-model flag | **20 s** subprocess timeout |
| 4 | Heuristic | none | none | instant |

Worst case when everything degrades: ~12 s + one API attempt + ~20 s. That is acceptable
because titling is asynchronous from the user's point of view and the heuristic always
produces something.

### 5.9.3 Prompt strategy

One shared system prompt: *"You generate very short titles for coding chat sessions. Rules:
3–4 words MAX, describe the core task, use words from the messages, never include file paths
or URLs."* Then **five few-shot pairs** drawn from the coding-assistant domain (review git
changes; debug idle state; frontend polish pass; test suite gaps; fix 502 errors). Close with
*"Reply with ONLY the title, nothing else."* The user message is the extracted texts as a
bulleted list.

Per-path deltas:

- The **daemon** path appends *"IMPORTANT: Do NOT use any tools. Just reply with the title text
  directly."* — the agent runtime wraps the model in tool-using agent behavior and it will
  otherwise start exploring the repository to write a title.
- The **CLI** path has no system channel, so concatenate the system prompt, a
  `"Here are the user messages:"` line, and the block.

### 5.9.4 The daemon titling path in detail

Spawn a session id of the form `_title_<8 hex>` with the system working directory,
`max_turns = 1`, the small model, **no allowed tools**, plan permission mode, session type
`title`, and **low reasoning effort**.

> **Low effort is load-bearing.** Without it the CLI enables extended thinking by default, and
> the API **silently upgrades the small model to a larger one** (the small model does not
> support extended thinking) — producing a slow, expensive, verbose response that fails title
> validation. This is also why the old "titles are always under 5 KB" cleanup heuristic had to
> be removed.

Compute the encoded system-project name **once at spawn time**, so cleanup targets the right
directory even if the user switches projects mid-flight.

Poll `get_session_state` **first** (cheaper than fetching entries), accepting either a bare
string or a dict. Terminal states are `idle` and `stopped`. On completion or timeout: fetch
entries, extract the title, remove the session, delete its transcript.

**Title extraction from entries**, per assistant entry, in order: (a) validate the whole text;
(b) validate each line after stripping `#`, `*`, `-`; (c) if a line matches a numbered-list
prefix, **peel the number and validate the remainder**. Step (c) rescues real titles from
list-shaped responses while a bare numbered line stays rejected.

### 5.9.5 Validation and sanitization

Normalize first: trim, strip surrounding quotes, strip trailing periods. Then reject on:

| Check | Threshold |
|---|---|
| length | empty, ≤2 chars, or ≥80 chars |
| single word | fewer than 2 words |
| too many words | more than 8 words (the prompt asked for 3–4; longer means an instruction-style response) |
| all caps | uppercase and longer than 4 chars |
| numbered list | matches `^\s*\d+[.)]\s` |
| instruction prefix | matches `^\s*(title\|here'?s a title\|the title is\|suggested title)\s*[:\-]` |
| prompt echo | contains any of nine phrases: `generate a title`, `coding chat session`, `very short title`, `the format you showed`, `following the format`, `<paste>`, `<example>`, `your title`, `your session` |
| markdown emphasis | contains `**` **and** the word "title" or "session" **and** at least two `**` runs |
| no overlap | no title word longer than 3 characters appears in the joined lowercased source text (an empty word set returns valid — you cannot check overlap for very-short-word titles) |

**Every one of these corresponds to an observed phantom-title shape that polluted the stored
names file in production.** The markdown-emphasis rule is the exact shape of a bug that
produced 169 phantom rows across five projects, discovered only when a user scrubbed them by
hand. **Maintenance rule: prefer adding a tight, observed pattern over a broad heuristic.**

### 5.9.6 Heuristic fallback

`to_title(text, max_chars=55)`: strip URLs and paths → fix dangling prepositions → strip ~21
question/request prefixes → strip ~25 action-verb fluff phrases ("take a look at", "figure
out", "make sure that", …) → strip leftover leading punctuation → loop leading-filler removal
up to 3 times with early exit → strip code-comment prefixes → truncate at the **earliest** of
15 clause separators found within the first 120 characters → **if fewer than 2 words remain,
return the empty string** (the "stripping ate everything" signal) → cap at `max_chars` on a
word boundary → capitalize the first character only.

The heuristic title takes the first text through that pipeline. If the result is under 12
characters and a second text exists, compute a 45-character runner from it and join with an
em-dash unless it is already a substring. If still empty, use the raw first text (URLs
stripped, 55-character cap). Last resort: **`"Untitled Session"`** — a load-bearing sentinel
that the persistence layer **must refuse to save**.

### 5.9.7 When titling fires, and the do-not-re-title rules

`POST /api/autoname/<sid>`:

1. **Hard skip:** an existing entry in the stored-names file →
   `{ok: true, title: <existing>, skipped: true, reason: "User-set name preserved"}` with **no
   model call at all**.
2. Input: the request body's `prompt` if present (this enables naming *before* any transcript
   exists), else the transcript. If neither, scan every non-internal project directory. 404 if
   still absent.
3. Raw-transcript rescue: use the first queued-operation record with content, or the first user
   record with a text block.
4. A genuinely empty session gets `"Empty Session (N)"`, appended to the transcript only and
   **never written to the names file**.
5. `re_evaluate` with an unchanged title →
   `{skipped: true, reason: "Title unchanged"}`, nothing written.
6. Otherwise generate the title.
7. **Phantom-prevention gate**, two skip cases: (a) the title is the `"Untitled Session"`
   sentinel; (b) the session has **no transcript on disk AND the daemon does not know it** —
   an autoname driven by a fresh prompt for a session that may be abandoned before flush.
8. Writes: append a custom-title record to the transcript **with de-duplication** (read the
   most recent custom-title record first; without this, one production session accumulated
   **52 identical title lines**, which corrupted sorting). Read the file **backwards in
   8192-byte chunks** so this is O(rename history), not O(file size). Then, only if the gate
   passed, persist the name and emit `session_renamed`.

**`session_renamed` contract.** Emit a *targeted* rename event, never a full-list refresh —
autoname fires often and a list reload per name change is a broadcast storm. **Callers must
emit it only after a title was actually persisted and is user-meaningful.** Never for skipped,
unchanged, or placeholder cases.

**Client trigger schedule** (this is the part that determines cost):

- On send: immediate, silent, carrying the prompt text.
- On board-driven session creation.
- **+1500 ms** after a session leaves the working state (lets the transcript flush).
- An untitled sweep on **every 15th poll (~30 s)**.
- **+3000 ms** after a session-id remap.
- Explicit menu/toolbar action.
- Bulk "auto-name all" at **concurrency 2**.

**Per-session hard cap: 2 attempts.** If it did not work twice, the heuristic fallback has
already run — stop spawning processes. Check the "user has named this" set **twice** — before
the request and again when it returns — so a rename landing mid-flight discards the auto-name.

### 5.9.8 Cleaning up after titling

Daemon-spawned title sessions persist a transcript under the **system utility project**, never
the active project. Passing the active project here was the original bug and made cleanup
silently miss the file. Three cleanup strategies, in order: (1) the spawn-time session id;
(2) the proxy's in-process id-alias map; (3) a **content scan** — read each transcript, parse
the first line, and match the title system-prompt signature. Then tombstone every id cleaned.
**Do not size-cap the scan** (see §5.9.4 — responses can be multi-KB).

---

## 5.10 Search indexing

### 5.10.1 Role and storage

The index answers three questions: *where did we decide X* (full-text), *which session touched
file Y* (lookup table), and *which sessions hit this error* (tool output is indexed).

- Store at a **user-level path outside the repository** so it can never be committed, and
  compute that path **lazily on every call** so a test that redirects the home directory gets an
  isolated database for free.
- SQLite with write-ahead logging and an explicit schema version.
- **The index is disposable.** Any database error → delete the file and rebuild from the
  transcripts, which are the source of truth. An unrecognized schema version also rebuilds —
  *rebuild rather than guess*.

### 5.10.2 Schema

```
indexed_files(project, session_id, mtime REAL, size INTEGER,
              PRIMARY KEY(project, session_id))

session_files(project, session_id,
              file_path,   -- as recorded in the tool input
              norm_path,   -- lowercased, forward-slash form, for matching
              PRIMARY KEY(project, session_id, norm_path))

messages  -- full-text virtual table
  content                       -- the only indexed column
  project, session_id, role, ts, msg_idx   -- all unindexed
  tokenizer: unicode61
```

### 5.10.3 What is indexed

Extraction must mirror the normal transcript loader exactly. Keep records of type `user` and
`assistant`. Content may be a string or a list of blocks, where:

- text blocks append their text;
- tool-use blocks contribute **no searchable text**, but when the tool name is one of the
  file-writing tools, record the input's file path into the file map;
- tool-result blocks append their text **capped at 4000 characters per block** — tool output
  can be megabytes, and errors appear early;
- thinking blocks are ignored.

Blank and corrupt lines are skipped silently. An OS error reading the whole file yields an
empty result; the next pass removes its rows.

**"Touched" means edited.** Read-only access is deliberately *not* recorded, matching the
daemon's tracked-files semantics.

### 5.10.4 Incremental indexing

`ensure_index(project, force=False)`:

1. No-op on an empty project.
2. Hold the write lock for the whole pass.
3. **Debounce: 20 s per project on a monotonic clock**, seeded so a never-indexed project
   always proceeds. Results may lag disk by up to 20 s — an accepted trade so search-as-you-type
   never re-stats the directory per keystroke.
4. Run the pass; on a database error, delete and retry **once**.
5. Record the timestamp *after* the work, not before.

The pass itself: glob transcripts, skipping underscore-prefixed stems (the same exclusion the
session lister uses — which is also why utility title sessions never enter the index); `stat()`
each, skipping files deleted between glob and stat. **Staleness detection is an (mtime, size)
signature comparison, not hashing.** Compute `changed` (signature differs or absent) and
`removed` (indexed but gone). **Early-exit when both sets are empty** — that is the common
case, and it is what makes the TTL cheap. Otherwise one explicit transaction: delete rows for
removed + changed from all three tables, re-extract and bulk-insert the changed ones, commit,
and log the counts.

Acknowledged cost: deleting from the full-text table by an unindexed column scans the table.
Measured fine at ~15k messages per project; revisit only if you exceed that by an order of
magnitude.

**There is no separate full-rebuild entry point.** Full rebuild is emergent: delete the
database, the indexed-files table is empty, everything is "changed."

**Scope limit:** indexing only ever runs inside a search request, in the web process. Never in
the daemon, never on a per-turn hot path. No watcher, no scheduler, no background thread. It
must be called from exactly one place.

### 5.10.5 Query semantics

Build the match expression by whitespace-splitting the query; per token, double internal quote
characters per the full-text engine's escaping rules and strip user-supplied wildcards; skip
empties; wrap each token as a **quoted phrase**; give **only the last token** a trailing
wildcard (prefix match for search-as-you-type); join with spaces (implicit AND). An empty
result raises a validation error → 400.

> **Design intent: each token becomes a quoted phrase so user input can never be parsed as
> query syntax.** Boolean operators, proximity operators, and parentheses are treated as
> literal text. This is the injection defense; do not "improve" it by passing raw input
> through.

Ranking is the engine's raw relevance score (lower is better). A session's rank is the score
of its best-ranked matching message. No column weights, no recency boost, no aggregation.

Three modes:

- **query only** — full-text, over-fetch `LIMIT max(200, limit × 10)` message rows, group by
  session in relevance order.
- **query + file** — build the file map first, then **intersect**.
- **file only** — no full-text; sessions ordered by indexed mtime **descending**, `rank: 0`,
  empty snippets.

File filtering uses a case- and separator-insensitive `LIKE` with an explicit escape character;
escape `\`, `%`, and `_` in the user's value.

**There is no date filter.** The timestamp is stored but never appears in a filter.

Grouping: create a new session bucket only while the bucket count is under `limit`, but let
existing buckets keep accumulating up to **3 snippets** each. Snippets come from the engine's
snippet function with **12** context tokens, an ellipsis separator, and **non-HTML delimiters**
around the hit.

> **The client must convert those delimiters to markup only AFTER HTML-escaping the snippet
> text.** Preserve that ordering or raw transcript content can inject markup into the results
> pane.

**Exclusions are applied at query time, not index time:** deleted ids, utility ids, and
remapped ids are filtered out of results. *Tombstones change without touching the transcript's
mtime, so an index-time filter would keep serving a session the user just deleted.*

`stats` counts are **pre-exclusion index totals** for the project, not result counts, and the
reported elapsed time excludes the ensure-index pass the route runs first. Results carry no
title, preview, or timestamp — the client joins on session id against the session list it
already has.

### 5.10.6 Self-healing and concurrency

Wrap the search in a retry for the one corruption case the ensure-pass cannot see: damage
localized to full-text pages that a no-change pass (which only reads the indexed-files table)
never touches. Without this, **every search would return 500 until some transcript's mtime
happened to change.** Re-raise validation errors (→ 400); on a database error, delete under the
lock, force a rebuild, and retry once.

**Close the connection before re-raising a database error** — on Windows an open handle blocks
the unlink the rebuild path needs to perform. Tolerate OS errors when deleting the database
files, with a warning.

One lock guards **writes only**; reads take no lock, because write-ahead logging lets searches
read while another request indexes. Fresh connection per operation, closed in a `finally`. No
pool, no cross-thread connection sharing, **no threads created**.

## 5.11 Authentication and auth-status checking

### 5.11.1 Application-level authentication: none

State this in your API documentation in plain words: *authentication is none; this is a
localhost-only development tool; all endpoints are available without credentials.* No
decorator, no token, no session cookie, no CSRF. The only trust boundary is the loopback bind.

**That assumption is deliberately broken by the remote-access feature.** An unauthenticated
`POST /api/mobile/enable` publishes the entire console — including restart, shutdown, the test
runner, the browser bridge, and the watchdog GET — onto the user's private overlay network
over HTTPS. The only access control at that point is overlay-network membership; there is no
application-level token and no per-device pairing.

> **Clean-room recommendation:** this is precisely where an auth layer belongs. At minimum:
> a per-device pairing token stored server-side, required on every request whose `Host` is the
> tunnel hostname, plus signing on the watchdog deep link (§5.5.12).

### 5.11.2 Agent CLI auth

`GET /api/auth-status` shells out to the CLI's status command with a **10 s timeout** and no
console window, then parses stdout as JSON and returns it verbatim. **The return code is never
checked** — success is defined solely as "stdout parsed as JSON."

**Failure UX is deliberately flattened.** Every failure mode — CLI absent, not on PATH, the
10 s timeout, non-JSON stdout, malformed JSON, non-zero exit — collapses into the same
**HTTP 200** body `{"loggedIn": false, "error": "<text>"}`. The client therefore cannot
distinguish "definitely logged out" from "we could not tell," and that is intentional: a broken
CLI renders as "logged out, here's why" and the UI shows a login prompt rather than an error
state the user cannot act on.

Resolve the CLI binary path **once at import**. Consequence: installing the CLI after boot is
not picked up until restart. (This is exactly why the launcher's PATH augmentation, §5.3.2
step 4, exists.)

`POST /api/auth-login` must open a **visible** terminal so the user can complete the OAuth
flow: on Windows a console with the login command; on macOS a scripted Terminal invocation; on
Linux, try **11** emulators in popularity order (`x-terminal-emulator, gnome-terminal, konsole,
xfce4-terminal, tilix, mate-terminal, lxterminal, alacritty, kitty, wezterm, xterm`), each with
its own argument convention, and 500 if none is found. Any platform outside those three
branches returns `{ok: true}` without launching anything.

### 5.11.3 Client-side blocker overlays

Implement a small pluggable registry: `registerHealthCheck(id, {label, icon, message, test,
action})`. Poll every **3 s while blocked, 10 s while healthy**. The **first failing check by
registration order** wins the overlay. **Registration order is load-bearing** — register in the
order below.

| Check | Test | Threshold | Failure UX |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wifi` | server-reachable **OR** internet-reachable | probe a well-known 204 endpoint with a no-CORS HEAD; browser `online`/`offline` events are **hints to re-probe, never authoritative** | "No Internet Connection" |
| `server-reachable` | `/api/ping` every **3 s** | **4** consecutive failures | "Server Unreachable", with guidance that sessions are likely safe inside the daemon and a pointer to the server log. **A 503 (the reviver announcing takeover) must reload immediately with no threshold; a 502 or connection-refused must NOT reload** — reloading lands on the tunnel's script-less error page and strands a phone |
| `daemon-reachable` | `/api/health`'s `daemon` field, every 5 s | **5** consecutive failures (~25 s) | "Engine Stopped" blocking overlay with a restart button |
| `claude-auth` | `/api/auth-status`'s `loggedIn`, every **30 s** (5 s while blocking) | first negative poll | "Not Logged In" plus an action that POSTs the login endpoint |

Server reachability **implies** internet reachability, which suppresses false positives during
overlay-network reconnection where the public probe is slow but the local ping works. The
daemon threshold was raised from 3 to 5 because mobile handoffs and phone-lock wake windows
clipped the shorter window and produced false "Engine Stopped" overlays.

Every foreground transition (`visibilitychange`, `pageshow`, `focus`, `online`) must run a
**decisive single-probe** check — no single lifecycle event fires reliably across mobile
Safari, mobile Chrome, and installed web apps. The daemon's decisive check uses a **two-probe
pattern with a ~1.5 s retry** to absorb transient network hiccups. **All checks must bail when
an in-app restart overlay is present** so they never fight a restart the user initiated.

### 5.11.4 Permission policy (tool approval)

Persisted by the daemon. Allowed policy values — **defined in exactly one place and re-imported
by the WebSocket validator** — are `manual`, `auto`, `almost_always`, `claude_auto`, `custom`.
Per-tool custom rules accompany `custom`.

The approval flow is **hook-driven, not SDK-callback-driven** (the SDK's tool-permission
callback does not work with current CLI versions):

```
Agent CLI PreToolUse hook
  → a standalone stdlib-only hook script
     reads {tool_name, tool_input, session_id} from stdin
     POSTs to the web tier's hook endpoint (socket timeout 3600 s)
     6 retries, exponential backoff 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 s
  → web tier hook handler
     3 retries, fixed 1 s sleep, on daemon IPC error
  → daemon proxy call (IPC timeout 3600 s)
  → daemon: mint a request id, set state WAITING,
     emit session_state + session_permission, wait up to 3600 s
  → user answers over the socket (permission_response)
  → daemon returns {"action": "allow" | "deny"}
  → hook script prints {"decision":"block","reason":…} and exits 2
                    or {"decision":"allow"} and exits 0
```

**Fail-open is the deliberate global policy at both layers.** Unparseable stdin, exhausted
retries, an IPC error, or a missing `action` key all yield *allow*. Only an explicit
server-side deny blocks. The rationale: a broken approval path that blocks every tool call
makes the product unusable and looks like a hang; a broken path that allows behaves like the
"auto" policy the user could have chosen anyway.

**Session targeting fallback** — the only session-matching logic on this surface: the hook
fires for *any* agent session, so if the reported session id is not tracked, adopt the first
session in the WORKING state; the end-of-tool handler mirrors that on the first WAITING
session.

> **Known constraint to fix in a clean-room build:** the hook script hardcodes the web port
> rather than reading it from config or environment. A non-default web port breaks the hook —
> it fails open on every tool call after ~15 s of retries, which the user experiences as
> "everything is slow and permission prompts stopped appearing." Pass the port to the hook
> script when you install it.

The watchdog bridge (§5.5.12) forces the policy to `manual` **and** passes a default permission
mode — belt and braces, because policy is global-only and this is the only mechanism that
guarantees a WAITING state regardless of the operator's prior setting.

## 5.12 Configuration file: full schema and caching rules

### 5.12.1 Application config

Path: `<repo-root>/app-config.json`, overridable by an environment variable (used by tests).
**Gitignored** — it can carry third-party service credentials. Missing keys are always filled
from defaults, so callers see the full set.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `board_backend` | str | `"sqlite"` | local file store vs. hosted store |
| `backend_url` | str | `""` | hosted store URL (secret-bearing) |
| `backend_secret_key` | str | `""` | |
| `backend_publishable_key` | str | `""` | |
| `board_depth_limit` | int | `5` | max subtask nesting |
| `project_id_aliases` | obj | (absent) | `{local_encoded: remote_encoded}` — **task-board routes only**; sessions, git, and file paths keep the real locally-derived id |
| `browser_launch_mode` | str | **`"tab"`** | `tab` \| `app` (§5.13) |
| `auto_start_on_session` | bool | `true` | starting a session moves its task to Working |
| `auto_parent_working` | bool | `true` | child Working promotes a Not-Started parent |
| `auto_parent_reopen` | bool | `true` | child Remediating reopens a Complete parent |
| `auto_advance_to_validating` | bool | `false` | all children done → Validating |
| `ai_can_modify_status` | bool | `true` | the agent may change task statuses |
| `ai_can_mark_complete` | bool | `true` | the agent may mark tasks complete |
| `cross_session_awareness` | bool | `true` | inject the awareness block (§5.8) |
| `wrong_session_detection` | bool | `true` | warn when a prompt looks off-topic for the session |
| `validation_url_enabled` | bool | `false` | |
| `validation_base_url` | str | `""` | |
| `validation_url_dismissed` | bool | `false` | |
| `file_tracking_enabled` | bool | `true` | per-turn mtime snapshots powering undo/rewind; disable to speed up very large repositories |
| `large_session_media_eviction` | bool | `true` | master switch for lossless stale-media eviction — runs only in the pre-resume pass, never per turn; externalizes old inline images to a content-addressed store and replaces them in the replayed transcript with a text placeholder |
| `large_session_media_keep_recent_turns` | int | `4` | how many recent user turns keep their images inline |
| `large_session_dedup_recent_tooluseresult` | bool | `true` | also externalize the redundant base64 duplicate inside the recent-turn window |
| `remote_access_enabled` | bool | `false` | overlay-network bridge on/off |
| `remote_access_port` | int | `5050` | |
| `remote_access_device_name` | str | (absent) | home-screen label, ≤40 chars; empty removes the key, falling back to the short hostname and then the product name |

**Caching rule — mandatory.** Cache the parsed config with a **10.0 s TTL** on a monotonic
clock. Saving must invalidate the cache immediately so writes are visible at once.
**The getter must return a shallow copy**, because callers mutate what they receive; without
the copy they corrupt the cache in place. This getter is called on every session start and from
many routes; the cache eliminates a file read and JSON parse per call. Pin the TTL with a
structural test asserting it is at least 10 seconds.

### 5.12.2 Agent CLI settings file

Exposed via `GET/PUT /api/config`. **Whole-file replace, not a patch.** GET returns the object
verbatim (`{}` when the file is absent) and **500s on invalid JSON without overwriting** — the
browser mirror must skip its PUT on this 500, so a corrupt file stays intact for the user to
repair. PUT writes atomically (temp file, then replace) and requires a JSON **object** at the
top level.

The browser mirrors single keys via a **GET → merge → PUT** cycle. A partial PUT would wipe the
user's other settings. Pin this with a test that sets one key and asserts the others survive.

### 5.12.3 UI preferences file (daemon-owned)

One writer (the daemon), many readers. A retention setting must be one of a fixed choice set
(30, 60, 90, and a "forever" sentinel like 36500 days); an invalid value drops **only that
key**. Reject booleans explicitly — in most languages `bool` passes an `int` type check.

The web tier reads this file **directly, not over IPC**, so trash pruning still works when the
daemon is down and no round-trip is needed per trash operation.

> **Safety rule, load-bearing.** Every path that resolves retention must treat a missing key,
> a non-integer, a boolean, a non-positive number, or an unreadable file as **Forever — never
> as the shortest retention.** Time-based deletion of a user's work must require a deliberate
> user selection. A defaulting bug here destroys data silently.

### 5.12.4 Per-project folder tree

Stored per project at a user-level path, exposed via `GET/PUT /api/folder-tree`. With no active
project, glob the per-project files and take the first, else a default filename. GET returns
**200 `{}`** on corrupt JSON — **deliberately unlike the settings endpoint** — so a corrupt
tree never bricks the file panel. PUT is atomic; use the replace primitive that overwrites an
existing destination (plain rename fails on Windows when the destination exists).

### 5.12.5 Confirmed-models cache

`{model_id: display_name}`, grown as sessions run; the session layer records a model on each
session-init message.

> **Trap:** the CLI reports a bracketed suffix when an extended context window is active (for
> example `model-name[1m]`), and the SDK **rejects bracketed model ids** — which surfaces in
> the UI as "model not available." The recorder must strip a `\[[^\]]*\]` suffix and hard-gate
> the remainder on a strict model-id pattern before persisting.

`/api/models` composes: the persistent cache ∪ a provider API listing (8 s timeout) ∪ a CLI
probe (20 s) ∪ an always-offer list ∪ a family fallback ∪ a hardcoded known-models list.
De-duplicate by display name keeping the first (the shortest, cleanest id). Emit **exactly one**
`default: true`, chosen as: CLI-detected default → first mid-tier model → first entry, with a
family preference order.

**The endpoint must answer from cache in under a millisecond.** Refresh on a background thread
with a 3600 s TTL; on cold start set the cache timestamp to 0 to force an immediate background
refresh. Run the API and CLI probes in a two-worker pool. Sequential fetching on the request
thread costs **up to 28 s of blocking** — the model picker would hang the UI on first open.

---

## 5.13 Consequential decisions

| Decision | What we chose | Why | What breaks if you choose differently |
|---|---|---|---|
| Process split | Separate web and daemon processes | Sessions must survive UI restarts; the web tier is the part that changes and restarts most | A single process means every code change or crash kills every running session; users lose in-flight agent work |
| Async model | Threading mode, one thread per handler, no event loop | Lets the whole codebase use blocking libraries (subprocess, blocking IPC, synchronous browser automation) with no colored-function split | An async model forces every blocking call into an executor; a partial migration produces event-loop stalls that look exactly like the IPC congestion incident |
| Broker | None; single web process, direct in-process broadcast | A local single-user tool; a broker is pure operational cost | Multiple web workers silently break broadcast — background threads emit into a process no client is attached to |
| Rooms / namespaces | None; broadcast everything, filter on the client | Simplest correct thing at 1–3 browsers; and event-ingress filtering provably breaks streaming for brand-new sessions whose cwd is not yet known | Ingress filtering drops the first entries of every new session. Rooms are a fine upgrade *later*, but keep the display-level filters — they also carry utility-session hiding |
| Replay | None; no server-side event buffer | Buffering per-client state means tracking per-socket state, which nothing else in this design does | Without the client compensation set (§5.7) users see permanently stale panels after any network blip |
| Liveness probe | HTTP `/api/ping`, side-effect free | Must not be starved by IPC latency | A WebSocket heartbeat on the shared worker pool cascades into socket cycling → reconnect storms → daemon IPC congestion → false "engine stopped" overlays |
| Permission approval | CLI hook + HTTP callback, fail-open | The SDK's tool-permission callback does not work with current CLI versions | Fail-closed turns any broken link in the chain into "every tool call blocks forever," which users read as a hang |
| Auth-status failure shape | Always HTTP 200 with `loggedIn:false` and an error string | The UI should show an actionable login prompt, not a red error state | A 500 makes a missing CLI look like a server bug, and the health-check registry cannot distinguish it from a dead server |
| Config caching | 10 s TTL, shallow-copy on read, invalidate on save | Read on every session start and from many routes | No cache = file read + parse per call; no copy = callers mutate and corrupt the cache; no invalidation = the settings UI appears not to save |
| Awareness caching | 2 s TTL, **IPC outside the lock** | Runs on every session start; the fetch is a blocking round-trip serializing all state | No cache: 5–10 concurrent starts serialize the entire worker pool. IPC inside the lock: cache hits queue behind the one thread doing IPC |
| Search index | SQLite full-text, incremental by (mtime, size), rebuilt on any corruption | The transcripts are the source of truth, so the index is disposable and never needs migration | Treating the index as precious means writing migrations for a cache, and one corrupt page 500s every search until a transcript happens to change |
| Search query building | Every token becomes a quoted phrase; only the last gets a prefix wildcard | User input can never be parsed as query syntax | Raw pass-through lets a stray parenthesis or boolean keyword produce confusing errors — and is an injection surface into the query engine |
| Snippet markup | Non-HTML delimiters, converted to markup **after** escaping | Transcript content is attacker-influenced text | Escaping after conversion, or emitting HTML delimiters from the database, lets transcript content inject markup into the results pane |
| Titling chain | Daemon → API → CLI → heuristic, heuristic always available | Titles must always exist; quality is a bonus | A single LLM path means sessions sit untitled whenever the model path is unavailable, and the sidebar becomes a wall of UUIDs |
| Title validation | A long list of tight, *observed* rejection patterns | Every rule maps to a real phantom-title shape seen in production | Broad heuristics reject good titles; no validation lets instruction-shaped model output become permanent session names |
| Browser launch | Chrome-first on all three platforms; default to a tab in the user's own profile, isolated app window opt-in | The voice input API is Chromium-only; the system default browser may be a non-Chromium browser and voice then fails with **no error message at all** | Falling back to the system opener alone silently breaks voice. An unconditional isolated window wedges the user's browser focus state; an unconditional bare URL gets swallowed by session restore on a cold start |
| Third-party browser bridge headless | Always headed, real browser channel, automation-detection flag disabled; the `headless` parameter is accepted and **ignored** | Measured: bundled browser → blocked; real browser headless → blocked; real browser headed → passes | Honoring `headless` reintroduces a bot-detection block that presents as a mysterious hang |
| Remote access transport | Overlay-network HTTPS proxy to loopback, tunnel-only (never a public funnel) | HTTPS is needed for the **secure context** (microphone), not for privacy — the overlay already encrypts | A public tunnel exposes an unauthenticated console to the internet |
| Restart scope | Endpoint defaults to web-only and sets a preserve flag | The daemon holds all live sessions | Defaulting to "both" means any restart destroys every running session |

---

## 5.14 Non-negotiable rules

Each rule states the failure mode if violated. Numbers are stable references; cite them in code
comments.

1. **The daemon-state cache TTL is 2.0 s, and the IPC call runs outside the lock.**
   *Failure mode:* every session start performs a blocking round-trip serializing all session
   state (20–100 ms under load); 5–10 concurrent starts serialize the whole worker pool. Holding
   the lock across the IPC additionally blocks every cache-hit thread behind the one miss.
2. **The application-config cache TTL is 10.0 s, invalidated on save, and the getter returns a
   shallow copy.**
   *Failure mode:* a file read plus JSON parse on every session start and many routes; without
   the copy, callers that mutate the result corrupt the cache for every subsequent reader;
   without invalidation, the settings UI appears not to save for up to 10 s.
3. **The compose/awareness setup thread pool is module-level, two workers, and is bypassed
   entirely when only one resolver is needed.**
   *Failure mode:* sequential resolution adds **~200 ms** per composition-backed session start;
   creating a pool per request costs more than the parallelization saves.
4. **Startup cleanups (orphaned system sessions, title-only stubs) run exactly once at boot and
   never on a request path.**
   *Failure mode:* a full multi-project directory scan lands on the sidebar hot path. Pin this
   with a test asserting the cleanup function name does not appear in the session-lister's
   source.
5. **Use a dedicated entry-count call, never `len(get_entries(sid))`.**
   *Failure mode:* counting via the entry list serializes **all** entries over IPC just to
   count them — measured **25–32 ms for 300 entries** versus **0–1 ms**.
6. **The parsed-entry cache is keyed by (session id → mtime, size, entries), capped at 200
   with FIFO eviction, and partial/tail reads must NEVER populate it.**
   *Failure mode:* re-parsing a whole transcript on every log fetch; and a cached truncated
   list is later served as if complete, silently hiding messages.
7. **The search-index ensure pass is debounced at 20 s per project on a monotonic clock.**
   *Failure mode:* every keystroke re-stats the entire project directory. Accepted trade:
   results may lag disk by up to 20 s.
8. **The search-index lock guards writes only; reads rely on write-ahead logging.**
   *Failure mode:* taking it on reads serializes every search behind indexing for no benefit.
9. **Session-name and access-timestamp files are cached per project and invalidated on mtime
   change.**
   *Failure mode:* re-read and re-parse per session inside the sidebar render loop.
10. **The session-summary cache is keyed by (path, mtime, size) and access timestamps are
    deliberately NOT part of the key — so the access overlay must be applied on every call
    including cache hits, returning a shallow copy.**
    *Failure mode:* a full transcript re-parse per sidebar row; or, if you mutate the cached
    dict to apply the overlay, the cache accumulates stale access data.
11. **Session summaries parse in parallel only when summary-only and there are more than 10
    files** (worker count `min(16, n)`); otherwise serial.
    *Failure mode:* serial parsing of hundreds of transcripts blocks the session-list endpoint;
    unconditional pooling costs more than it saves for small projects.
12. **The models endpoint answers from a 3600 s cache in under a millisecond; refresh happens
    on a background thread with a two-worker probe pool.**
    *Failure mode:* a sequential provider-API (8 s) plus CLI (20 s) fetch means **up to 28 s of
    blocking on the request thread** and a model picker that hangs the UI.
13. **The agent-catalog path cache is invalidated by all four asset-mutation endpoints.**
    *Failure mode:* a stale catalog file is handed to new sessions, or the catalog is rewritten
    on every request.
14. **The local skill/agent scan is cached per project keyed on max mtime, with bounded child
    depth (2), bounded find depth (4), and a skip-directory set.**
    *Failure mode:* a deep filesystem walk per request.
15. **Reading the latest custom-title record scans the transcript backwards in 8192-byte
    chunks.**
    *Failure mode:* an O(file size) scan of multi-megabyte transcripts on every rename and every
    autoname.
16. **`/api/ping` must be side-effect free and must never be replaced by a heavier endpoint for
    reachability checking.**
    *Failure mode:* if the reachability probe does anything slow (such as the auth endpoint's
    10 s CLI shell-out), it produces false "server unreachable" overlays on a perfectly healthy
    server.
17. **`/api/health` reports the daemon flag from cached connection state, never a round-trip.**
    *Failure mode:* a round-trip makes the health check lie — it hangs or times out exactly when
    the daemon is the thing that is broken.
18. **The console log handler must be attached to both the routes namespace and the
    daemon-client namespace, in the same iterable.**
    *Failure mode:* nothing crashes; the operator silently loses all IPC latency logging. Pin
    with a test that asserts both literals **and** that they sit in the same bracketed tuple, so
    a rename cannot drop one while leaving a reassuring comment.
19. **The daemon proxy uses a dedicated emitter thread draining a queue.**
    *Failure mode:* a slow broadcast emit (WebSocket backpressure) blocks the reader loop and
    delays every IPC request and response in the process.
20. **Connect without resync, then resync from a background thread once the reader is running.**
    *Failure mode:* resyncing first blocks **30 s** waiting for a response nobody will deliver,
    and blocks application construction — the product fails to boot.
21. **Search over-fetches `max(200, limit × 10)` message rows before grouping by session.**
    *Failure mode:* grouping under-fills the requested result count whenever one session
    dominates the matches.
22. **Git refresh has a 45 s minimum interval.**
    *Failure mode:* a network fetch on every poll.
23. **Phantom scrubs are serialized with a non-blocking lock returning 429.**
    *Failure mode:* two concurrent scrubs race the same names file and one overwrites the
    other's result.
24. **The test-run lock is held through process spawn.**
    *Failure mode:* two simultaneous requests both observe "nothing running" and both spawn a
    test process.
25. **The composition file watcher polls at 4.0 s.**
    *Failure mode:* tighter polling burns CPU for a feature nobody is watching; looser feels
    broken.
26. **Client watchdog rate limits: socket cycle at most 1 per 60 s; page reload at most 1 per
    120 s (persisted in session storage).**
    *Failure mode:* without these, the documented cycle storm recurs — chained reconnect
    handshakes, each firing an all-states IPC call, cascading into false "engine stopped"
    overlays.
27. **The client's session-id membership structure is a set kept in sync with the session list
    at every mutation site.**
    *Failure mode:* replacing set membership with a linear scan makes an O(n) check run inside
    render loops.
28. **Never use client-supplied state to decide server-side data freshness.**
    *Failure mode:* during fast session switching the client's state is stale; the server
    skipped the daemon check and returned old transcript data, losing the just-sent turn's
    entries from the user's view.
29. **`close_session` errors whose text is exactly "session not found" must be swallowed.**
    *Failure mode:* the client emits close unconditionally so a stop is authoritative even when
    its local running-set is stale, which makes this reply the *common* case; surfacing it
    toasts an error on every stop of an already-dormant session.
30. **User-stop intent must be recorded before emitting `close_session` at every explicit stop
    path, and ghost-recovery timers must check it twice — once on fire, once inside the
    close→start gap — with a 60 s TTL backstop.**
    *Failure mode:* client-side ghost recovery re-starts the session and re-sends the last
    prompt; "sleep" does not stick and the session comes back awake, having re-run the user's
    work. Do **not** "simplify" by cancelling recovery on the stopped state — a genuinely dead
    session also reports stopped, and that is exactly the case recovery exists to repair. The
    discriminator is the **cause**, not the state.
31. **`session_renamed` may be emitted only after a title was actually persisted and is
    user-meaningful.**
    *Failure mode:* autoname fires on a schedule; emitting for skipped, unchanged, or
    placeholder cases produces a broadcast storm and re-renders the sidebar constantly.
32. **Never persist the "Untitled Session" sentinel, and never persist a title for a session
    with no transcript that the daemon does not know.**
    *Failure mode:* phantom rows accumulate in the names file — 169 of them across five projects
    in one observed incident — each rendering as a name the user never chose and cannot easily
    find to remove.
33. **De-duplicate custom-title records before appending.**
    *Failure mode:* one production session accumulated 52 identical title lines, which corrupted
    session sorting.
34. **Search snippets carry non-HTML delimiters and the client converts them to markup only
    after escaping.**
    *Failure mode:* transcript content injects markup into the search results pane.
35. **Search exclusions (deleted / utility / remapped) are applied at query time, never at index
    time.**
    *Failure mode:* tombstones do not change a transcript's mtime, so an index-time filter keeps
    serving a session the user just deleted until something unrelated touches the file.
36. **Every file endpoint is gated to the user's home directory (403 outside), and every session
    id is shape-validated before it is composed into a filesystem path.**
    *Failure mode:* directory traversal out of the sessions directory and arbitrary file
    read/write across the machine.
37. **The delete pipeline order is: close the session synchronously → guard against signalling
    pid ≤ 1 or our own pid → capture the user-set name → write the tombstone **first** → move to
    trash (hard-delete with retries, truncate to zero bytes as the absolute last resort) → force
    an immediate registry save.**
    *Failure mode:* a still-running agent process recreates the transcript after deletion; a
    signal to pid 0 broadcasts to the entire process group, which on Linux **includes the
    daemon**; a tombstone written last lets the session reappear; and recovery resurrects a
    session the user deleted.
38. **Unlink with retries (5 × 0.2 s) and log a warning on exhaustion.**
    *Failure mode:* on Windows, antivirus holds the transcript handle for tens to hundreds of
    milliseconds after the process dies; a single silent retry produced **zero-byte transcript
    files** left on disk.
39. **The tombstone reader is strictly write-free, and pruning keeps entries whose transcript
    still exists past the TTL.**
    *Failure mode:* a reader that also pruned-and-saved raced the writer and overwrote a fresh
    tombstone — **the deleted session reappeared on the next page load**. And a
    still-locked zombie file becomes visible again.
40. **Sidebar sort must not take the max of the effective timestamp and file mtime, and opening
    or previewing a session must not bump its access timestamp.**
    *Failure mode:* the agent appends untimestamped state records in the background, bumping
    mtime with no user interaction — one incident clustered 7 sessions at the same minute and
    pushed the user's actually-recent conversation **9 positions down**. Access timestamps must
    be bumped by exactly two hooks (send-message and start-session) so sessions move only when
    the user does work in them.
41. **Every retention-resolution path treats missing / non-integer / boolean / non-positive /
    unreadable values as Forever, never as the shortest retention.**
    *Failure mode:* silent time-based deletion of a user's session history.
42. **The restart endpoint defaults to web-only scope and sets the preserve-daemon flag;
    restarts launch the bootstrap script (so the splash shows), resolve ports from the
    environment, use a new process session on the outer spawn, redirect to a log file rather
    than the null device, and `export` environment variables *before* invoking `nohup` rather
    than using command-prefix syntax.**
    *Failure mode:* each one of these was a real, separately-diagnosed bug. Without the new
    process session, the replacement process's port kill propagates back through the shared
    process group and kills the spawning shell **before** it finishes spawning the replacement.
    The command-prefix form is not valid with `nohup` — the shell passes `VAR=value` as the
    first argument and `nohup` tries to execute a file by that literal name, which **silently
    broke every Linux web restart**, leaving the user with no web server at all.
43. **Singleton lock names must include the port.**
    *Failure mode:* every test and side-by-side instance fails the singleton check because the
    production instance holds the lock — which manifests as unrelated features appearing broken.
44. **The early-boot shim is the first import, before any third-party module.**
    *Failure mode:* a third-party import triggers a platform-identification query; a wedged OS
    management service then freezes boot indefinitely, and the splash blames the wrong step.
45. **The daemon spawn passes an explicit environment dictionary.**
    *Failure mode:* the WSGI environ filter strips the daemon port variable on the restart path,
    so a restarted web tier spawns a daemon on the wrong port.
46. **Static assets get no-store; `text/html` gets `no-cache, must-revalidate`.**
    *Failure mode:* mobile Safari and installed web apps serve cached HTML pointing at stale
    cache-busted asset URLs, so fixes never reach the device even though the version query
    changed.
47. **Chrome-first browser launch on all three platforms, with the running-state branch:
    already-running → bare URL (new tab); cold start → new-window flag.**
    *Failure mode:* the system default opener alone silently disables voice input with no error
    message (already shipped to users once). An unconditional new-window wedges the browser's
    focus state so windows opened from outside the app silently no-op until the browser is fully
    restarted. An unconditional bare URL gets swallowed by session restore on a cold start.
    Bias the running-state detector to "running" on failure: a wrong "yes" costs one reopened
    shortcut, a wrong "no" wedges focus.
48. **Add a proximity meta-guard:** a test that parses the working diff and **warns** (never
    fails) when a changed line sits within 5 lines of a performance-critical marker comment, plus
    a test that **fails** if the markers themselves disappear — otherwise the guard has nothing
    to protect.

Paste these to a coding agent in order. Each is self-contained and ends with acceptance
criteria. Do not skip ahead — later prompts assume the seams built by earlier ones.

```text
5. Write a STATIC parity test: scan route and handler source for `proxy.<method>` call sites;
```

```text
PROMPT 5.3 — IPC client and live state

Build the daemon proxy and the live-state routes.

1. Newline-delimited JSON over loopback TCP with TCP_NODELAY: request / response / error /

   3600 s.
2. Threads, started in this order: connect WITHOUT resync -> reader -> emitter -> heartbeat
   (20 s interval, 8 s timeout) -> deferred resync on a background thread.
3. Framing and disconnect correctness: decode only up to the LAST newline in the byte buffer;
   the reader snapshots its socket and marks disconnected only if that snapshot is still
   current; force-disconnect calls shutdown(SHUT_RDWR) before close(); enable TCP keepalive
   tuned to roughly 30 s total.
4. Reconnect loop: 2 s retries, emitting a broadcast progress event with statuses
   disconnected / connecting / restarting / connected plus attempt and message; respawn the
   daemon at exactly attempt 5.
5. Routes: GET /api/live/state/<sid> using a dedicated entry-COUNT call (never the length of a
   fetched entry list), and GET /api/session-log/<sid>.
6. Cross-session awareness: the full algorithm from §5.8 with a 2.0 s cached all-states
   accessor whose IPC call runs OUTSIDE the lock.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test that splits a multi-byte character across two simulated recv() calls does not raise a
  decode error.
- A test that reconnects while a stale reader is finishing does not leave the client marked
  disconnected.
- A structural test asserts the awareness TTL constant exists and is <= 2.0, and that the IPC
  call site is outside the lock block.
- /api/live/state for an unmanaged session returns 200 with state "stopped", managed false,
  entry_count 0 — never a 404.
```
