**Staggering by index is the house style:** skeleton rows at `i × 0.06s`, chat skeleton lines at `delay + line × 0.04s`, agent pills at `index × 0.06s`. It costs nothing and makes lists feel authored rather than dumped.

**Accessibility gap you must fix.** In the reference implementation, reduced-motion handling exists only inside the mobile stylesheet and only under the mobile breakpoint. **That is a genuine defect.** Honor `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` **globally**, at minimum disabling every ambient loop (working gradient, wait pulse, shimmer, blocker pulse) and every entrance animation. Similarly, inputs use `outline: none` plus a border-color change on focus; **replace that with a real `:focus-visible` ring.** Do not inherit these two gaps.

### 7.14.9 Polish details

- **Scrollbars:** 8px wide (6px inside the transcript log), transparent track, themed thumb at r4 (r2 in the log), a lighter thumb on hover.
- **Glass:** backdrop blur plus saturation appears on exactly two components (the primary modal at 40px/1.6, the grid card at 12px/1.4), always with a vendor-prefixed twin. Restraint is what keeps it feeling premium.
- **Layered shadows:** the primary card uses a large soft drop shadow **plus** a 1px white inset ring as a second shadow layer; the grid card adds a subtle inset top highlight.
- **Resize affordances** always pair a 1px visible element with an invisible wider hit area (a pseudo-element with negative insets), and set the body cursor and disable user-select for the duration of the drag. *Failure mode without the latter: dragging selects text across the whole page.*
- A subtle hairline rule beneath the load-more button so the pagination boundary reads as a section break.

### 7.14.10 Responsive layer

**One breakpoint: 768px**, loaded as a separate stylesheet *after* the main one. It is explicitly **not a separate UI** — same DOM, same scripts, same realtime connection.

At the breakpoint: the header shrinks to a 52px single row with shortened labels injected via generated content; a drilled-in state hides the wordmark and reserves space for the drawer opener; the resize handle is hidden; **the sidebar becomes a full-viewport fixed drawer** that slides via a horizontal transform over 280ms.

**The drawer's most instructive bug:** the desktop collapsed rule sets `width: 0 !important` and hides the children. On mobile that **silently defeats the transform transition** — the width snaps to zero and the children vanish, so there is nothing left on screen for the transform to animate. The drawer just disappears, which users described as "sudden." **The mobile layer must re-assert full width on the collapsed state and explicitly restore the children's display**, so they slide out *with* the drawer. One CSS override fixes every collapse path at once — session tap, new session, view change, backdrop tap, close button — with no script changes. When an animation "doesn't play," check whether something removed the thing being animated.

Other mobile adaptations: a 46px close-button touch target with a 26px icon; the long-press hint becomes visible (there is no right-click on touch); Enter never sends; no autofocus on session open; blur on send; the context menu becomes a bottom sheet; and **the visual-viewport resize event is used to scroll a programmatically focused composer above the keyboard.** That last one is subtle: **a scripted focus does not trigger the browser's native "reveal the field" pass** — that only fires on the first keystroke, which is the "the input doesn't move into view until I start typing" bug. You must reproduce the reveal yourself, and only *after* the viewport resize fires, because at focus time the keyboard is not up yet and there is nothing to scroll past.

### 7.14.11 Embed mode

An `?embed=1` parameter adds a body class, and a small dedicated stylesheet hides exactly the controls that would either navigate away from the pinned project or perform publishing actions from inside a host UI: the project switcher, the view switcher, the project overlay, and the version-control buttons. A `?chrome=1` parameter restores them for debugging. The script that pins the embedded project must load **before** the main script, because it shims the persisted-project read that the main script performs during boot.

## 7.15 Consequential decisions

| Decision | What we chose | Why | What breaks if you choose differently |
|---|---|---|---|
| Framework | None; globals + `innerHTML` | Zero boot cost, trivially debuggable, no build step | You inherit our entire bug class: lost typed text, lost focus, blanked panels, destroyed static children, duplicated timers. **Recommendation: choose a reconciler.** |
| State ownership | One owner, one write path, one resolver per concept | The alternative produced a value stored in six places and derived by four disagreeing chains | The UI shows one value while the system uses another, and a choice made for one entity leaks into the next |
| Optimistic updates | Render before confirmation, reconcile by position/id | Perceived latency is the product | Reconciling by text content silently eats legitimate duplicate messages |
| Re-fetch policy | Never blind; gate on "DOM empty" or "server has more" | A re-fetch mid-stream is destructive | Already-streamed content is wiped and the response's tail is sliced off — invisible data loss |
| Socket recovery | Only cycle on *proof* of breakage | Every heuristic we tried manufactured the outage it claimed to detect | Cycle storms, dropped in-flight streams, backend IPC congestion, spurious engine-down overlays |
| Stop semantics | Intent registry keyed on *cause*, not state | A dead session and a slept session look identical | Either sleep does not stick, or genuinely dead sessions never recover |
| Health probe endpoint | A trivial, side-effect-free ping | A heavier endpoint can stall on an external process | False "server unreachable" overlays during normal operation |
| 502 vs 503 | Reload only on 503 | 503 means a supervisor has taken the port; 502 means nobody has | Reloading on 502 lands on a JavaScript-less proxy error page and strands mobile users with no controls |
| Foreground detection | Bind all four lifecycle events + a decisive immediate probe | Timers freeze when backgrounded; no single event fires reliably everywhere | Recovery takes ~12s of foreground polling, or never triggers on some platforms |
| Auto-scroll | One entry point, with a 150ms programmatic-scroll exclusion | Multiple scroll call sites stomp each other | Auto-scroll silently disables itself, or the user's own message is hidden behind the previous reply |
| Composer re-render | State-key memo + hard guards for voice and focus | State events arrive constantly | Typed text vanishes mid-sentence; voice capture is destroyed and the message is dropped |
| Autofocus | Only on a deliberate user action; never on mobile | Focus reopens the on-screen keyboard | The keyboard flails open and closed on every state tick, and covers the session the user just opened |
| Queue authority | Server-authoritative, client cache | Queued work must survive a refresh | A refresh loses queued messages; snapshot reconciliation wipes cross-project queues |
| Cross-project isolation | Generation counter on every async continuation | Retrofitting isolation produced half the guards in this codebase | Slow responses for the old project overwrite the new project's state |
| Sort behavior on open | Sort-neutral | Order should reflect work, not navigation | The clicked session yanks to the top of the list under the user's cursor |
| Border color | Translucent accent, not gray | Gives every edge a faint brand cast | The UI reads as a generic dark-mode dashboard |
| Content width | 760px, shared by log and composer | Makes the transcript read as a document | A stretched terminal; and if the two values drift, visible misalignment |
| Reduced motion | (Ours is mobile-only — a defect) | — | **Fix this: honor it globally, or the app is hostile to motion-sensitive users** |

---

## 7.16 Non-negotiable rules

1. **Apply the theme synchronously before first paint, from persisted storage.**
   *Failure mode if violated: a flash of the wrong theme on every cold load, which users read as a broken app.*

2. **Never blind-re-fetch the session log.** All three re-fetch call sites and the response handler must gate on "the DOM is empty" or "the server genuinely has more entries than are rendered."
   *Failure mode if violated: already-streamed content is wiped and re-rendered through pagination, slicing the tail off the response the user just watched appear. Silent data loss.*

3. **Re-request the session log on every reconnect when a session is mounted.**
   *Failure mode if violated: the transport does not replay, so every entry pushed during the outage is lost forever — "skeleton forever" and "stale entries, nothing new."*

4. **Never cycle a socket that reports connected without proof it is broken.** Proof means an independent-channel success while the realtime channel produced nothing, or a disconnect event from the transport itself.
   *Failure mode if violated: dropped in-flight streams (responses cut off mid-sentence), reconnect handshake storms, backend IPC congestion, and spurious engine-down overlays caused by your own recovery code.*

5. **Every automatic recovery mechanism must be triggered by a user-visible symptom, escalate cheapest-first, and be rate-limited.**
   *Failure mode if violated: recovery fires on healthy-but-idle systems and chains across user interactions into a storm.*

6. **Mark user-stop intent BEFORE emitting the stop, at every stop entry point, and check it twice inside the recovery path.**
   *Failure mode if violated: sleeping a session within ~3 seconds of sending silently revives it and re-sends the last prompt. The server looks innocent, so this is nearly undebuggable from logs.*

7. **Always ask the server to stop a session; never gate the stop on client-side "is it running" state.**
   *Failure mode if violated: Stop is a client-side no-op for sessions tracked through any secondary path, the session keeps running, and the next refresh shows it idle again.*

8. **The composer must never be rebuilt while voice capture is active, and must preserve typed text and focus across every rebuild.**
   *Failure mode if violated: the recognition target is destroyed mid-sentence and the dictated message is dropped, every time.*

9. **State-driven re-renders must never take focus. Mobile must never autofocus at all.**
   *Failure mode if violated: the on-screen keyboard opens and closes on every state tick and covers the session the user just opened.*

10. **Reconcile optimistic bubbles positionally, never by text content.**
    *Failure mode if violated: legitimate repeated messages ("yes", "ok", "continue") are silently eaten.*

11. **Clear the composer before dispatching, not after.**
    *Failure mode if violated: key repeat double-submits the message.*

12. **Auto-scroll has exactly one entry point, with a ~150ms exclusion window around programmatic scrolls, and only top-aligns a fallback target when nothing newer follows it.**
    *Failure mode if violated: auto-scroll permanently disables itself, and sending a message hides the user's own bubble behind the previous reply.*

13. **Extract embedded preview markers before truncation and before markdown parsing.**
    *Failure mode if violated: markers render as raw JSON and get sliced mid-marker into unparseable garbage.*

14. **Never clear a parent container whose static children other code resolves by id — clear only the dynamic child region.**
    *Failure mode if violated: the view's initializer writes to null references and the panel renders blank while the API returns valid data. This shipped twice.*

15. **Every async continuation must carry a generation guard, and list fetches must be abortable.**
    *Failure mode if violated: a slow response for the previous project overwrites the current project's state — cross-project data bleed.*

16. **The periodic resync must carry the active project explicitly.**
    *Failure mode if violated: the server falls back to a global active project, filters out the current project's idle sessions, and demotes them to sleeping until a manual refresh.*

17. **Reconcile queues only for the sessions a snapshot actually reports on.**
    *Failure mode if violated: queued messages on sessions outside the current project vanish, repeatedly, as the user navigates.*

18. **Distinguish 502 from 503 in the server health check: reload only on 503.**
    *Failure mode if violated: reloading on 502 lands on a JavaScript-less proxy error page and strands the device with no controls.*

19. **Bind foreground detection to all four lifecycle events and run a decisive immediate probe with exactly one retry.**
    *Failure mode if violated: mobile timers are frozen while backgrounded, so thresholded polling needs ~12 seconds of foreground time to notice a dead server — or never fires at all on some platforms.*

20. **The health blocker and the restart overlay sit above everything and must be mutually aware; every reload path bails when the restart overlay exists.**
    *Failure mode if violated: two recovery mechanisms fight, reload each other, and neither completes.*

21. **Reset the message watchdog on streaming data (do not cancel it), and only after the session-id match check.**
    *Failure mode if violated: a long response leaves no safety net for a lost final idle event; or entries under a stale alias reset the watchdog without rendering, permanently defeating recovery while appearing healthy.*

22. **Keep the id-mirror set in sync with the session list at every mutation site, and never replace a set lookup with a linear scan.**
    *Failure mode if violated: the entry handler performs a linear scan of the session list on every streaming token — thousands of scans per response.*

23. **Use history replacement, not a push, for id-remap URL rewrites.**
    *Failure mode if violated: temporary client-generated ids linger in browser history and break back / forward / refresh.*

24. **Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` globally and provide real focus-visible rings.**
    *Failure mode if violated: the app is actively hostile to motion-sensitive users and unusable by keyboard.*

25. **Keep the diagnostic surface: consistent console prefixes per subsystem, and performance marks for submit→first-entry and switch→rendered.**
    *Failure mode if violated: every future latency or "it got stuck" report is unfalsifiable and you debug by guessing.*

## 7.17 Implementation prompts

Build in this order. Each prompt assumes the previous ones are complete.

```
PROMPT 7.1 — Foundations: tokens, theming, primitives, state discipline

Build the design foundation before any feature.

1. Define the CSS custom-property token system: surfaces, text, borders, accents,
   semantic colors, and effects. Declare the dark theme on the document root and
   override it wholesale with a light-theme attribute selector. Use translucent
   accent color for all four border weights — not gray. Add a sentinel token that
   exists only to prove the stylesheet loaded. Add theme-aware neutral tint tokens
   (white-alpha in dark, black-alpha in light) so hover states need no per-theme
   override at call sites.
2. Add a synchronous inline script in <head> that reads the persisted theme
   preference and sets the theme attribute BEFORE any stylesheet-dependent paint.
   Support dark / light / auto; in auto mode read cached sunrise/sunset minute
   values from local storage, falling back to a 7am-7pm window.
3. Implement the typography scale, spacing scale, and radius table. Use a system
   sans stack for UI, one display font used ONLY for the wordmark and the health
   blocker, and a monospace stack for the transcript container and code. Set
   tabular numerals on every ticking counter.
4. Build primitives: toast (bottom-anchored, 3s, error variant), promise-returning
   confirm/alert/prompt, spinner, shimmer skeleton, and the health-blocker overlay
   shell (unkillable, top of the z-index ladder).
5. Publish the z-index ladder as a documented constant table.
6. Write down the state-ownership discipline before writing features: for every
   piece of state, name one owner, one write path, and derive all rendering from a
   single resolver.

Acceptance criteria:
- No component hard-codes a color; every color reads a token.
- Toggling the theme repaints the entire app with no per-component overrides.
- A cold load in either theme shows no flash of the wrong theme.
- prefers-reduced-motion:reduce is honored globally, disabling ambient loops and
  entrance animations.
- Inputs show a visible :focus-visible ring.
```

```
PROMPT 7.2 — The shell: views, view switching, projects

1. Build the header (logo, system dropdown, action buttons, theme cycle), the

- Switching projects twice rapidly never renders data from the wrong project.
- Reloading in any view shows that view's skeleton first, never another view's.
- A view switch preserves the realtime connection, drafts, sort mode, and per-project
  view/session memory.
- Tearing down a view never clears a parent container holding statically declared
  children; only the dynamic child region is cleared.
- The view flyout can be opened and closed on a touch device.
```

```
PROMPT 7.4 — The realtime client

Build this BEFORE the chat panel; the chat panel is downstream of it.

   on every project switch and on every connect.
2. Implement the full event catalogue. On connect: cancel the disconnect-flash

   session log if a session is mounted.

   showing a failure indicator.
4. Snapshot reconciliation, in order: capture generation and time; rebuild the
   working-since map from scratch; skip any session with a state update newer than
   5 seconds ago; detect working→non-working for the mounted session but re-fetch
   ONLY if the DOM has no messages; preserve optimistic working state for
   just-started in-scope sessions; apply a FINAL generation guard before committing;
   inject stub rows; re-apply row-state classes AFTER the list filter; reconcile
   queues ONLY for the sessions the snapshot reports on.

   auto-resuming substatus which persists into idle. Preserve an optimistic
   compaction substatus until the authoritative event, unless the server explicitly
   sends an empty one. Track retry as an absolute epoch timestamp, not a duration.

   entry arrives for a session believed idle; heal id aliases in both directions;
   reset the watchdog ONLY AFTER the id match check.

   history REPLACEMENT for the URL, record the alias, and re-schedule any pending

10. Add performance marks for submit→first-entry and switch→rendered, and consistent

Acceptance criteria:
- Killing the network for 60 seconds and restoring it results in a complete,
  correct transcript with no manual refresh.
- A snapshot arriving during a project switch is discarded entirely.
- A queued message on a session in another project survives navigating between

- An id remap leaves no temporary id in browser history.
```

```
PROMPT 7.7 — Resilience: health checks, ghost recovery, stop intent, socket recovery

Build this LAST, against a working app, so you can observe real failure modes.

1. Health-check registry: registration order determines overlay priority; first
   failing check wins; 3s default cadence, 1s while blocking, 10s while healthy;
   a throwing test counts as failing; mutate overlay DOM only when the failing
   check's identity changes.
2. Implement four checks in this registration order:
   a. Internet — our own server's reachability is the PRIMARY signal; an external
      probe is only a tie-breaker. 10s cadence, 3s while blocking. Browser
      online/offline events are hints to re-probe, never authoritative.
   b. Server reachable — probe a trivial side-effect-free endpoint. 200 = healthy;
      503 = reload IMMEDIATELY with no threshold; 502/other/refused = show the
      overlay after 4 consecutive failures but NEVER reload. Add a decisive
      foreground probe with exactly one retry ~1.2s later.
   c. Daemon reachable — registered after (b). 5 failures at 5s. Same decisive
      foreground pattern. Include a restart action button that polls health until
      recovery with a 90s ceiling. Clear instantly on the realtime reconnect event.
   d. Authentication — assume healthy until the first poll says otherwise; 5s while
      blocking, 30s while healthy.
3. Bind foreground detection to visibilitychange, pageshow, focus, AND online.
4. Restart overlay: two phases, sniff the returned HTML for a supervisor sentinel
   and refuse to reload onto it. Its presence in the DOM is a global mutex — every
   reload path and every decisive probe must bail when it exists.
5. Ghost recovery AND the user-stop intent registry MUST ship in the same commit.
   Ghost recovery: 3s with no state event → close, then 1.5s later → resuming start.
   Intent registry: mark/clear/check with a 60s TTL, reachable from every module.
   Mark intent BEFORE emitting any stop, at EVERY stop/sleep/delete entry point.
   Check intent twice in each ghost path — once when the 3s timer fires and again
   inside the 1.5s gap — plus once in the send-error fallback that matches
   "not found" or "is stopped". Clear intent on any explicit send.
6. Never gate a stop emit on client-side running state; always ask the server, and
   clear restore-across-restart memory for stopped sessions.
7. Socket recovery — implement ONLY these four mechanisms:
   a. Full page reload on a persisted pageshow (guarded by the restart overlay).
   b. Unconditional log re-request on connect.
   c. Three-stage skeleton watchdog: 8s re-request; 16s HTTP probe and cycle ONCE
      only if HTTP succeeds while the realtime channel produced nothing (max 1 cycle
      per 60s); 28s full reload (max 1 per 120s, skipped if the restart overlay
      exists). Every stage requires the symptom to still be visible for that exact
      session. Clear the timers before the mounted-session guard in the response
      handler.
   d. Passive wake resync on visibilitychange/pageshow/focus/online, debounced 750ms,
      which only reconnects a disconnected socket or requests a snapshot — and NEVER
      cycles a connected socket.
   Add a 4s grace period before showing a disconnected indicator.
   DO NOT add: a backgrounded-duration cycle heuristic, a staleness-based zombie
   watchdog, a wake-resync call on session mount, or a client heartbeat. Read
   section 7.10.3 for why each one failed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backgrounding the app for 10 minutes and returning produces a correct, live UI
  with no manual refresh and no truncated in-flight response.
- Sleeping a session within 1 second of sending it a message keeps it slept, and the
  prompt is not re-sent.
- Killing the daemon while the web server survives shows the engine overlay within
  ~25 seconds, and within ~1.5 seconds if the user foregrounds the tab.
- A 502 never triggers a reload; a 503 triggers one immediately.
- No code path in the app calls disconnect-then-connect except skeleton stage 2.
```

# Part 8 — The Workflow Board

> **Reading this chapter.** The Workflow Board is the largest single feature in the product and the one users spend most of their day inside. Everything in it derives from one idea, stated in §8.1. If you internalise that idea, the rest of the chapter reads as consequences. If you skim §8.1 and start at the data model, you will build a Trello clone and the product will be worthless.
>
> Terms used throughout, defined once here:
> - **Session** — a long-running, stateful conversation with an AI coding agent, executing inside a project working directory, with tool access to the filesystem and shell. Sessions are managed by a separate process (the *daemon*, Part 4) and stream events to the browser over WebSocket. A session has a lifecycle state: `working`, `idle`, `stopped`, `question`.
> - **Project** — one filesystem directory that sessions run against. Identified by an opaque `project_id` string derived from its absolute path.
> - **Task** — a persisted unit of intended work. Rendered as a **card**.
> - **Board** / **Workflow view** — the column-per-status surface that renders tasks.
> - **Drill-down** — the full-screen detail view for a single task, which replaces the board.

---

## 8.1 The core concept: cards that launch and mirror real sessions

**A card is not a note about work. A card is a launcher and a status mirror for real running processes.**

This is the entire thesis. In a conventional Kanban tool, a card is inert text; a human reads it, goes elsewhere to do the work, comes back and drags the card. Here, the card *is* the control surface:

- **Launcher.** Every leaf card carries a one-click **Execute** action. Clicking it creates a real AI session in the project directory, injects a context block describing the task, its ancestors, its siblings, and what other sessions are currently doing, auto-submits a prompt, and navigates the user into the live chat. Time from "I want this done" to "an agent is doing it" is one click.
- **Status mirror.** Once a session is linked to a task, the session's lifecycle pushes the card around the board. Session starts → the card moves to Working. Session goes idle with no siblings outstanding → the card may advance to Validating. The card shows a live green dot while its session is thinking.
- **Two-way, but asymmetric.** Sessions push status onto tasks. Tasks **never** push lifecycle onto sessions. No status transition ever starts, stops, sleeps, or kills a session. This asymmetry is deliberate and is a non-negotiable rule (§8.13).

Three consequences fall out immediately, and each shapes a later section:

1. **Only leaves are executable.** A parent task is a container; executing it is meaningless because the concrete work lives in its children. The UI must refuse to execute a task with children, loudly, with an explanation.
2. **The state machine must tolerate both actors.** A human dragging a card and a daemon event arriving 200 ms later are both legitimate writers of `status`. The design resolves this by making the transition graph *binding on the AI and on automatic transitions*, and *advisory for the human* (§8.3.2).
3. **The board must stay live without thrashing.** Sessions emit events constantly. A naive "re-render on every event" board flickers, drops drag operations, and destroys open panels. §8.10 and §8.11 are about the guard discipline that makes this survivable.

The board is the only view in the product that closes the full loop:

| Stage | Board affordance |
|---|---|
| Intent | "Plan with AI" — describe a goal in prose |
| Decomposition | An AI planner returns a nested task tree; the human reviews and accepts |
| Execution | Execute / Execute + Validate on a leaf card |
| Parallelism | Multi-select leaf subtasks → batch-launch up to 20 sessions with cross-awareness injected |
| Supervision | Cards show live session status; agents move their own cards via output markers |
| Validation | A ceremony modal: review the verification URL and subtask checklist, then Approve or Reject-with-issues |
| Record | Per-task status history plus a live analytics dashboard over the transition log |

Every other view in the application is a view onto **sessions**. The board is the only view onto **work**.

---

## 8.2 Data model

### 8.2.1 Storage architecture

- **Repository pattern behind an interface.** Define one abstract repository with a complete method surface, then implement it at least once (embedded SQL database in the app data directory). A second cloud implementation (Postgres via a REST gateway) is optional and should be built **last** — it is the highest-risk, lowest-value part of the system.
- **Synchronous throughout.** The web tier runs threaded, not on an event loop. Do not introduce async in this layer; you will end up bridging it everywhere.
- **No `projects` table.** A project is an opaque `project_id: TEXT` denormalised onto `tasks` and `board_columns`, derived from the project's absolute path with `/ \ : _` mapped to `-`. All projects share one database. There is no foreign key.
- **IDs are UUID4 strings generated in application code, never by the database.** This is what makes a backend migration a pure data copy.
- **All timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 strings.** Store as TEXT on an embedded DB, TIMESTAMPTZ on Postgres. *Warning:* the two render the same instant differently on read. Normalise on hydration or you will get subtle sort bugs after a migration.
- **`updated_at` is bumped by hand on every write path.** There is no DB trigger. Every mutation must set it. Forgetting is the single most common source of "the Last-updated sort is wrong" bugs.

### 8.2.2 `tasks` — the central entity

| Field | Type | Null | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT PK | no | — | UUID4, app-generated |
| `project_id` | TEXT | no | — | Denormalised project scope |
| `parent_id` | TEXT | **yes** | NULL | Self-FK → `tasks(id)` ON DELETE CASCADE. NULL = root. Arbitrary depth. |
| `position` | INTEGER | no | 0 | Gap-numbered sort key. See §8.2.8 for scoping. |
| `title` | TEXT | no | — | Card headline. Empty is a 400. |
| `description` | TEXT | yes | NULL | Rich text (HTML from the editor) |
| `verification_url` | TEXT | yes | NULL | URL or file path a human opens to validate the work |
| `status` | TEXT | no | `not_started` | One of the five enum values |
| `owner` | TEXT | yes | NULL | Free-text assignee, set by claim/unclaim |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | — | ISO UTC |
| `updated_at` | TEXT | no | — | ISO UTC |

**Indexes:** `(project_id)`, `(parent_id)`, `(project_id, status)`, `(project_id, status, position)`, `(owner)`.

**`depth` is not a column.** It is derived at read time in application code from the flat task list. Do not store it; do not compute it by walking the parent chain per row (§8.11).

**Include `owner` in the INSERT.** In the original it was on the object, indexed, and read back — but no create path ever wrote it, so a task created with an owner silently came back unowned. Write it.

### 8.2.3 `board_columns` — column configuration

| Field | Type | Null | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT PK | no | — | UUID4 |
| `project_id` | TEXT | no | — | Owning project |
| `name` | TEXT | no | — | Display label |
| `status_key` | TEXT | no | — | The `tasks.status` value this column collects. Join key, not an FK. |
| `position` | INTEGER | no | 0 | Left-to-right order. **Dense small integers 0..N, not gap-numbered** — unlike tasks. |
| `color` | TEXT | yes | grey | Hex accent |
| `sort_mode` | TEXT | yes | `manual` | `manual` \| `last_updated` \| `date_created` \| `alphabetical` |
| `sort_direction` | TEXT | yes | `desc` | Direction for non-manual modes |

Unique constraint on `(project_id, status_key)`.

**Default columns, seeded lazily on first board read for a project:**

| position | name | status_key | color | sort_mode | direction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Not Started | `not_started` | neutral grey | manual | asc |
| 1 | Working | `working` | blue | manual | asc |
| 2 | Validating | `validating` | amber | last_updated | desc |
| 3 | Remediating | `remediating` | red | last_updated | desc |
| 4 | Complete | `complete` | green | last_updated | desc |

Seeding is a **write triggered by a read**. Cache "this project has been ensured" in a process-level set so it costs one query per project per process lifetime, and invalidate that cache whenever columns are written. Also implement *repair*: if some but not all defaults exist, recreate the missing ones — a partial column write must be self-healing, because a mid-loop failure on a non-transactional backend otherwise leaves a project permanently short a column.

### 8.2.4 `task_sessions` — the task ↔ session link

| Field | Type | Null | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task_id` | TEXT | no | — | Composite PK, FK → tasks CASCADE |
| `session_id` | TEXT | no | — | Composite PK. **Not** an FK — sessions live outside this database. |
| `session_type` | TEXT | no | `session` | `session` \| `planner` |
| `created_at` | TEXT | no | — | Sole ordering key |

The relation is many-to-many by schema; the reverse lookup (`session → task`) returns only the first match, so the application behaves as if a session belongs to at most one task. That is fine — just be consistent about it.

**`session_type` is load-bearing.** Only `session`-typed links drive the state machine. `planner` links are inert: they do not auto-transition anything, and they must be excluded from session counts and every report. This discriminator was added specifically because planning conversations were inflating "sessions on this task" counts and polluting analytics.

Add an index on `session_id` alone. The original lacked one, making reverse lookups full scans — and the reverse lookup runs on **every session-state event**, which is the highest-frequency query in the system.

### 8.2.5 `task_status_history` — the audit log

| Field | Type | Null | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | TEXT PK | no | UUID4 |
| `task_id` | TEXT | no | FK → tasks CASCADE |
| `project_id` | TEXT | no | **Add this.** The original omitted it. |
| `old_status` | TEXT | **yes** | NULL specifically marks the task-creation row |
| `new_status` | TEXT | no | Status after the transition |
| `changed_by` | TEXT | yes | Actor |
| `changed_at` | TEXT | no | Sole ordering key |
| `session_id` | TEXT | yes | Which session caused this transition (provenance) |

This table is the raw material for every report. Two corrections over the original are mandatory:

1. **Carry `project_id` on the row.** Without it every project-scoped report must join `tasks`, and no index helps.
2. **Index `(project_id, changed_at)`, `(project_id, new_status, changed_at)`, and `(task_id, changed_at)`.**

Note the semantics you are accepting: history **cascades on task delete**, so deleting a task silently rewrites past analytics. Either accept that explicitly or soft-delete tasks. Do not leave it undecided.

### 8.2.6 `task_issues`, `task_tags`, `preferences`

**`task_issues`** — `id` PK · `task_id` FK CASCADE · `description` NOT NULL · `session_id` nullable · `created_at` · `resolved_at` nullable.
`resolved_at IS NULL` is the *only* representation of "open". There is no severity, no assignee, no un-resolve. That minimalism is correct for v1; issues exist to feed the Remediating loop, not to be a bug tracker.

**`task_tags`** — `id` PK · `task_id` FK CASCADE · `tag` TEXT · `created_at` · `UNIQUE(task_id, tag)`.
Tags are raw case-sensitive strings. There is no tag entity and no stored colour: the client derives a colour by hashing the tag string into a fixed 8-colour palette, so the same tag is always the same colour without any storage. Decide whether to normalise case; if you do, do it on write, not on read.

**`preferences`** — `key` PK · `value` (always stringified) · `updated_at`. Type coercion is the caller's job. Board-level configuration (backend selection, validation URLs, page size) lives in a separate gitignored JSON config file with a short-TTL in-process cache.

### 8.2.7 The status enum and the custom-column hole

Five closed values: `not_started`, `working`, `validating`, `remediating`, `complete`.

Row hydration constructs the enum from the stored string and raises on anything unknown. Meanwhile `board_columns.status_key` is free text and the column-update endpoint accepts arbitrary values. **A user who creates a custom column and drags a task into it writes a row whose next read crashes the entire board load for that project.**

You must resolve this deliberately. Pick one:

- **(A) Closed enum.** Enforce it with a CHECK constraint, and make the columns editor rename/recolour/reorder the five fixed statuses but refuse to create new ones. Simplest, and matches the state machine.
- **(B) Open statuses.** Drop the enum, make `status` free text validated against the project's `board_columns`, and express the transition graph as data rather than code.

**Recommendation: (A).** The state machine (§8.3) encodes real product semantics — "only a human may mark complete", "remediating reopens the parent". Those semantics do not generalise to arbitrary user-invented columns. Ship a closed enum with cosmetic column customisation, and revisit only if users demand it.

Whatever you choose, hydration must never crash the whole board because of one bad row. Unknown status → coerce to `not_started` and log, or filter the row out. A single bad row taking down a project's board is unacceptable.

### 8.2.8 Ordering strategy: gap numbering with midpoint insertion

**Constant: `POSITION_GAP = 1000`.**

- **Append:** `MAX(position) + 1000` within the ordering scope, or `1000` if empty.
- **Insert at top:** `MIN(position) − 1000`.
- **Insert between two neighbours:** `new = (after_pos + before_pos) // 2`. `after_pos` defaults to `0` when there is no predecessor; `before_pos = None` means append semantics (`after + 1000`).
- **Collision:** if the midpoint equals either neighbour, the gap is exhausted. Renumber the entire scope to `1000, 2000, 3000, …` in position order, then **retry the same reorder**.

Termination relies on the invariant that post-renumber neighbours differ by exactly 1000, so the midpoint is `after + 500`, distinct from both. **Add an explicit recursion depth counter (max 2) and bail with an error.** The original had none, and degenerate inputs — the same task passed as both neighbours, or neighbours in different columns — recurse forever and hang a worker thread.

Also: **`reorder` on a non-existent task must return an error, not silently succeed.**

**Why gap numbering:** O(1) insertion anywhere without touching sibling rows. This matters because drag-and-drop is applied optimistically in the DOM before the server confirms, and a scheme that rewrites N rows per drop produces visible lag and a much larger reconciliation surface.

**The scoping decision is the load-bearing one.** The original scopes `position` to `(project_id, status)` — **per column, not per parent**. Hierarchy and ordering are fully orthogonal. Consequences you inherit if you copy it:

- Root tasks and deeply nested subtasks compete in the same position space when they share a status.
- Reordering two subtasks inside one parent can trigger a renumber of that entire status column **across the whole project**.
- A renumber bumps `updated_at` on every touched row, which corrupts the stale-task report and scrambles any `last_updated`-sorted column.

**Recommendation: scope position to `(project_id, parent_id, status)`.** Root cards are ordered among roots; subtasks are ordered among siblings. Renumbers stay small and local. The only cost is one extra predicate in every ordering query. Take it.

**Status change re-positions.** Changing status assigns the task a fresh position at the end of the destination column unless the caller supplied one explicitly. A cross-column drag is therefore two operations — move, then reorder — and they are not transactional. Accept that; the reconciliation strategy (§8.10.5) is a full board reload, which papers over the window.

**Where sorting happens.** Store `sort_mode` per column, but decide *once* whether it is honoured server-side or client-side and be consistent. The original stores it, round-trips it, and then ignores it in the repository (every query is `ORDER BY position ASC`), applying sort client-side at render — *and* the client carries a hardcoded map that forces `complete`, `validating`, and `remediating` to `last_updated` even when the stored mode says `manual`. That divergence is a bug generator: the drag handler asks "is this column manual?" and gets a different answer than the renderer used. **Recommendation: honour `sort_mode` server-side in the board query, remove the client-side override map, and seed the defaults table with the sort modes you actually want (as in §8.2.3).** Then "is this column manual?" has exactly one answer.

### 8.2.9 Serialization contract

**snake_case everywhere in this layer. Zero camelCase.** Pick it and never mix.

A task as emitted by the API:

```
{ id, project_id, parent_id, title, description, verification_url,
  status, position, depth, created_at, updated_at, owner,
  // computed by the HTTP layer, not persisted:
  children_count,     // RECURSIVE subtree count
  children_complete,  // RECURSIVE count of descendants at status=complete
  session_count,      // RECURSIVE, work sessions only (planner links excluded)
  active_sessions,    // count currently in working/idle
  tags                // string array — MUST be present on the board payload
}
```

Board envelope:

```
{ columns: [ { ...column, total_count, page, has_more } ],
  tasks:   [ ...flat array, all columns interleaved... ],
  tags:    [ "string", ... ],           // all distinct tags in the project
  active_tag_filter: [ ... ],
  _timing: { ensure, board, counts, enrich, total, tasks }   // ms diagnostics
}
```

Two deliberate choices:

- **`tasks` is a flat array**, not a dict keyed by status. The client re-buckets by `status`. A flat array survives a task whose status has no matching column; a keyed dict silently drops it.
- **`tags` must actually be attached to each task in the board payload.** In the original, the board query returned task objects with no `tags` attribute, and the server-side tag filter tested `all(tag in [])` — which is false for every task. **Applying any tag filter emptied the board.** This is the single most user-visible latent bug in the original feature. Write a test for it: create a task, tag it, filter by that tag, assert the task is returned.

### 8.2.10 Project aliasing (optional, cloud backends only)

Because `project_id` derives from an absolute path, two machines pointing at the same shared board land in different silos. Solve it with a `project_id_aliases` map in the local config file (`local_id → canonical_id`), applied transparently on **every** board request **and every report request**. Sessions, git, and file APIs deliberately keep using the raw local id — only board data is aliased.

Discovery: enumerate distinct `project_id`s present in the backend, score each against the local id (100 = exact basename match; 60 = one basename is a substring of the other id; 0 otherwise; **0 when the ids are identical**, because then no alias is needed), sort by score desc, then task count desc, then id asc, and let the user adopt one with a single click.

Rules that came from real incidents:
- **Reports must resolve the alias exactly as CRUD does.** A user who adopted a shared board saw their tasks but got empty charts, because the report queries used the local id.
- **Never accept the local id from the client.** Derive it server-side, or a misconfigured caller can overwrite an unrelated alias.
- **Aliasing is explicit and one-click, never automatic.** Auto-aliasing on backend switch is spooky action for a user who genuinely wants per-machine boards.
- **Saving an alias must not reset the repository singleton** — same backend, same connection, only the queried `project_id` changes. Bust the columns cache and nothing else.

## 8.3 The task state machine

### 8.3.1 States and legal transitions

```
   ┌─────────────┐
   │ not_started │
   └──────┬──────┘
          │ session linked / user drag
          ▼
     ┌─────────┐        all children done       ┌────────────┐
     │ working │ ────────────────────────────►  │ validating │
     └─────────┘                                └─────┬──────┘
          ▲                                           │
          │ work resumes                    ┌─────────┴─────────┐
          │                     human approves│                 │issues found
          │                                   ▼                 ▼
          │                             ┌──────────┐      ┌─────────────┐
          └─────────────────────────────│ complete │─────►│ remediating │
                                        └──────────┘      └──────┬──────┘
                                          reopened               │
                                                                 └──► working
```

| From | To | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `not_started` | `working` | Work session linked or started; user drag |
| `working` | `validating` | All children done + auto-advance preference; user drag |
| `validating` | `complete` | **Human approval only** (validation ceremony) |
| `validating` | `remediating` | Issues found during validation |
| `complete` | `remediating` | Reopened — new issue found |
| `remediating` | `working` | Work resumes |

**Explicitly forbidden**, and each deserves a test: `not_started ↛ complete`, `not_started ↛ validating`, `working ↛ complete`, `working ↛ not_started`, `complete ↛ working`.

### 8.3.2 The `force` escape hatch — read this twice

The transition function takes a `force` flag that skips graph validation entirely.

**Every user-initiated UI path passes `force: true`.** Drag-and-drop, the context-menu "Move to…", the status-badge dropdown, bulk actions, and the validation ceremony all force. Therefore:

- The graph constrains **AI-initiated** transitions and **automatic** transitions. It never constrains the human.
- A user dragging a card from Not Started straight to Complete succeeds, with no modifier key and no confirmation. This is intentional: humans reorganising their own board should not be argued with by a state machine.

This is the resolution of the "two actors" problem from §8.1. Write it down in your own spec in exactly these terms, because a reviewer who sees `force=True` hardcoded at every call site will otherwise "fix" it and break every drag.

### 8.3.3 Side effects of every transition

In order:

1. **No-op guard.** If `new_status == current_status`, return immediately. No history row, no event.
2. Write `status` and bump `updated_at`.
3. **Assign a new position** at the end of the destination column, unless the caller supplied one.
4. Insert a `task_status_history` row: `(task_id, project_id, old_status, new_status, changed_at, session_id?)`.
5. **Propagate upward** (§8.3.4).
6. Emit exactly one realtime event (§8.10.1).

### 8.3.4 Upward propagation

Two rules, each independently toggleable by a preference, applied recursively up the ancestor chain:

| Rule | Preference key | Default | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Child → `working` promotes a `not_started` parent to `working` | `auto_parent_working` | on | A parent visibly "starts" when any subtask does |
| Child → `remediating` reopens a `complete` parent to `remediating` | `auto_parent_reopen` | on | Finding a bug in a subtask un-closes the epic |

Propagation **writes history rows for the parent but bypasses graph validation**, writing the status directly. That is how `complete → remediating` on a parent works even though only the child's transition was validated. Add a depth cap on the ancestor walk (see the cycle guard, §8.6).

### 8.3.5 Session-driven transitions

**On session start or work-session link** — preference `auto_start_on_session`, default **on**:
- `not_started → working`
- `remediating → working`
- anything else: no-op

**On session complete or unlink** — preference `auto_advance_to_validating`, default **off**:
- Fires only from `working`.
- Requires **zero** remaining linked work sessions **and** all children in `validating` or `complete`.
- Target is `validating`.

**The system never auto-advances to `complete`.** This is a deliberate, permanent invariant: completion requires a human. An agent that can mark its own work complete produces a board that lies.

### 8.3.6 The session-state bridge

**The browser is the bridge, not the server.** On every `session_state` socket event with state in `{working, idle, stopped}`, the client fires a best-effort POST to a bridge endpoint with `{session_id, state}`. The server resolves the linked task and calls the session-start hook (for `working`) or the session-complete hook (for `idle`/`stopped`). If the session is not linked to any task, respond **200 with `linked: false`** — not an error, because the overwhelming majority of sessions are not board-linked.

Consequence: the daemon knows nothing about the board. The coupling lives entirely in an open browser tab. **If no tab is open, no board transitions happen from session activity.**

That is a real limitation. Two honest options:
- **Keep it.** Simple, and the board is a human supervision surface — if nobody is watching, nothing needs to move. Retroactive state is recoverable because the session's own state is authoritative.
- **Move the bridge server-side.** Have the daemon-facing layer publish state changes to an in-process hook that calls the state machine directly. Costs one coupling; buys correctness when the tab is closed.

**Recommendation: move it server-side.** The client bridge was expedient, not right. If you keep the client bridge, document it as a known gap.

### 8.3.7 AI-initiated transitions

An AI session moves its own cards by emitting a marker in its output stream:

```
<!-- kanban:status task_id=<UUID> status=<STATUS> -->
```

The client scans every assistant text chunk with a regex, **deduplicates on `taskId:status` for 30 seconds** (streamed text can repeat, and the marker may be echoed in a summary), and POSTs to an AI-status endpoint. The server:

- **403** with `{blocked: true}` if the `ai_can_modify_status` preference is off.
- **403** with `{blocked: true}` for `status=complete` if `ai_can_mark_complete` is off.
- Otherwise calls the transition **with `force=False`** — the AI is the only actor bound by the graph.

The marker format, the valid status values, per-status guidance, and the list of task IDs it may touch are injected into the session's system prompt by the context builder (§8.4.3), scoped to sibling tasks only, with an explicit instruction not to touch anything else.

### 8.3.8 What happens to the underlying session at each transition

**Nothing.** No transition starts, stops, sleeps, or kills a session. The only task→session actions are user-initiated: Execute, Clear/unlink, and the destructive mode switch. See rule 3 in §8.13.

---

## 8.4 Launching a session from a card

### 8.4.1 The three launch paths

| Path | Entry points | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Execute** (one-click) | Context menu, leaf panel buttons, subtask row hover action, batch bar | Create session → inject context as system prompt → **auto-submit a canned prompt** → navigate into the live chat |
| **Spawn Session** | Context menu, expanded card, "Spawn session…" ghost row | Create session → inject context as system prompt → show an **empty input** for the user to type |
| **Link existing** | "Link existing session…" ghost row | Attach an already-running session to the task |

### 8.4.2 The Execute algorithm

```
1. Fetch task detail and task context in parallel.
2. GUARD: if status == 'complete' → toast "Task is already complete", abort.
3. GUARD: if children_count > 0 → toast
     "Cannot execute a parent task — execute its subtasks instead", abort.
4. Check for an existing active session on this task.
     If found → confirm "This task already has an active session. Launch another?"
5. Generate a client-side UUID for the session.
   Register it in BOTH the sessions array AND the O(1) id Set. (§8.11)
6. Build the prompt text (quick or validate mode).
7. If an agent catalog is available, ensure the catalog file exists and append
   a one-line pointer to the system prompt.
8. Emit start_session with
     {session_id, prompt, cwd, name, model?, thinking_level?, system_prompt?}
9. Link the session to the task → triggers auto-transition to Working.
10. Set the display title, auto-name the session, push to recents, navigate.
```

Step 4 requires a `GET /api/kanban/tasks/<id>/sessions` endpoint. **The original never routed it** — only POST — so the framework returned 405, `response.ok` was false, and the duplicate-session confirmation *silently never fired*, in three separate call sites including both batch pre-checks. Route the GET.

### 8.4.3 The two prompt texts

**Quick mode:**

> Implement this task. You already have the full context of what needs to be done — go ahead and do it.

**Validate mode:** the same opener, plus an instruction to spin up an independent "stickler QA" sub-agent after implementation whose job is to (1) review all changes against the original spec, (2) return a report with a recommended APPROVE or DENY, (3) categorise issues as Critical/High/Medium/Low, and (4) give a realistic, honest recommendation rather than a rubber stamp. If it recommends DENY, iterate on its feedback and re-review until it approves.

Note the honest limitation: this is a **prompt-level** QA loop, not a system feature. The board has no representation of the QA agent's verdict. If you want the verdict on the card, that is new design work — the natural home is a status marker (§8.3.7) plus an issue row.

### 8.4.4 Context assembly

Target budget: **~600 tokens**, ~900 with AI-action instructions. Assemble a fixed template with these slots in this order:

| Section | Content | Cap |
|---|---|---|
| **Current Task** | Bold title + description | description truncated to 200 chars + ellipsis |
| **Verification** | "Check your work at: {verification_url}" | falls back to `(none set)` |
| **Position in Project** | Breadcrumb `Root → Epic → Feature → This Task` | — |
| **Parent Context** | `{parent title}: {parent description}` | description truncated to 200 |
| **Sibling Tasks (same level)** | `- [status] Title` per sibling, current excluded | **max 10** |
| **Active Sessions on Sibling Tasks** | `- [working] on "Sibling Title" (23m)` | **max 8** |
| **Open Issues** | `- {description}` for each unresolved issue on this task | — |
| **Coordination footer** | Fixed prose: siblings and their sessions are shown for awareness; coordinate if your changes touch shared code | — |
| **Task Status Actions** *(conditional)* | Marker format, valid statuses, per-status guidance, and `` `uuid` — Title [status] `` for every sibling with the current one flagged | siblings capped at 10; only when `ai_can_modify_status` is on |

Active-session status is queried live against the daemon. Only `working` / `idle` / `question` are shown; durations are humanised to `Nm` or `Nh`.

**If the daemon is unreachable, render `(unavailable)` rather than omitting the section.** An explicit "you are flying blind" signal is far better than an implicit "nothing is running," which the model will otherwise assume.

The mark-complete guideline flips on the `ai_can_mark_complete` preference: either *"When you are confident a task is fully complete, emit `status=complete`"* or *"You may NOT mark tasks complete — leave them at `validating` for human review."*

### 8.4.5 Batch context

A batch endpoint takes up to **20** task IDs (>20 → 400) and returns `{contexts: {task_id: string}}`. Each task's normal context is built, then a **shared suffix** is appended to all of them:

> ## Batch Execution — Sibling Sessions
> The following tasks are being executed simultaneously: [titles]
> Coordinate carefully to avoid file conflicts. Re-read any file before editing if another batch session may have modified it.

**Launch sequentially, not in parallel** — a burst of 20 simultaneous session creations overwhelms the daemon. Pass `navigate: false` so the user stays on the board watching cards light up. Count per-task failures and report in aggregate: `"Launched 17/20 (3 failed)"`.

---

## 8.5 The AI planner

There are two possible planner architectures. **Build exactly one: the HTTP single-turn planner.** This is the most important lesson in the whole feature.

### 8.5.1 Why HTTP and not an agentic session

The original design launched a full agentic session, with tools enabled, in the project directory, and asked it to produce a plan. It "frequently wandered (tool calls, prose) or returned no clean JSON," which surfaced to users as **"Couldn't parse a task structure."** An agent with tools will use them; an agent asked to *only* produce structured output should not have them.

The replacement is a **single bounded server-side call**: context is injected server-side, exactly one turn is allowed, no tools. Two strategies in order:
1. Call the model provider's API directly (requires a key).
2. On failure or absence of a key, shell out to the local CLI in one-shot mode with a text output format, a one-turn cap, a mid-tier model, no console window, and a **120-second timeout**.

### 8.5.2 System prompt strategy

A base instruction plus up to four conditionally appended context blocks.

**Base.** Break the request into a hierarchical task tree. The refusal-suppression language must be emphatic and repeated:

> NEVER ask the user questions. NEVER ask for clarification. NEVER request more information. If the request is ambiguous, use your best judgment and produce a task tree immediately. Your ONLY job is to output a proposed task tree.

Guidelines: concrete actionable units; each completable in 1–3 sessions; 2–4 nesting levels maximum; descriptions only when the title is not self-explanatory; the `response` field is a brief explanation and **never** a question.

**Block 2 — existing task tree.** A compact indented rendering of the current board (`- [status] Title (N subtasks)`), depth-capped at 4 and character-capped at 2000 with a `... (truncated)` marker, prefixed *"Consider these existing tasks. Avoid duplicating work that already exists."*

**Block 3 — detected routes.** A list of real URL paths scraped from the project source (§8.5.5), prefixed *"ONLY use routes from the list above for `verification_url`. NEVER invent or guess URLs."*

**Block 4 — validation base URL.** When enabled: *"Construct `verification_url` as base URL + a route from the DETECTED ROUTES list above."*

### 8.5.3 Output contract and the robust extractor

Requested shape:

```json
{ "response": "brief explanation, not a question",
  "tasks": [ { "title": "...", "description": "...", "verification_url": null,
               "subtasks": [ { "...recursive..." } ] } ] }
```

An `id` field on a task means *"update this existing task"* rather than *"create new."*

**Parsing must be aggressive, in this priority order.** Models interleave prose containing stray braces; trusting the first `{` fails constantly.

1. Every fenced block body (```json … ``` first, then bare ``` … ```).
2. The whole raw text (the bare-JSON case).
3. **Every** balanced `{…}` substring, scanned string-aware (track quote state and backslash escapes).
4. **Every** balanced `[…]` substring, string-aware.

Objects are scanned before arrays so `{tasks:[…]}` wins over a stray list. Each candidate is parsed and coerced; accept `{tasks:[…]}`, a bare `[{title…}]` array, or any object with a non-empty `tasks`. **The first candidate that yields a usable task list wins.** The rule to write on the wall: *rather than trust the FIRST brace, scan EVERY balanced candidate.*

### 8.5.4 Panel behaviour

- **Entry:** the "Add to Board" modal has a "Plan with AI" textarea alongside the quick-add title field. Submitting opens a right-hand slide-out panel.
- **Failure UI is not a toast.** A parse failure renders an inline error panel — *"Couldn't parse a task structure. Try rephrasing below."* — plus the first 2000 chars of raw text in a `<pre>` for debugging, and stashes the full raw text under a local-storage debug key. Network/API errors render a distinct panel. The user stays in the panel and refines. A toast here is a dead end.
- **Refinement:** the panel keeps a `[{role, content}]` history and posts follow-up turns with the prior history, so "make the subtasks smaller" works.
- **Persistence across reload:** panel state (`open` / `minimized`) is written to both a URL query param and local storage, and a valid proposal is stashed so it survives a refresh. The create modal then shows a **"Resume previous plan (N tasks)"** button. Advertise minimising in the UI: *"minimize to keep working — it'll notify you when complete."*
- **Accept:** POST the whole proposal. The server flattens the tree recursively, splits items into *updates* (an `id` that resolves to an existing task) and *creates*, applies updates, then **batch-inserts** the creates in one multi-row statement along with one creation history row each. Return the new root IDs so the client can apply a temporary highlight animation, cleared after 4 s.
- **Scoped planning (subtree replacement):** invoked from a task's drill-down, the panel carries a parent ID and augments the user message with `[SCOPED EDIT] Return EXACTLY ONE top-level task in "tasks" — the parent being edited (titled "X") — including its updated subtasks. Its old subtree will be replaced.` On accept the server **deletes every existing child of the parent first**, updates the parent's title/description in place, then creates the returned subtasks. Confirm before running: *"This will replace the N existing subtasks with AI-generated ones."*

Two lifecycle traps, both from real bugs:
- **Detach planner listeners BEFORE closing the panel**, so a late `idle` event does not fire the result handler with empty text and flash a spurious parse error.
- **Skip the idle handler when a proposal already exists** — a deferred idle re-emit ~3 s later will otherwise overwrite the result with empty text.

### 8.5.5 URL detection (feeding `verification_url`)

A framework-agnostic source scan. Walk the project tree, skipping vendored directories (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `coverage`, `.tox`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, and the app's own dot-directory) and reading only known source extensions (`.py .js .ts .jsx .tsx .rb .go .java .php .rs .ex .exs`).

Seven regex families: decorator routes (Python web frameworks), function-call registration (Node frameworks), URL-config patterns (Django/Rails/Laravel), JSX route components (`<Route path>`, `<Link to>`), string-literal fetch/axios paths, Go/Java handler registration, and Rust attribute macros.

Normalisation: ensure a leading slash; `${id}` → `:param`; `<task_id>` → `:task_id`; `{id}` → `:id`.
Noise rejection: drop empty or bare `/`, anything over 120 chars, anything containing regex metacharacters (`^ $ * + ? \ ( ) [ ] |`), and anything containing `..`.
Output shape: `{path: "LABEL (relative/file.py)"}`.

### 8.5.6 Validation-URL onboarding

The first time a user plans with AI, if validation URLs are neither enabled nor dismissed, show a modal asking where the dev server runs. Three outcomes: **Enable** (saves the base URL), **Not now** (skipped, asks again next time), **Don't ask again** (persists a dismissal flag). Click-away is treated as "Not now."

---

## 8.6 Hierarchy: parents, subtasks, and grouping

### 8.6.1 The tree

- Self-referential `parent_id`. No depth limit in the data layer. If you expose a depth-limit config key, **enforce it** — the original defaults it to 5 and enforces it nowhere.
- `depth` is computed at read time from the flat list.
- Deleting a task **cascades to the entire subtree**. Declare the FK cascade *and* walk-and-delete in code; belt and braces, because not every backend honours cascades.
- Ancestors are fetched with a recursive query. **Add a cycle guard.** Nothing in the schema prevents a task from becoming its own ancestor, and the original recurses without a depth cap in four separate places (ancestor query, depth walk, propagation, and the report's depth CTE). Enforce it on write: reject a `parent_id` update whose target is a descendant of the task, and cap every recursive walk at a hard depth (e.g. 64).

### 8.6.2 The four-mode drill-down

Clicking a card replaces the entire board with a full-width task detail view. The right panel's mode is **inferred from data, not stored**:

| Mode | Condition | Right panel content |
|---|---|---|
| `subtasks` | task has children | Ordered, drag-reorderable subtask list + progress bar + ghost "add subtask" row + "Plan with AI" button |
| `leaf` | no children AND has a parent | **Two rows: Session and Planner**, plus Execute / Execute + Validate |
| `sessions` | no children, no parent, has work sessions | Session list + "Spawn session…" and "Link existing session…" ghost rows |
| `empty` | no children, no parent, no sessions | **Chooser:** three cards — "Break into subtasks" · "Spawn sessions" · "Plan with AI" |

The `leaf` mode is the design's most opinionated move and follows directly from §8.1: **a leaf task's children are not sub-tasks, they are modes of working on it.** Clicking either row drills into a full-screen live chat with breadcrumbs back to the task.

The `empty` chooser is the key onboarding moment: a fresh root task asks the user to commit to a decomposition strategy rather than presenting an empty panel.

### 8.6.3 Mode switching is destructive and must be confirmed

The subtasks and sessions panels each carry a switch icon:

- **→ sessions:** *"All subtasks (and their children) will be **permanently deleted**."* Deletes every child sequentially.
- **→ subtasks:** *"All linked sessions will be **unlinked**. The sessions themselves are not deleted."* Unlinks every session sequentially.

Both use a themed danger modal that spells out the rationale (*"You're choosing to work on this task directly with sessions instead of breaking it into subtasks"*) and states **"This cannot be undone."**

### 8.6.4 Board scoping

The board endpoint takes an optional `parent_id` scope. Without it the board shows **only root tasks** (`parent_id IS NULL`) with recursive rollup counts on each card. With it the board shows that parent's direct children. In practice the client only uses the default root mode; the drill-down uses the task-detail endpoint. Keep the parameter — it is nearly free and makes "focus on this epic" a one-line feature later.

---

## 8.7 Complete HTTP API for the board

Conventions: all routes JSON. **Success is always HTTP 200, never 201.** Mutations with no entity return `{ok: true}`; entity endpoints return the bare entity or a bare array. Errors are `{error: "<message>"}` with 400 / 403 / 404 / 500.

**Do not copy the original's error handling.** It wraps every handler in a bare catch-all and returns the raw exception string with 500 — an information-disclosure surface. Log the exception server-side; return a generic message plus a correlation id.

**Do not copy the original's partial-update builder.** It interpolates caller-supplied keys directly into the SET clause (values parameterised, column names not), and the PATCH endpoint forwards the entire request body. **Whitelist the mutable column names.**

### 8.7.1 Board and aggregate reads

| Method | Path | Params | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/kanban/board` | `page=1`, `page_size=50`, `tags=a,b`, `parent_id?` | `{columns[], tasks[], tags[], active_tag_filter[], _timing}` |
| GET | `/api/kanban/task-tree-summary` | — | `{summary}` — indented text, depth ≤ 4, ≤ 2000 chars |
| GET | `/api/kanban/detected-urls` | `cwd` | `{urls: {path: desc}, formatted}` |

### 8.7.2 Task CRUD

| Method | Path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks` | `{title*, parent_id?, description?, verification_url?, status?, insert_position?}` | `insert_position: "top"` → `min − 1000`, else append. Empty title → **400** |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>` | — | Task + `children[]` (enriched) + `sessions[]` (with live status) + `issues[]` + `tags[]`. Unknown → **404** |
| PATCH | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>` | whitelisted field subset | `status` routed through the state machine with `force=true`. Empty body → 400. Unknown → 404 |
| DELETE | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>` | — | `{ok: true}`. Cascades to subtree. Emits board refresh |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/move` | `{status*, force?, old_status?}` | Missing status → 400. Illegal transition without force → **400**. Emits **only** `kanban_task_moved` |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/reorder` | `{after_id?, before_id?}` | `{ok:true}`. **Emits no event.** Unknown task → 404 |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/bulk` | `{action: "complete_all"\|"reset_all"}` | `{ok, updated}`. Direct children only, forced, skips failures |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/ancestors` | — | `{ancestors[], task}` — ordered immediate-parent → root |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/history` | `page`, `page_size=20` | `{history[], total, page, has_more}` — newest first |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/claim` | — | Owner ← preference, else VCS user identity, else OS username |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/unclaim` | — | Owner ← null |

### 8.7.3 Session linking

| Method | Path | Body | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GET** | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/sessions` | — | **Route this.** Linked sessions with live state |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/sessions` | `{session_id*, session_type?}` | Type coerced to `session` if not in `{session, planner}`. Only `session` auto-transitions |
| DELETE | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/sessions/<sid>` | — | Triggers the auto-advance check |
| DELETE | `/api/kanban/sessions/<sid>/unlink-all` | — | Cleanup when a session is deleted |
| GET | `/api/kanban/unlinked-sessions` | — | `[{id, display_title, state}]`; skips names starting with `_` |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/from-session` | `{session_id*, title?}` | `{task, linked: true}` — creates a root task at `working` and links it |

### 8.7.4 Issues, tags, columns, context

| Method | Path | Body / Query | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/issues` | `{description*}` | Issue with `resolved_at: null` |
| PATCH | `/api/kanban/issues/<issue_id>` | `{resolution?}` | `{ok:true}` — sets `resolved_at` |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/tags` | — | `{tags: ["a","b"]}` |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/tags` | `{tag*}` | TaskTag |
| DELETE | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/tags/<tag>` | — | `{ok:true}` |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tags` | — | `{tags: [...]}` distinct for the project |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tags/<tag>/tasks` | — | bare array |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tags/suggest` | `q` | `{tags: [{tag, usage_count}]}` — usage desc, substring-filtered, top 10 |
| GET | `/api/kanban/columns` | — | bare array (ensures defaults) |
| PUT | `/api/kanban/columns` | bare array of columns | Updated array. Non-list → 400. Invalidates the ensure-cache. Emits board refresh |
| GET | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/context` | — | `{context}` (~600 tokens). Unknown → 404 |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/batch-context` | `{task_ids[]}` | `{contexts: {id: string}}`. Empty/non-list → 400; **> 20 → 400** |

**Column PUT is a delete-all-then-insert-each.** On a transactional backend that is one transaction. On a non-transactional REST backend it is N+1 calls, and a mid-loop failure leaves the project with fewer columns than it started with — which lazy default-seeding will *not* repair, because seeding only fires when the column list is entirely empty. **Fix both ends:** wrap in a transaction where you can, and make the ensure/repair step recreate individually missing defaults (§8.2.3).

### 8.7.5 Planner, config, bridges

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/kanban/planner/chat` | `{message*, history[]}` | `{response, proposal: {tasks}\|null}` |
| POST | `/api/kanban/planner/accept` | `{proposal, insert_position?, parent_id?}` | `{created_count, created_ids}` |
| GET | `/api/kanban/config` | — | backend, depth limit, auto-advance, page size, validation settings |
| PUT | `/api/kanban/config` | partial | `{ok:true}`. Boolean prefs whitelisted |
| POST | `/api/kanban/session-state-change` | `{session_id*, state*}` | `{ok, linked, task_id?}`. Unlinked → 200 with `linked: false` |
| POST | `/api/kanban/tasks/<id>/ai-status` | `{new_status*, session_id?}` | `{ok, task}`. Blocked by prefs → **403 + `blocked: true`**. Illegal transition → 400 (no force) |

### 8.7.6 Reports

Seventeen GET endpoints under `/api/kanban/report/`. Enumerated in §8.9.
