## 10.8 Mobile and remote access

### 10.8.1 Responsive strategy: same DOM, restyled

**Stated principle: do not change the web design. Same DOM, same components, same interactions.** No separate
mobile template, no separate route. **One breakpoint** at 768 px, mirrored in JavaScript through a media-query
match so CSS and behavior can never disagree about what "mobile" means.

- **The sidebar becomes the drawer.** Fixed position, full viewport width, translated fully off-screen when
  collapsed, with a ~280 ms eased transition. Toggle it through the application's **existing** collapse/expand
  functions so persisted state stays in sync. Do not invent a hamburger button: reposition the existing expand
  button and swap its icon, capturing the originals once so desktop restore is exact.
- **A CSS trap worth knowing.** The desktop collapsed rule typically sets `width: 0 !important` and hides
  children. On mobile that *silently defeats* the transform transition — width snaps to zero and children
  vanish, so there is nothing left to animate and the drawer just disappears rather than sliding. The mobile
  override must restore full width and the children's display. One override fixes every collapse path at once.
- **Drawer policy.** Auto-open on the sessions view *only while browsing* (no session active). Wrap the
  open-session and new-agent functions — single choke points — to close the drawer, so picking a session
  reveals the chat instead of the drawer springing back over it. Wrap the view-mode setter to re-evaluate on
  every view change. Attach a mutation observer to the sidebar's class attribute so the opener button and
  backdrop stay in sync no matter which code path changed the state.
- **Homepage fix.** A desktop homepage that vertically centers its cards pushes the top cards *above* the
  scroll area on a phone, where they are permanently unreachable. Force top alignment and automatic height.
- **Header.** 52 px tall; hide the logo and wordmark on drilled-in views and add left padding for the burger.
  Replace git button labels with one-word generated content (Update / Publish / Sync).

**iOS-specific CSS that is not optional:** disable the touch callout and user selection so long-press does not
trigger the selection magnifier; set `touch-action: manipulation` to opt out of double-tap zoom and the 300 ms
click delay; apply safe-area inset padding to the input bar and every bottom-anchored surface; disable vertical
overscroll on the document root to kill whole-page rubber-banding; and set `touch-action: pan-y` with contained
overscroll on the conversation log so a vertical drag scrolls the log rather than bouncing the page.

Note also that `!important` is required to beat an inline `display: none` set by a boot script.

### 10.8.2 Gestures

**Edge and anywhere swipe for the drawer**, following the finger 1:1. Skip the first 8 px from the screen edge
(browser back-swipe territory). Require 8 px of movement before locking to horizontal or vertical. Require
30 % of the drawer width to commit. **Bail out if the drag starts inside anything with horizontal overflow** —
a code block — so its own scroll is not hijacked. Direction must match intent: a leftward drag while the mode
is "open" is released back to content. On release, restore transitions, flip the application's own collapsed
state through its normal toggle so it persists, and drop the inline transform so it animates from where the
finger left it. The touch-move listener must be registered non-passive so it can prevent default.

**Long-press → context menu.** Use **pointer events** so mouse, touch, and pen share one implementation — a
touch-only version means desktop press-and-hold does nothing, which users read as a regression. Register
mouse events as a fallback for environments where pointer events are squelched, with a guard against
double-arming. 500 ms dwell, 20 px slop, a short haptic vibration wrapped in a try/catch. Match **any element
carrying a session-id data attribute**, so sidebar rows and card grids are both covered without enumerating
layouts. Deliberately **do not gate this on a mobile check** — tablets and touchscreen laptops also lack
right-click.

- **Do not let touch-cancel clear the long-press timer.** iOS Safari fires it spuriously when it decides to
  start its own gesture, and clearing means the menu never appears.
- Cards that are HTML5-draggable need a capture-phase drag-start handler that cancels the drag while a
  long-press is armed.
- **An 800 ms capture-phase click blocker** suppresses the synthetic click fired on release — but it must
  explicitly allow clicks inside the context menu, the bottom sheet, and the sheet backdrop, or the first tap
  on a menu row (or the backdrop dismiss) is swallowed. Make it one-shot.

**Bottom action sheet.** The desktop toolbar is a wide button row that cannot fit a phone. A `•••` button
harvests those buttons into an iOS-style sheet with a Cancel row. Run the chosen action on an ~80 ms delay
after the sheet closes so it does not fight the dismiss animation.

### 10.8.3 What is deliberately unavailable on mobile

Hidden on mobile: the desktop toolbar overflow control, the panel resize handle, the desktop toolbar button
group, the toolbar close button, the keyboard send hint, the per-session model selector, the queue suffix and
hint, the logo and wordmark when drilled into a session, and git button text labels (replaced by one-word
generated labels).

Shown **only** on mobile: a footer tip that makes long-press discoverable, since the desktop affordance is
right-click.

Also include a reduced-motion media block that disables the animations.

### 10.8.4 Remote access: a mesh VPN, not the LAN

**The invariant, and state it three times in your own source: the server stays bound to the loopback
interface. Nothing rebinds it to the LAN or the internet.**

The bridge is a mesh-VPN reverse proxy command — the **tailnet-only "serve" mode, explicitly not the public
"funnel" mode.** Traffic path: phone on the tailnet → HTTPS to the node's mesh DNS name → the local VPN
daemon → loopback port. Encrypted end to end by the mesh's own transport.

**Why HTTPS, given the tunnel is already encrypted:** iOS grants a *secure context* — the thing that unlocks
the microphone and speech recognition — only to `https://` origins and `localhost`. Plain HTTP over the tunnel
is not a secure context, so **voice silently dies there.** HTTPS is what makes voice work on the phone.
Privacy is not the reason; the tunnel already provides that.

**Cost:** the mesh's HTTPS-certificates feature must be enabled once in its admin console. Detect it from the
certificate-domains field of the VPN's status output. When it is off, **do not attempt to start the serve** —
an HTTPS serve blocks without a certificate — route the user to guided setup instead.

**No new runtime dependency.** Pure standard library plus the VPN's CLI. Discover the binary by path lookup
first, then per-OS candidate paths including snap and the macOS app bundle. A missing binary returns a
structured "not found" result so callers never special-case a null.

**API:** `/api/mobile/status`, `POST /api/mobile/enable`, `POST /api/mobile/disable`,
`POST /api/mobile/name {name}`. **Derive the port from the incoming request's Host header** — the port the
browser used is exactly the port the proxy should serve.

**Status response — one structured dictionary drives the entire UI:** `{enabled, installed, logged_in,
backend_state, serving, url, port, needs, https_help, device_name, account, phone_connected, phone_name,
host_os, install_url}`. The `needs` field is one of `null`, `install_vpn`, `vpn_login`, `enable_https`,
`starting`. **Every failure path degrades to a `needs` value that names the user's next action — never a
stack trace.**

**Persistence and rearm.** The on-flag lives in the application's configuration file. The enable operation
**persists the flag regardless of whether the serve command succeeds right now**, so a transient tunnel hiccup
does not silently disable the feature. A rearm routine runs at every startup and must be **threaded and
retrying**, for two documented reasons: (1) the reboot race — the VPN daemon is frequently not yet running
when the web server starts, so a one-shot attempt no-ops and the feature stays dark until a manual restart,
breaking the "set it once, it always works" promise; and (2) a synchronous attempt shells out for up to ~75
seconds and would stall startup. Retry roughly 24 times at 5-second intervals (~2 minutes), then hand off to
the setup modal's own retry.

**Certificate pre-warm.** The mesh issues the TLS certificate **lazily, on the first HTTPS connection**, which
can take seconds. Spawn a daemon thread that makes a throwaway HTTPS request to the node's own tunnel name
(3 attempts, 3 seconds apart) so the user's *first phone hit* is instant instead of a timeout. Make it
disableable by a module flag so unit tests stay network-free.

**"Already serving" detection is subtler than it looks.** Check that the existing proxy configuration serves
your port **over HTTPS**, not merely that something proxies to your port. A leftover serve from a previous
HTTP-on-port-80 configuration also proxies to the same local port; accepting it makes rearm think it is already
serving, so it never establishes the HTTPS serve — leaving a confident "On" state whose HTTPS QR code fails on
the phone. Implement this by **excluding the known-bad HTTP listener rather than requiring an assumed-good
HTTPS key shape**: your code only ever creates HTTPS serves and disable runs a full reset, so the only
non-HTTPS entry that can exist is the legacy one. Rejecting exactly that avoids a false negative — a perpetual
"starting" state — if the VPN keys a valid HTTPS serve differently than you assumed.

### 10.8.5 The guided setup wizard and pairing

Steps: `install → signin → https → bridge → phone → done`. **The current step is a pure function of live
state: pick the lowest unsatisfied rung.** This makes the wizard auto-advance on its own as the user completes
each step, with no state machine to get stuck in. Poll at a per-step cadence (1500 ms on the bridge step,
2000 ms on sign-in, 2500 ms elsewhere, none on the intro which waits for a click). Stop polling when the modal
closes.

Three design principles, and they are what make this usable by non-technical people:

1. **Every step gives a concrete call-to-action button** — download, open the exact settings page, copy the
   account name, copy the link, open the app store.
2. **Every step self-verifies and advances by itself.** "Check again now" exists only as a fallback that
   should never be needed.
3. **Account, phone, and OS are all read live from this machine.** Nothing about the user's identity is
   hardcoded.

Two signals make it feel intelligent:

- **The account reader** resolves the local node's user id to its login name and tells the user the *exact
  account to sign their phone into*. **This is the single most common first-time failure** — signing the phone
  into a different account and then finding the URL unreachable.
- **The phone detector** scans mesh peers for a mobile OS, preferring one that is online, and maps generic
  hostnames to friendly labels so the confirmation reads **"✓ Your iPhone is connected to your network"**
  rather than a junk hostname. This is unambiguous proof they did it right *before they even open the URL.*

**QR codes** use a vendored QR library with medium error correction, rendered as scalable SVG with a forced
white background. Render three: the app-store link for the VPN client, the tunnel URL, and the desktop
installer URL. **Nothing sensitive is encoded** — the tunnel URL is useless without mesh membership. Fall back
to plain text if the library did not load.

**Add to Home Screen.** A device name defaults to the machine's short hostname and is user-editable with a
40-character cap. It feeds the iOS web-app title meta tag *and* a **dynamically served** web manifest whose
short name is the first 12 characters, for Android. Without a per-machine value, every computer's home-screen
icon says the same thing and a user with two machines cannot tell them apart. The manifest is standalone
display, portrait orientation, generated per request rather than served as a static file. The device-name
resolver must read cached configuration plus the hostname with **no VPN call**, so it is safe to invoke on
every page render.

**The reviver — closing the last gap.** The proxy mapping lives in the VPN daemon and survives the application
being down. So a killed application presents the VPN's bare **502 Bad Gateway** with no way back short of
walking to the computer. A tiny supervisor process polls "is the main port alive?" every couple of seconds and
**binds that port only while the application is down**, serving a one-tap "Start" page. Invariants:

- **Zero hot-path footprint** — never a proxy, never in front of live socket or voice traffic.
- Both its serve socket and its control socket (a separate configurable port) bind loopback only.
- Singleton, enforced by binding the control port.
- On a real start, the launcher posts to its yield endpoint so it **releases the port without dying**, then
  goes dormant.
- It re-checks the remote-access flag every loop and self-retires when the feature is turned off.
- **Pure standard library**, because it must run when the application's own packages are broken — which is
  often *why* the server is down.
- It survives the application's own stop shortcut by design, since it is not one of the processes that
  shortcut kills and holds no port while dormant. That is the whole point.

For unattended reboots, provide one-time per-OS setup scripts, including an "unlock and start" page for
machines with encrypted home directories.

### 10.8.6 Security posture — state this plainly

- **There is no authentication anywhere.** No token, no PIN, no session cookie. Document it in your README in
  those words: *"The API has no authentication — it is a localhost-only development tool. All endpoints are
  available without credentials."*
- Security is **entirely topological**: bind to loopback, and let the mesh VPN's device-identity layer be the
  authentication and authorization boundary.
- Consequences a rebuilding team must weigh honestly: any process on the machine can drive the full API —
  spawn agent sessions, read and write anything under the home directory, open files with the system handler,
  and push to a remote. The preview proxy is an unauthenticated fetch-any-URL proxy. The file-drop endpoint
  writes arbitrary uploads anywhere under home.
- The home-containment check is the **only** filesystem boundary, and it must be applied consistently across
  every file endpoint (403 on violation), resolving before comparing so symlink escapes are closed.
- **The strongest security engineering in this product protects the publishing boundary, not the network
  boundary.** That inversion is intentional and worth naming: for a local development tool, the realistic
  threat is accidental publication, not remote intrusion. If your deployment assumptions differ — if the tool
  will ever run on a shared machine or a server — this entire posture must be redesigned, not patched.

## 10.9 Bridges and analysis endpoints

### 10.9.1 The third-party chat bridge

**What it is:** a standalone page that relays a prompt typed in the application to the user's **already
logged-in** third-party chat web session via browser automation, and returns the reply. **Why it exists:** to
reuse an existing consumer subscription with no API key and no per-token billing.

**Endpoints:** a page route; `GET /api/<bridge>/status` → `{ok, logged_in, busy, error}`;
`POST /api/<bridge>/login` → `{ok, message}`; `POST /api/<bridge>/ask {prompt, files?}` → `{ok, result,
error}` — HTTP 200 on success, **502** otherwise.

**The bot-detection finding, stated empirically:**

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| Bundled automation-framework browser | Blocked (stuck on verification) |
| Real Chrome, headless | Blocked — headless is the tell |
| Real Chrome, **headed**, with the automation-controlled blink feature disabled | **Passes cleanly** |

So the bridge uses the real installed browser channel, runs **always headed** (a visible window — the headless
parameter is accepted for API compatibility and ignored), and disables the automation-controlled flag. A
persistent profile directory, gitignored, keeps the login between calls.

**Detect login from the auth cookie, not the DOM.** The logged-out landing page also shows a chat composer, so
"composer visible" is not a login signal. Cookie reads require no navigation, so they never trip the bot check
and they are fast.

**Concurrency:** a persistent profile directory can be opened by exactly one browser at a time. Serialize every
launch behind a single lock. The login window holds the lock for its entire lifetime; ask and status acquire
with a timeout and report `busy` rather than crashing.

**Login-window robustness, learned the hard way:** third-party OAuth opens a **popup** — a second page in the
context — so the worker must keep running while *any* page is open, not just the first one, or it tears the
popup down mid-authentication. During the redirect chain the page navigates constantly and calls like reading
the title throw transient errors, so the loop should test `is_closed()` (which requires no navigation and never
throws on a live page) and exit only when all pages are closed. Cap the wait at 600 seconds.

**The ask sequence:** cookie check → navigate → poll for the bot check to clear (30 s) → wait for the composer
→ click and **insert text directly** rather than simulating keystrokes (avoids accidental newline-sends and is
far faster) → attach files → count existing assistant messages → click send, falling back to pressing Enter →
wait for the **stop button to appear and then disappear** as the generation-tracking signal → poll 15 s for the
message count to increase → read the last message's text.

**File upload:** set files on the hidden file input rather than simulating drag-and-drop; cap at the vendor's
limit (20); validate every path exists. **Attach files *after* typing the prompt**, so "send button becomes
enabled" is a **pure upload-done signal** — the vendor keeps it disabled while attachments process.

**Fragility management — the transferable part.** Carry an explicit fragility warning in the module: it
automates a DOM that changes without notice. **Centralize every selector in named constants** so updating is
a one-file edit, and **on any failure write a full-page screenshot plus an HTML snapshot** to a debug directory
keyed by tag and timestamp, so current selectors can be rediscovered in minutes rather than hours. Every
timeout is a named constant.

Treat this as an experiment with a maintenance budget, not a platform feature.

### 10.9.2 Analysis endpoints

Four endpoints, all taking a project parameter, all resolving a transcript file by session id, all returning
404 on a missing file.

| Endpoint | Analyzes | User gets |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/summary/<session_id>` | The **user's own messages** across the whole session | A rendered HTML summary card |
| `GET /api/extract-code/<session_id>` | Fenced code blocks | `{blocks[], count, languages[]}` |
| `GET /api/export-project/<session_id>` | Non-duplicate code blocks | A downloadable ZIP plus generated README |
| `GET /api/compare/<id1>/<id2>` | Two sessions' code blocks | Metadata, per-key diff rows, aggregate stats |

**The summary algorithm is deliberately extractive, not generative** — no model call, so it is instant, free,
and deterministic:

1. Filter to user messages, clean them, drop trivial ones.
2. Divide the remainder into **5 equal sections by position** and pick the highest-scoring message from each.
   This yields coverage across the session's arc rather than five bullets about the same topic.
3. For each pick, generate a 2–3 word **label** from the first three content words longer than three
   characters and not in a ~70-word stop list (these are more likely to be nouns and topics), title-cased; and
   a **description** that is *the user's own words*, cleaned, capitalized, truncated at 130 characters on a
   word boundary with an ellipsis.
4. Dedupe by the first 12 characters of the lowercased label.
5. Overview = the first one or two substantive user messages (over 20 characters), joined with an em dash,
   capped around 200 characters. "Recent focus" = the last three meaningful user requests.
6. Header = a smart title plus a statistics line (message count, size, last-active time).

**The design lesson is the important part:** a summary built entirely from *user* messages describes what the
human was trying to do — which is exactly what a session list needs — and it costs nothing. Using the user's
own words is naturally the right level of abstraction. Reserve the language model for cases this genuinely
cannot cover.

---

## 10.10 Consequential decisions

| Decision | What we chose | Why | What breaks if you choose differently |
|---|---|---|---|
| File attachment mechanism | Save to disk, then tell the agent the path in an ordinary chat message | Zero protocol, composes with every agent tool, no token budgeting | An attachment pipeline means MIME handling, upload lifecycle, transcript-renderer special cases, and per-model differences — weeks of work for no user-visible gain |
| Filesystem sandbox | Resolve, then require containment under the user's home directory | One rule, applied identically at six endpoints, easy to audit | Per-endpoint ad-hoc checks drift; a symlink escapes the first time someone forgets to resolve first |
| Output detection | Three strategies (tool name, shell command text, scanned result/prose) + extension allowlist | Strategy 3 is the only one that catches files written by a script the agent ran | Tool-name-only detection misses generated reports entirely; no allowlist buries the one artifact under a card per edited source file |
| Git status | Cached, background-refreshed, 45 s minimum interval, eagerly stamped | A status poll on every request spawns subprocesses per second and flashes console windows | Inline computation makes the header slow and the machine noisy; a lazily stamped timestamp lets a poll burst stampede |
| Post-push state | Trust the outcome; do not re-read the dirty flag | A concurrent agent session dirties the tree between commit and check | The Publish button sticks forever and users produce chains of empty commits |
| Branch guard | Enforced on both client and server, Cancel primary, fires before every other option | The client's polled status is up to 45 s stale | A non-technical user publishes to a feature branch and cannot understand why nothing changed |
| Pull conflict policy | Automatic, biased to remote | The target user cannot resolve a conflict, so a conflict must never be surfaced | A half-merged application with conflict markers, and a user with no path forward |
| Secret scanning | Deterministic regex over the **whole repo**, not the diff, no model call | What matters is what will exist after the push; deterministic means fast, free, and testable | Diff-only scanning ships every secret committed before the scanner existed; a model-based scanner is slow, costly, nondeterministic, and cannot gate a button |
| Scan block UX | Primary action spawns an agent session preloaded with findings and a machine-checkable exit criterion | A gate that only blocks trains users to bypass it | Users click "publish anyway" or disable the scanner |
| Preview transport | Server-side headless screenshot + marker protocol + conditional prompt preamble | The phone cannot reach the machine's loopback and the agent cannot "show" a screen | Without the preamble the agent describes screens in prose the user cannot verify; without the marker protocol there is no channel at all |
| Remote-request detection | Explicit flag, proxy-injected header, or Host suffix — never source IP | The proxy makes every request look like loopback | IP-based detection either never fires or fires on every local turn |
| Search index | Disposable derived state; transcripts are the source of truth; recover at both index and query time | Full-text index pages corrupt in ways a no-change ensure pass cannot see | Every search returns 500 until some transcript's mtime happens to change |
| Search project scoping | Validate the name against separators and `..`; never fall back when passed explicitly | The indexer will happily walk into and persist a foreign directory | Cross-project data leaks into the index; users get silently wrong results |
| Voice engine selection | Local model preferred, browser-native fallback, graceful none | Browser-native is Chromium-only and mangles project vocabulary | Chromium-only voice excludes Firefox and Safari users entirely and silently |
| End-of-speech detection | Gate every model-derived signal on real, recent microphone silence | Model signals are computed on audio submitted seconds ago | Auto-send fires mid-sentence, repeatedly, and users stop using voice |
| Message-loss policy | Only an explicit cancel may discard; empty finals fall back to live text; send is idempotent | Losing a dictated message is unrecoverable; sending early is merely awkward | Users lose long dictations and never trust the feature again |
| Browser launch | Chrome-first on all three platforms, isolated profile, cold-start-only new-window | Browser-native voice is Chromium-only and its absence is silent | A Firefox default silently removes the microphone button with no error anywhere |
| Mobile strategy | Same DOM, one 768 px breakpoint, restyled | A separate mobile template doubles every future feature | Feature drift between the two surfaces starts immediately and never stops |
| Remote access | Mesh-VPN tailnet-only serve over HTTPS; never rebind the server | HTTPS is required for iOS to grant a secure context and unlock the microphone | Plain HTTP over the tunnel silently kills voice; rebinding to the LAN exposes an unauthenticated API |
| Authentication | None; security is topological | A local development tool on a single-user machine | Any deployment onto a shared or networked machine is immediately, totally compromised |
| Session summary | Extractive from user messages only, no model call | Instant, free, deterministic; the user's own words are the right abstraction level | A model-generated summary costs money per session-list render and is nondeterministic |

---

## 10.11 Non-negotiable rules

1. **Resolve a path to its canonical form before checking home-directory containment.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* a symlink inside the home directory points outside it and the sandbox is open
   to the entire filesystem.

2. **The pre-push secret scanner ships in the same release as the one-click publish button — never after.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* there exists a window in which non-technical users publish unreviewed,
   agent-authored diffs from a repository containing credentials and home-directory paths. Public-repository
   pushes are indexed by scrapers within minutes, and the damage is permanent even after a force-push.

3. **Scan twice: before staging and again after `git add -A`. On the second failure, unstage everything.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* files created between the two moments are committed unscanned, and a block that
   leaves files staged means the *next* commit anyone makes — including one an agent makes from the shell —
   silently includes them.

4. **Redact every match in a security report (leading few characters plus a redaction marker).**
   *Failure mode if violated:* the report becomes a second copy of the secret, in a log, a screenshot, and a
   support ticket.

5. **Never hardcode owner personal information into a scanner that ships in a public repository. Load such
   patterns from a gitignored configuration file.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* you publish to the internet exactly the personal information the patterns exist
   to protect.

6. **Never let a secret-detection value class match newlines.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* the pattern slurps subsequent lines of code and reports a multi-line blob as a
   hardcoded password; users learn to ignore the scanner.

7. **Enforce the branch guard on the server, not only the client, and make Cancel the primary button.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* the client's status can be 45 seconds stale, so a user publishes to a feature
   branch believing they published to main.

8. **Trust the post-push state instead of re-reading the dirty flag; follow it with a cooldown.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* a concurrent agent session dirties the tree between commit and check, the
   Publish button never clears, and users generate chains of empty commits.

9. **On all three platforms, find and launch Chrome/Chromium before falling back to the system opener.**
   *Failure mode if violated:* on a machine whose default browser is Firefox, the microphone button silently
   disappears with zero errors in the console, the logs, or the UI. This regression already shipped once.

10. **Never open the browser until the server answers a health poll.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the user's first experience of the product is a connection-refused page.

11. **Gate every model-derived end-of-speech signal on real, recent microphone silence, and make the pending
    finish retractable.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* auto-send fires mid-sentence whenever the model is slow, truncating the user's
    message.

12. **The only thing that may discard a dictated message is an explicit cancel. Empty or timed-out finals fall
    back to the last live transcript, and the send is idempotent.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* users lose long dictations with no recovery, which is the single fastest way
    to kill adoption of a voice feature.

13. **Re-query the input element by id at send time.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the input bar re-renders mid-capture, the text is written to a detached node,
    and the user sees the send animation play while the message vanishes.

14. **Prime the audio context synchronously inside the tap gesture on iOS, before requesting the media
    stream.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* only the very first recording fails to auto-stop, which reads as random
    flakiness and is nearly impossible to reproduce on demand.

15. **Never detect "remote/mobile" from the source IP address when a proxy is in the path.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the tunnel makes every request look like loopback, so the feature either never
    activates or activates on every local turn.

16. **The server stays bound to the loopback interface. Remote access is a tailnet-only VPN serve, never a
    public tunnel and never a rebind.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* an API with no authentication that can spawn shell-capable agent sessions and
    read the entire home directory becomes reachable from the LAN or the internet.

17. **Serve remote access over HTTPS.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* iOS does not grant a secure context over plain HTTP, and voice silently stops
    working on the phone with no error message.

18. **Every remote-access failure path reduces to a structured `needs` value naming the user's next action.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a non-technical user sees a stack trace and files a support ticket for a
    two-click fix.

19. **Filter deleted and tombstoned sessions at query time, not index time.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* deletion does not change a transcript's mtime, so search keeps returning
    sessions the user just deleted.

20. **HTML-escape search snippets before substituting highlight markers; split titles on the raw string and
    escape each part.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a cross-site-scripting hole fed directly by arbitrary agent output.

21. **A route module must be importable with zero side effects. Duplicate a small helper rather than import a
    module whose import starts servers.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* importing a blueprint boots a second copy of the application.

22. **Optional dependencies degrade; they never 500.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* a missing image library turns every gallery tile into a broken endpoint
    instead of a heavier-but-working image.

23. **In embed mode, shim storage as own properties via a property definition — never a prototype patch, never
    plain assignment — and match the server's path encoder exactly.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the embed repoints the user's own window to a different project, or the panel
    renders silently empty with no error.

24. **Use a drag counter, not a boolean, for drop-overlay visibility, and queue multiple dropped files.**
    *Failure mode if violated:* the overlay flickers whenever the cursor crosses a child element, and dropping
    ten files opens ten racing modals.

## 10.12 Build priority within this part

### v1 — must have

| # | Item | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **File API with the home-scoped sandbox**, including a proper platform branch on the open-file endpoint | Every other file feature sits on it |
| 2 | **Output shelf** | Highest value-per-line in the entire part. Without it, agent-produced artifacts are invisible and the user hunts the filesystem. The three-strategy detection is what makes it actually work |
| 3 | **Drag-and-drop + folder picker**, including the drop-notifies-the-session message | Cheap, and the tell-the-agent-in-prose trick removes the need for an attachment pipeline entirely |
| 4 | **Git status polling + one-click Publish** — branch guard, auto-commit message, plain-English messages, post-push trust. **Build it project-scoped, not self-scoped** | The non-technical Update button is a headline capability |
| 5 | **Pre-push secret/PII scanner** with whole-repo scope, blocked files, redacted findings, and streaming progress | Non-negotiable alongside item 4. Ship them together, never sequentially |
| 6 | **Chrome-first browser launch on all three platforms** | A prerequisite for any voice feature; getting it wrong is invisible until a user reports a missing microphone button |
| 7 | **Browser-native voice** with the silence timer, the onstart-guarded restart loop, cancel-discards, and the transcript-processor seam | The seam costs nothing now and is expensive to retrofit |
| 8 | **Find-in-transcript (Ctrl/Cmd+F)** | Roughly 70 lines, immediately useful, no backend |
| 9 | **Mobile responsive layer** — drawer, choke-point wrappers, safe areas, touch-action, and the collapsed-width override | Same DOM, one breakpoint. Very high usability-to-effort ratio |
| 10 | **A read-only working-tree diff viewer** (our addition; see §10.1) | The publish button is not honest without a way to see what is being published |

### v1.5 — strongly recommended, small

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 11 | **Long-press context menu** via pointer events, with the touch-cancel and click-suppression subtleties |
| 12 | **Bottom action sheet** harvesting the desktop toolbar |
| 13 | **Extractive summary endpoint** and **code extraction + ZIP export** |
| 14 | **"Fix with AI" remediation session** launched from a blocked scan |

### v2 — high value, higher cost

| # | Item | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | **Full-text transcript search** with incremental indexing, TTL debounce, query-time tombstone filtering, and both corruption-recovery layers | Only pays off once users have history worth searching. Build the disposability doctrine in from the start — retrofitting recovery is painful |
| 16 | **The real file browser** — project tree, viewer with syntax highlighting, `@`-mention into prompts | The most conspicuous gap in the reference product. Scope it deliberately rather than inheriting the absence |
| 17 | **Remote access** — VPN bridge, guided wizard, QR pairing, dynamic manifest, device naming | Depends on the mobile layer. The wizard's self-verifying design is what makes it usable; a bare "here's a URL" version generates support load indefinitely |
| 18 | **Preview channel** — headless render, thumbnails, proxy, marker protocol, conditional prompt preamble | Only meaningful once remote access exists, but the marker-protocol pattern is reusable well beyond mobile |
| 19 | **Local speech engine** with streaming local agreement, mic-confirmed end-of-speech, windowed partials, and the caption UI | The single largest engineering investment in this part and the source of the most regressions. Ship browser-native voice in v1; do this only once the product's identity depends on cross-browser, vocabulary-aware dictation |
| 20 | **Dormant reviver supervisor** | Only matters if remote access is a promise you intend to keep |

### v3 — optional / situational

| # | Item | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | **Session comparison** | Narrow use case; transcript-block diffing is approximate |
| 22 | **Embed mode** | Only if a host application actually exists. The storage-shim technique is worth reading regardless |
| 23 | **Third-party chat bridge** | Genuinely useful, but structurally fragile: it automates a vendor DOM that changes without notice, requires a *visible* browser window, and serializes on a single profile lock. Treat it as an experiment with a maintenance budget |

**Two sequencing warnings, repeated because they are the two that cost us the most.**

First: **the scanner and the publish button must ship together.** Shipping the button first creates a window
in which non-technical users publish unreviewed diffs, and that window is exactly when the damage becomes
permanent.

Second: **build the Chrome-first launcher before any voice feature, not after.** The failure mode is a
silently missing microphone button with no error anywhere, which is nearly undiagnosable from a user report.

## 10.13 Implementation prompts

```
PROMPT 10.1 — File API and sandbox

Implement the file-handling HTTP API for the application, backed by a single containment rule.

Build a helper that takes a user-supplied path, resolves it to an absolute canonical form with symlinks
resolved, and returns true only if it lies under the current user's home directory. Apply it at EVERY
endpoint below; return HTTP 403 on violation.

Implement a dedup-naming helper: given a target directory and a filename, return a free filename by
inserting " (n)" before the extension and incrementing n until no file exists.

Endpoints:
- GET  /api/file-info?path=            -> {name, size, exists}; size humanized server-side (B/KB/MB)
- POST /api/open-file {path}           -> {ok}; branch on platform (Windows shell-open, macOS `open`,
                                          Linux `xdg-open`)
- POST /api/download-to-downloads {path} -> {ok, filename, dest}; copy into the Downloads folder with dedup
- POST /api/copy-file-to {source, target_dir} -> {ok, filename, path}; sandbox-check both ends
- POST /api/file-drop (multipart file, form target_dir) -> {ok, path, filename}; sanitize the filename,
                                          then dedup
- GET  /api/browse-dir?path=           -> {path, dirs[]}; directories only, one level, dot-directories
                                          filtered, permission errors swallowed to an empty list
- GET  /api/default-save-dir           -> {path}; Downloads, falling back to home
- GET  /api/project-path               -> {path}

Acceptance criteria:
- A request for a path outside home returns 403.
- A symlink inside home pointing outside home returns 403 (write a test for this specifically).
- Uploading the same filename three times yields "name.ext", "name (1).ext", "name (2).ext".
- Every endpoint returns valid JSON on failure — no HTML error pages, no stack traces.
- /api/open-file succeeds on all three platforms (mock the platform call in tests).
```

```
PROMPT 10.2 — Drag-and-drop, folder picker, and the output shelf

Implement three client-side surfaces on top of the file API from PROMPT 10.1.

(A) Global drag-and-drop:
- Bind dragenter/dragover/dragleave/drop on the document; react only when the drag payload includes files.
- Track drag depth with an integer COUNTER (increment on enter, decrement on leave); hide the overlay only
  at zero. A boolean here is a bug.
- On drop, push all files into a queue and process ONE AT A TIME.
- For each file, open the folder picker defaulted to /api/default-save-dir, POST to /api/file-drop, then —
  if a live session is running — emit a normal chat message reading:
  "[file dropped] <name> is now at <absolute path>"

(B) Folder picker modal:
- Breadcrumb built by splitting on BOTH path separators; special-case a Windows drive-letter first segment
  so "C:" navigates as "C:/".
- Navigate one level at a time via /api/browse-dir.
- Expose a headless mode: open the picker with no pending file and a completion callback, turning it into a
  generic "choose a folder" dialog.

(C) Output shelf:
- Watch the conversation stream. Detect agent-produced files with THREE strategies:
  1. tool-use entries for write/edit/multi-edit/notebook-edit -> the description field is the path; strip a
     trailing "(write N chars)" suffix and a leading "file_path:" prefix
  2. shell tool-use entries -> regex-scan the command text
  3. ANY tool result or assistant prose -> regex-scan for absolute paths ending in a known extension
- Gate on an extension allowlist: spreadsheets, documents, presentations, pdf, images, svg, csv, json, zip,
  html, txt. Source-code extensions are excluded on purpose.
- Render a card per detected file: family-colored icon, basename, async size from /api/file-info, an Open
  button, and a Save-to button (folder picker -> /api/copy-file-to, falling back to the downloads copy).
- Dedupe with a Set of paths across re-renders; clear both the Set and the shelf DOM on session switch.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dragging across nested child elements never flickers the overlay.
- Dropping 5 files produces 5 sequential prompts, never overlapping modals.
- A file written by a Python script that the agent ran through the shell still produces a card (this
  exercises strategy 3 — test it explicitly).
- Editing a .py file produces NO card.
- Re-rendering the same message ten times during streaming produces exactly one card.
```

```
PROMPT 10.3 — Git status cache and read-only status endpoints

Implement cached git status with a throttled background refresher. Target the repository configured as the
active project.

State: a module-level cache dict {has_git, ready, ahead, behind, uncommitted, branch, default_branch,
on_default}, a fetch lock, a post-sync cooldown timestamp, and a last-refresh timestamp.

Background refresh routine:
- If there is no .git directory: set has_git=false, ready=true, return.
- Run `fetch --quiet` (15s timeout, failures swallowed).
- Ahead/behind in ONE call: `rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{upstream}`.
- Dirty: `status --porcelain` as a boolean.
- Branch: `symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD`. Default branch: `symbolic-ref --short -q refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`,
  taking the segment after the first slash.
- FAIL OPEN: on_default = (not default_branch) or (branch == default_branch).

refresh_if_idle(), called from the status endpoint, is TRIPLE-GATED:
  (a) return if now < cooldown_until
  (b) return if now - last_refresh < 45 seconds
  (c) return if the fetch lock is held
Stamp last_refresh EAGERLY, before spawning the thread. Re-check the cooldown INSIDE the thread under the
lock.

Every subprocess: explicit timeout (fetch 15s, pull 30s, all else 5s) and the Windows flag that suppresses
console-window creation.

Endpoints:
- GET /api/git-status         -> the cache dict; calls refresh_if_idle first
- GET /api/project-git-status -> {is_git, branch, dirty_count, recent_commits[{hash,message}], project_path}
                                 using `status --porcelain` line count and `log --oneline -5`

Acceptance criteria:
- 100 concurrent status requests spawn at most ONE refresh thread.
- A repository with no origin/HEAD reports default_branch="" and on_default=true (never a spurious warning).
- No console window appears on Windows during a background refresh.
- The status endpoint responds in under 10 ms when the cache is warm.
```

```
PROMPT 10.4 — Deterministic pre-push secret and PII scanner

Implement a regex-only, no-model, whole-repository scanner. This gates the publish button and must ship
with it.

Scope: union of `git ls-files` and `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`. Scan the whole repository,
not the diff.

Per file, evaluate in this order:
1. Skip list — the scanner's own source file, plus a configurable list.
2. Per-file finding suppressions: (path pattern, finding-type-or-null); null skips the file entirely.
3. Forbidden filenames -> BLOCKED: env files, credentials/service-account/token JSON, SSH private keys of
   every algorithm, *_rsa, *.pem/.p12/.pfx/.p8, keystores, .htpasswd, package-manager credential files,
   Terraform state, and the application's own config file.
4. Private-document detection -> BLOCKED: by extension (office, pdf, csv/tsv, email exports, accounting)
   AND by filename pattern regardless of extension (invoice, receipt, contract, NDA, tax, payroll,
   financial statement, medical, identity document, confidential, customer list, salary, board minutes,
   legal memo, proposal, purchase order, term sheet, resume, offer letter). Plus a binary-extension
   blocklist and "larger than 500 KB -> too large to scan, review manually".
5. Content scan — roughly 40 patterns across cloud keys, platform tokens, AI provider keys, SaaS tokens,
   payment keys, database connection strings, generic api_key/secret/token/bearer/password assignments,
   private-key headers, JWTs, base64 blobs, hardcoded home paths, internal IPs, confidentiality markers,
   and personal identifiers.

MANDATORY pattern rules:
- Every value-matching character class EXCLUDES newlines: use [^"'\r\n]{8,}, never [^"']{8,}.
- The environment-variable secret pattern carries a negative lookahead excluding quoted pure-lowercase
  snake_case values (config-key constants are not credentials).
- Owner-PII patterns, if any, load from a GITIGNORED config file — never from tracked source.

Output: {ok, findings[<=50], blocked_files[<=20], summary, files_scanned}. Each finding is
{file, line, type, desc, match} where `match` is REDACTED to the first 6 characters plus a redaction
marker (4 characters for short matches).

Also provide:
- A quick file-count function for progress UI (lists files, scans nothing).
- A generator variant yielding {"type":"progress", current, total, file} per file and a terminal
  {"type":"done", ...}, exposed as GET /api/git-scan-stream (server-sent events). Plus GET /api/git-scan
  for the non-streaming result.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test fixture containing `body: 'password=' + encode(pw),` produces ZERO findings.
- A test fixture containing `_CONFIG_KEY = "mobile_command_enabled"` produces ZERO findings.
- A file containing a real-looking cloud key produces exactly one finding whose `match` does NOT contain
  the full key.
- A repository with 200 secret-bearing files returns at most 50 findings and 20 blocked files.
- The scanner returns ok=false when a .env file is present, even if that file is untracked-but-not-ignored.
```

```
PROMPT 10.5 — The one-click Update / Publish flow

Implement the sync endpoint and the client flow. This is safety-critical: the user does not read diffs.

SERVER — POST /api/git-sync {action, confirm_branch}, action in {pull, push, both}:

1. No .git -> {ok:false, messages:["<App> has no git repo."]}
2. BRANCH GUARD, before ANY git operation: if not confirm_branch, read the current and default branches. If
   a default exists and differs, return {ok:false, needs_branch_confirm:true, branch, default_branch,
   messages:[plain-English explanation]} WITHOUT touching git.
3. Pull path: `stash --include-untracked` -> `pull --rebase -X theirs` -> on failure `rebase --abort` then
   `pull -X theirs` -> if the second also fails, return "Could not pull: <stderr>" AND DO NOT PROCEED TO
   PUSH -> `stash pop` if anything was stashed. Detect "Already up to date" by substring and report it
   distinctly.
4. Push path:
   a. Run the scanner (PROMPT 10.4). If not ok, return with the scan payload and a block message.
   b. If the tree is dirty: `add -A`, then RUN THE SCANNER AGAIN. If the second scan fails, run
      `reset HEAD` to unstage everything, then return the block.
   c. Commit with an auto-generated message "Update <App> YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM". On failure, if stderr contains
      the missing-identity phrases, append paste-ready `git config --global user.name/user.email` commands.
   d. `push`. On failure, surface stderr as "Could not push: ...". NO auto-retry. NO force-push, ever.
5. Cache update under the lock: if the push succeeded, TRUST the outcome — set ahead=0, behind=0,
   uncommitted=false WITHOUT re-running `status --porcelain`. Otherwise re-read actual state. Then set a
   10-second cooldown suppressing background refresh.

CLIENT — three mutually exclusive header buttons driven by the cached status:
  behind>0 -> "Update App"; ahead>0||uncommitted -> "Publish App Update"; both -> a single "Sync App".

Publish sequence:
1. Nothing to do -> modal "Nothing to publish — your app is already up to date on remote." (OK only)
2. Branch guard modal FIRST if on_default is false. Copy is non-technical. CANCEL IS THE PRIMARY BUTTON;
   the secondary is 'Sync to "X" anyway'.
3. Test gate: Fast Tests + Publish (primary) / Full Tests + Publish / Skip & Publish / Cancel. Stream test
   output. On failure show "Publish Blocked — Tests Failed" with failing lines in a scrollable block and
   Publish Anyway / Cancel (primary). On runner error: "Could not run tests. Publish anyway?"
4. Streaming security scan via the SSE endpoint: progress bar with current/total AND the name of the file
   being scanned. On block: "Fix with AI" (primary) / Close. If the STREAM errors, fall through — the
   server scans again anyway.
5. Server sync with an indeterminate pulse animation.
6. Result modal listing the server's plain-English messages.

Also: a minimize button on the progress modal, shown only while in flight, that collapses to a floating pill
with a spinner and the current step; on completion while minimized the pill turns done/error, reveals a
close button, and flashes briefly. Clicking while working restores the modal; clicking when finished
dismisses.

Acceptance criteria:
- With the working copy on a non-default branch, a sync request WITHOUT confirm_branch performs zero git
  operations (assert via a subprocess spy) and returns needs_branch_confirm.
- Injecting a secret-bearing file between the first scan and `add -A` causes the second scan to block AND
  leaves the index empty (`git diff --cached` is empty).
- After a successful push, an immediate status call reports ahead=0/uncommitted=false even if a concurrent
  process dirtied the tree.
- A commit failure with a missing git identity returns a message containing both `git config --global`
  commands.
- No code path anywhere invokes `push --force`.
```

```
PROMPT 10.6 — Voice input: browser-native engine, processor seam, and Chrome-first launch

Implement dictation into the prompt box, plus the launcher rule it forces.

(A) LAUNCHER — before anything else. On all three platforms, find and launch Chrome or Chromium BEFORE
falling back to the system opener:
- Windows: registry app-paths entry (machine hive, then user hive), then Program Files, Program Files (x86),
  local app data. Launch via the OS shell-execute API (focus-safe from a minimized parent), falling back to
  the system start-file call.
- Linux: path lookup over google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, chromium-browser, and beta/unstable
  channels; then standard bin directories, snap, the vendor install directory, and Flatpak system and
  per-user exports. Launch by direct spawn, falling back to xdg-open.
- macOS: system and user Applications directories for Chrome and Chromium. Direct spawn, falling back to
  `open`.
Pass an app-mode URL flag plus a dedicated user-data directory inside the app's data folder (gitignored);
if that directory cannot be created, fall back to a new-window launch. Detect whether the browser is already
running: if yes, open a BARE URL (new tab); if no, use the new-window flag. Bias the detection to "running"
on any failure. Gate the whole launch on a health poll of the server URL (60 attempts, 1s apart) — if the
server never answers, do NOT open a browser.

(B) VOICE UI — a microphone button with an injected sibling Send button on its right (visible only when
there is text and no recording) and a Cancel (X) button on its left (visible only while recording). One
shared function updates icon, title, and class on every state change.

(C) BROWSER-NATIVE ENGINE — continuous recognition with interim results:
- Preserve existing textarea content; voice APPENDS.
- Paint interim results raw into the textarea.
- 7-second silence timer, reset on every result, then an intentional stop.
- Auto-restart on unexpected end, max 5 times, counter reset on any result. GUARD: auto-restart engages only
  after the engine's start event fired (proving permission was granted and audio is flowing).
- Errors: network/aborted/audio-capture fall through to the end handler; no-speech is silent; anything else
  toasts.
- On end: if the user pressed X, clear the textarea. Otherwise run the processor chain, write the result,
  and fire submit.

(D) PROCESSOR SEAM — a registered, ordered chain of fn(text, context) -> string | Promise<string> with
context {textarea, onSubmit, source}. Ship it EMPTY. A non-string return is ignored; a THROW is caught and
the prior text preserved. Include a synchronous fast path when zero processors are registered.

(E) SEND SAFETY — re-query the input element by id at send time (the bar can re-render mid-capture). If
submit throws, leave the text in the input and toast "Your dictation is ready — press Enter to send."

Acceptance criteria:
- On a machine whose default browser is Firefox, the app still opens in Chrome.
- A first-run permission prompt that ends recognition before it started does NOT trigger the restart loop.
- Pressing X during recognition clears the textarea; ending any other way never clears it.
- A processor that throws leaves the dictated text intact.
- Writing to a re-rendered input bar still lands in the visible textarea (test by swapping the node
  mid-capture).
```

PROMPT 10.7 — Mobile responsive layer, gestures, and tunnel-based remote access

Implement phone support without changing the desktop design and without exposing the server.

(A) RESPONSIVE — same DOM, one breakpoint at 768px, mirrored in JS via a media-query match.
- Sidebar becomes a full-width fixed drawer, translated off-screen when collapsed, ~280ms eased.
- CRITICAL: override the desktop collapsed rule inside the mobile block — the desktop `width: 0 !important`
  plus hidden children silently defeats the transform transition.
- Toggle through the app's EXISTING collapse functions so persisted state stays in sync. Reposition the
  existing expand button and swap its icon; capture the originals so desktop restore is exact.
- Auto-open the drawer on the sessions view only while browsing. WRAP the open-session, new-agent, and
  view-mode functions (single choke points) to close/re-evaluate. Attach a mutation observer on the sidebar
  class attribute to keep the opener and backdrop in sync.
- Force top alignment on the homepage (a centered desktop layout pushes cards above the scroll area).
- iOS CSS: disable touch callout and user select; touch-action: manipulation; safe-area insets on every
  bottom-anchored surface; disable vertical overscroll on the document root; pan-y plus contained overscroll
  on the conversation log.

(B) GESTURES
- Swipe drawer following the finger 1:1: skip the first 8px from the edge, 8px slop before axis lock, 30% of
  width to commit, bail if the drag starts inside a horizontally scrollable element, direction must match
  intent. Touch-move listener must be non-passive.
- Long-press context menu via POINTER events (mouse fallback registered separately with a double-arm guard),
  500ms dwell, 20px slop, short haptic. Match any element with a session-id data attribute. Do NOT gate on a
  mobile check. Do NOT clear the timer on touch-cancel. Cancel HTML5 dragstart while armed. Add an 800ms
  one-shot capture-phase click blocker that WHITELISTS the menu, sheet, and sheet backdrop.
- Bottom action sheet harvesting the desktop toolbar buttons, with a Cancel row; run the chosen action
  ~80ms after the sheet closes.

(C) REMOTE ACCESS — the server stays bound to loopback. Bridge via the mesh VPN's tailnet-only serve mode
over HTTPS (never the public tunnel mode, never a rebind).
- Endpoints: GET /api/mobile/status, POST /api/mobile/enable, POST /api/mobile/disable,
  POST /api/mobile/name {name}. Derive the port from the incoming Host header.
- Status returns ONE structured dict: {enabled, installed, logged_in, backend_state, serving, url, port,
  needs, https_help, device_name, account, phone_connected, phone_name, host_os, install_url}, where `needs`
  is null | install_vpn | vpn_login | enable_https | starting. EVERY failure degrades to a `needs` value —
  never a stack trace.
- Persist the on-flag even if the serve command fails right now. Run a THREADED, RETRYING rearm at startup
  (24 attempts, 5s apart) because the VPN daemon is often not running yet after a reboot and a synchronous
  attempt would stall startup by ~75s.
- Pre-warm the lazily issued TLS certificate with a throwaway HTTPS request to the node's own tunnel name
  (3 attempts, 3s apart), disableable by a module flag for tests.
- "Already serving" detection must require HTTPS on your port — exclude the legacy plain-HTTP listener

Acceptance criteria:
- The server never binds anything other than loopback (assert in a test).
- With the VPN binary absent, /api/mobile/status returns needs="install_vpn" and HTTP 200 — never a 500.
- Enabling while the VPN daemon is down still persists the flag, and a simulated startup rearm establishes
  the serve once the daemon comes up.
- Collapsing the sidebar on a 375px viewport animates rather than snapping to invisible.
- Long-press works with a mouse on a desktop viewport.
- Tapping the first row of the long-press menu is NOT swallowed.

PROMPT 10.8 — Preview channel, search, and the analysis endpoints

Implement the remaining surrounding tools.

(A) PREVIEW
- POST /api/preview/render {url, name, width, height, wait_ms} -> {ok, id, src, file, bytes, name,
  type:"image"}. Accept only http/https/data URLs. Clamp width 200-2000 (default 1024), height 200-4000
  (default 1400), wait 0-20000 (default 3000). Discover the browser binary IN THIS MODULE — do NOT import
  the launcher module, whose import starts servers. Headless flags MUST include a virtual time budget equal
  to the wait, run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw, and an opaque white default background color, or
  single-page apps capture as blank frames. 45s timeout -> 504; non-zero exit / missing / zero-byte output
  -> 500. RETURN THE ABSOLUTE FILE PATH so the agent can look at its own screenshot.
- GET /api/preview/asset/<id> — id must match ^[0-9a-f]{32}$, resolved only inside the previews directory.
- GET /api/preview/thumb/<id> — width 480, quality 78, high-quality resampling; crop tall captures to a max
  1.4 aspect ratio KEEPING THE TOP; regenerate when missing or stale; long cache lifetime. If the image
  library is absent, SERVE THE FULL-SIZE PNG — never 500.
- GET /api/preview/proxy?u= — best-effort; rewrite src/href/action/poster to absolute proxied URLs on HTML
  responses; skip data:, mailto:, fragments, javascript:; 502 with a plain-text message on failure. Document
  that this is an unauthenticated open proxy, defensible only because the app is loopback-bound.
- MARKER PROTOCOL: the agent emits a line containing a JSON payload wrapped in [[VN-PREVIEW ... ]] or a
  Unicode bracket pair. Client extraction is IDEMPOTENT — the id is a hash of type|src|name — strips markers,
  collapses 3+ newlines to 2, upserts into a per-session store, and renders cards inline. A refresh control
  cache-busts with an incrementing query parameter. Live iframes are sandboxed and any loopback source is
  rewritten through the proxy.
- MOBILE PREAMBLE: when a turn is detected as remote, prepend a delimited preamble instructing the agent to
  emit markers, giving the exact render call, and requiring it to OPEN AND LOOK AT the returned file before
  emitting a marker. Detect remote via an explicit payload flag, the proxy-injected identity header, or a
  Host suffix — NEVER by source IP. Any detection failure means "not remote".

(B) SEARCH
- Full-text index in a database stored OUTSIDE the repository, with the path computed LAZILY on every call.
  Write-ahead logging; a schema version that triggers a rebuild on mismatch.
- Tables: indexed_files(project, session_id, mtime, size); session_files(project, session_id, file_path,
  norm_path); and a full-text `messages` table with content indexed and project/session_id/role/ts/msg_idx
  unindexed.
- Incremental indexing comparing (mtime, size); delete rows for vanished transcripts; a 20-second per-project
  TTL. Index tool-result output too, capped at 4000 characters per block. "Touched" means EDITED — only
  write-class tools register a file.
- Recovery at BOTH index time and query time: on a database error, delete the database and its sidecars and
  rebuild; at query time, rebuild and retry ONCE. Close the connection before re-raising on corruption
  detection (Windows file locking).
- Query: quote every token as a phrase with embedded quotes doubled; AND-join; wildcard-suffix ONLY the last
  token. `file:<fragment>` uses only the FIRST such token, matched with LIKE and an explicit escape
  character. Rank by BM25. OVER-FETCH max(200, limit*10) before grouping by session. Up to 3 snippets per
  session. Filter deleted/tombstoned sessions at QUERY time.
- GET /api/search?q=&file=&project=&limit= — q needs 2+ characters unless file is given; limit clamped
  1-100 (default 20). VALIDATE the project name against "/", "\", and ".."; when project is passed
  explicitly, do NOT fall back to the active project.
- Client: 350ms debounce, a sequence guard, an active-project guard, defensive JSON parsing, and XSS
  discipline — ESCAPE SNIPPETS FIRST then substitute highlight markers for <mark>; split titles on the RAW
  string then escape each part.

(C) ANALYSIS
- GET /api/summary/<session_id> — EXTRACTIVE, no model call: filter to user messages, divide into 5 equal
  sections by position, pick the highest-scoring message from each, generate a 2-3 word title-cased label
  from the first three content words over 3 characters not in a stop list, and a description that is the
  user's own words truncated at 130 characters on a word boundary. Dedupe by the first 12 characters of the
  lowercased label.
- GET /api/extract-code/<session_id> — every fenced block with language, content, message index, role,
  inferred filename, shell flag, and duplicate-of index (same-language similarity above 0.85).
- GET /api/export-project/<session_id> — in-memory ZIP of non-duplicate blocks plus a generated README.
- GET /api/compare/<id1>/<id2> — key blocks by inferred filename / language / "unknown", union the keys,
  classify added/removed/same(>0.98)/changed, return both metadata blocks, the diff rows, and aggregate
  stats.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rendering a client-rendered single-page app produces a non-blank screenshot (assert non-white pixel
  variance).
- With the image library uninstalled, the thumbnail endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a PNG.
- Calling marker extraction ten times on the same streaming text yields exactly one preview entry.
- Deleting a session removes it from search results immediately, with no transcript modification.
- A search query containing `" OR 1=1 --` returns zero results and does not error.
- A snippet containing `<script>` renders as visible text, never as markup.
- The summary endpoint completes in under 200 ms on a 500-message session and makes no network calls.
